modules.title: Bloch's theorem on the lattice
modules.doc:
A translation-invariant evolution of configurations of unit cells acts through its Bloch matrix.

## i. Overview

Consider degrees of freedom attached to the cells of a lattice whose translation group is `Λ`,
an abelian group such as `ℤ ^ d`. The contents of one unit cell, orbitals or spin components, form
a module `M`, and a configuration is a finitely supported assignment of an element of `M` to each
cell: `ψ : Λ →₀ M`. Translation acts by `(T a ψ) m = ψ (m - a)`. A crystal momentum is a character
`χ` of `Λ`, and the Fourier transform of a configuration is `ev χ ψ = ∑ m, χ m • ψ m`.

* The kernel of the Fourier transform is precisely the span that defines the momentum fiber. So the
  fiber at momentum `χ` is a copy of the unit cell `M`: Bloch's reduction to a single cell.
* Every translation-invariant linear map `D` satisfies `ev χ (D ψ) = H(k) (ev χ ψ)` for a matrix
  `H(k)` on the unit cell, its *Bloch matrix*. No finite-range assumption is needed, as a
  configuration has finite support, and the matrix is `H(k) v = ∑ m, χ m • (D (δ₀ v)) m`.
* The Bloch matrix of a product is the product of Bloch matrices, and of the inverse the inverse.
* A hopping Hamiltonian with amplitude `t n` to the cell displaced by `n` has
  `H(k) = ∑ n, exp (i k n) t n`: the Fourier transform of its hoppings.

No analysis, finite dimensionality or positivity is used. The analytic counterpart on `ℓ²` is in
`RegularRep` and `Spectrum`, and the finite periodic crystal in `FiniteBloch`.

## ii. Key results

- `translation` : translating a configuration of unit cells.
- `ev` : the Fourier transform of a configuration at a crystal momentum.
- `ker_ev` : the kernel of the Fourier transform defines the momentum fiber.
- `fiberEquiv` : the fiber at momentum `χ` is the contents of a unit cell.
- `symbol` : the Bloch matrix of a translation-invariant map.
- `ev_apply` : Bloch's theorem, Fourier transform intertwines the map and its Bloch matrix.
- `symbol_comp`, `symbol_id`, `isUnit_symbol` : the Bloch matrix of a product and of an inverse.
- `hopping`, `symbol_hopping` : the Bloch Hamiltonian of a hopping model.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Translations and Fourier evaluation
- B. The momentum fiber is the unit cell
- C. Bloch matrices
- D. Hopping operators

## iv. References

* F. Bloch, Über die Quantenmechanik der Elektronen in Kristallgittern, Z. Phys. 52 (1929). [ref:
  bloch_1929]
* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapters 4 and 8.

sections.text: ## B. The momentum fiber is the unit cell

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.translation
declarations.doc: Translation of finitely supported configurations: `(T a ψ) m = ψ (m - a)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def translation : Multiplicative Λ →* Module.End K (Λ →₀ M)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.translation_single
declarations.statement:
lemma translation_single (a : Multiplicative Λ) (m : Λ) (v : M) :
    translation (K := K) a (Finsupp.single m v)
      = Finsupp.single (m + Multiplicative.toAdd a) v

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.charFun
declarations.doc: A character `χ` of `Λ`, viewed as a function on the multiplicative group of translations.
declarations.statement: def charFun (χ : AddChar Λ K) : Multiplicative Λ → K

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.ev
declarations.doc: Fourier evaluation at the character `χ`: `ev χ ψ = ∑ m, χ m • ψ m`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ev (χ : AddChar Λ K) : (Λ →₀ M) →ₗ[K] M

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.ev_single
declarations.statement:
lemma ev_single (χ : AddChar Λ K) (m : Λ) (v : M) :
    ev χ (Finsupp.single m v) = χ m • v

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.ev_translation
declarations.statement:
lemma ev_translation (χ : AddChar Λ K) (a : Multiplicative Λ) (ψ : Λ →₀ M) :
    ev χ (translation (K := K) a ψ) = charFun χ a • ev χ ψ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.ev_single_zero
declarations.statement: lemma ev_single_zero (χ : AddChar Λ K) (v : M) : ev χ (Finsupp.single 0 v) = v

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.ev_surjective
declarations.statement: lemma ev_surjective (χ : AddChar Λ K) : Function.Surjective (ev (M := M) χ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.sub_single_ev_mem_cobound
declarations.doc:
Every configuration is congruent, modulo the fiber relations, to its Fourier evaluation
placed in the origin cell.
declarations.statement:
lemma sub_single_ev_mem_cobound (χ : AddChar Λ K) (ψ : Λ →₀ M) :
    ψ - Finsupp.single 0 (ev χ ψ)
      ∈ cobound (translation (K := K) (Λ := Λ) (M := M)) (charFun χ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.ker_ev
declarations.doc: The kernel of Fourier evaluation is exactly the span defining the momentum fiber.
declarations.statement:
lemma ker_ev (χ : AddChar Λ K) :
    LinearMap.ker (ev (M := M) χ)
      = cobound (translation (K := K) (Λ := Λ) (M := M)) (charFun χ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.fiberEquiv
declarations.doc:
The momentum fiber of the translation action at `χ` is canonically the unit-cell space
`M`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fiberEquiv (χ : AddChar Λ K) :
    Fiber (translation (K := K) (Λ := Λ) (M := M)) (charFun χ) ≃ₗ[K] M

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.fiberEquiv_mk
declarations.statement:
lemma fiberEquiv_mk (χ : AddChar Λ K) (ψ : Λ →₀ M) :
    fiberEquiv χ (Fiber.mk (translation (K := K)) (charFun χ) ψ) = ev χ ψ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.symbol
declarations.doc:
The Bloch matrix of a linear map `D` at the character `χ`: apply `D` to the unit cell at the
origin and Fourier-evaluate.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def symbol (χ : AddChar Λ K) (D : (Λ →₀ M) →ₗ[K] (Λ →₀ M)) :
    M →ₗ[K] M

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.symbol_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma symbol_apply (χ : AddChar Λ K) (D : (Λ →₀ M) →ₗ[K] (Λ →₀ M)) (v : M) :
    symbol χ D v = ev χ (D (Finsupp.single 0 v))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.ev_apply
declarations.doc:
**Bloch theorem.** Fourier evaluation intertwines a translation-equivariant linear map with
its Bloch matrix.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.symbol_id
declarations.doc: The Bloch matrix of the identity is the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma symbol_id (χ : AddChar Λ K) :
    symbol χ (LinearMap.id : (Λ →₀ M) →ₗ[K] _) = .id

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.symbol_comp
declarations.doc: The Bloch matrix is multiplicative: only the left factor needs to be equivariant.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.symbol_add
declarations.doc: The Bloch matrix is additive.
declarations.statement:
lemma symbol_add (χ : AddChar Λ K) (D₁ D₂ : (Λ →₀ M) →ₗ[K] (Λ →₀ M)) :
    symbol χ (D₁ + D₂) = symbol χ D₁ + symbol χ D₂

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.isUnit_symbol
declarations.doc:
If an equivariant map is invertible by an equivariant map, its Bloch matrix is invertible a
every momentum.
declarations.statement:
lemma isUnit_symbol {D E : (Λ →₀ M) →ₗ[K] (Λ →₀ M)}
    (hD : IsEquivariant (translation (K := K)) (translation (K := K)) D)
    (hE : IsEquivariant (translation (K := K)) (translation (K := K)) E)
    (h₁ : D ∘ₗ E = LinearMap.id) (h₂ : E ∘ₗ D = LinearMap.id) (χ : AddChar Λ K) :
    IsUnit (symbol χ D)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.hop
declarations.doc: One hopping term: apply `Hn` in each cell, then translate by `n`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hop (n : Λ) (Hn : M →ₗ[K] M) : (Λ →₀ M) →ₗ[K] (Λ →₀ M)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.hopping
declarations.doc:
A finite-range hopping operator with hopping matrices `H n : M → M`:
`(hopping H ψ) m = ∑ n, H n (ψ (m - n))`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hopping (H : Λ →₀ (M →ₗ[K] M)) : (Λ →₀ M) →ₗ[K] (Λ →₀ M)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.isEquivariant_hop
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_hop (n : Λ) (Hn : M →ₗ[K] M) :
    IsEquivariant (translation (K := K)) (translation (K := K)) (hop n Hn)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.isEquivariant_hopping
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_hopping (H : Λ →₀ (M →ₗ[K] M)) :
    IsEquivariant (translation (K := K)) (translation (K := K)) (hopping H)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.symbol_hopping
declarations.doc: **Bloch Hamiltonian.** The Bloch matrix of a hopping operator is `∑ n, χ n • H n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma symbol_hopping (χ : AddChar Λ K) (H : Λ →₀ (M →ₗ[K] M)) :
    symbol χ (hopping H) = H.sum fun n Hn => χ n • Hn

modules.title: The spectrum of a finite periodic crystal
modules.doc:
The spectrum of a translation-invariant operator on a finite periodic crystal is the union of the
spectra of its Bloch matrices.

## i. Overview

A finite periodic crystal has a finite abelian translation group `G`, for instance `(ℤ / mℤ) ^ d`,
and `N` orbitals in each cell. A configuration is a function `ψ : G → ℂ ^ N`, and a hopping
operator `(B ψ) x = ∑_r A_r ψ (x - r)` moves amplitude by the lattice vector `r` through the
matrix `A_r`. A plane wave `x ↦ χ(x) v` of crystal momentum `χ`, a character of `G`, is mapped to
`χ(x) b(χ) v`, where `b(χ) = ∑_r χ(-r) A_r` is the Bloch matrix. So an eigenvector of `b(χ)`
gives an eigenvector of `B` with the same eigenvalue. Conversely, the Fourier transform
`ψ̂(χ) = ∑_x χ(-x) ψ(x)` of an eigenvector of `B` satisfies `b(χ) ψ̂(χ) = λ ψ̂(χ)`, and a
nonzero function has a nonzero Fourier transform at some momentum, by orthogonality of the
characters. Hence `spec B = ⋃_χ spec b(χ)`, with no analysis: the space is finite dimensional.

For the infinite lattice `ℤ ^ d` the same statement holds on `ℓ²`, where the Fourier transform is
a unitary map onto `L²` of the Brillouin zone, and is proved in `RegularRep.spectrum_blochOperator`.

## ii. Key results

- `FiniteBloch.hopping` : the hopping operator with matrices `A_r`.
- `FiniteBloch.bloch` : its Bloch matrix at a crystal momentum.
- `FiniteBloch.fourier_hopping` : the Fourier transform intertwines the operator with its Bloch
  matrix.
- `FiniteBloch.spectrum_hopping` : the spectrum is the union of the spectra of the Bloch matrices.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The hopping operator and its Bloch matrix
- B. The spectrum

## iv. References

* F. Bloch, Über die Quantenmechanik der Elektronen in Kristallgittern, Z. Phys. 52 (1929). [ref:
  bloch_1929]
* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapters 4 and 8.

sections.text: ## A. The hopping operator and its Bloch matrix

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.FiniteBloch.hopping
declarations.doc:
The hopping operator `(B ψ) x = ∑_r A_r ψ (x - r)` on configurations of a finite periodic
crystal.
declarations.statement:
def hopping (A : G → Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) :
    (G → Fin N → ℂ) →ₗ[ℂ] (G → Fin N → ℂ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.FiniteBloch.hopping_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma hopping_apply (A : G → Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) (ψ : G → Fin N → ℂ) (x : G) :
    hopping A ψ x = ∑ r, (A r).mulVec (ψ (x - r))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.FiniteBloch.bloch
declarations.doc: The Bloch matrix `b(χ) = ∑_r χ(-r) A_r` of a hopping operator.
declarations.statement: def bloch (A : G → Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) (χ : AddChar G ℂ) : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.FiniteBloch.fourier
declarations.doc: The Fourier transform `ψ̂(χ) = ∑_x χ(-x) ψ(x)` of a configuration.
declarations.statement: def fourier (χ : AddChar G ℂ) (ψ : G → Fin N → ℂ) : Fin N → ℂ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.FiniteBloch.fourier_hopping
declarations.doc:
**Bloch's theorem on a finite crystal.** The Fourier transform of `B ψ` at momentum `χ` is
the Bloch matrix applied to the Fourier transform of `ψ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_hopping (A : G → Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) (χ : AddChar G ℂ)
    (ψ : G → Fin N → ℂ) : fourier χ (hopping A ψ) = (bloch A χ).mulVec (fourier χ ψ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.FiniteBloch.mem_spectrum_iff_exists
declarations.doc: An eigenvalue of an operator on a finite-dimensional space is a point of its spectrum.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_spectrum_iff_exists {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] [FiniteDimensional ℂ V]
    (f : Module.End ℂ V) (μ : ℂ) : μ ∈ spectrum ℂ f ↔ ∃ v, v ≠ 0 ∧ f v = μ • v

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.FiniteBloch.mem_spectrum_matrix_iff
declarations.doc: A complex number is in the spectrum of a matrix exactly when it has an eigenvector.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_spectrum_matrix_iff (M : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) (μ : ℂ) :
    μ ∈ spectrum ℂ M ↔ ∃ v : Fin N → ℂ, v ≠ 0 ∧ M.mulVec v = μ • v

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.FiniteBloch.fourier_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma fourier_smul (χ : AddChar G ℂ) (c : ℂ) (ψ : G → Fin N → ℂ) :
    fourier χ (c • ψ) = c • fourier χ ψ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.FiniteBloch.sum_character_smul_fourier
declarations.doc: **Fourier inversion** on a finite abelian group.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_character_smul_fourier (ψ : G → Fin N → ℂ) (x : G) :
    ∑ χ : AddChar G ℂ, χ x • fourier χ ψ = (Fintype.card G : ℂ) • ψ x

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.FiniteBloch.eq_zero_of_fourier_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A configuration with vanishing Fourier transform vanishes.
declarations.statement: lemma eq_zero_of_fourier_eq_zero {ψ : G → Fin N → ℂ} (h : ∀ χ, fourier χ ψ = 0) : ψ = 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.FiniteBloch.hopping_planeWave
declarations.doc: A plane wave of crystal momentum `χ` is mapped to a plane wave with the same momentum.
declarations.statement:
lemma hopping_planeWave (A : G → Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) (χ : AddChar G ℂ)
    (v : Fin N → ℂ) :
    hopping A (fun x => χ x • v) = fun x => χ x • (bloch A χ).mulVec v

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.FiniteBloch.spectrum_hopping
declarations.doc:
**The spectrum of a translation-invariant operator on a finite periodic crystal is the union
of the spectra of its Bloch matrices.**
declarations.statement:
lemma spectrum_hopping (A : G → Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) :
    spectrum ℂ (hopping A) = ⋃ χ : AddChar G ℂ, spectrum ℂ (bloch A χ)

modules.title: Nearest-neighbour hopping on the hypercubic lattice
modules.doc:
The band of nearest-neighbour hopping on the hypercubic lattice, and the irreducible zone modulo
the hyperoctahedral group.

## i. Overview

Nearest-neighbour hopping with amplitude `t` on `ℤ^d` has the Bloch matrix, a `1 × 1` matrix,
`2 t ∑_j cos (2π k_j)` at the momentum with coordinates `k`. Every signed permutation of the
axes is a symmetry of the lattice, and acts on the coordinates by permuting them and changing
their signs, so the band is invariant. Every momentum is carried by a signed permutation into the
set `0 ≤ k_{d-1} ≤ … ≤ k_1 ≤ k_0 ≤ 1/2`, a simplex which is a fraction `1 / (2^d d!)` of the
Brillouin zone. This is the irreducible zone: the Brillouin zone modulo the point group. The
spectrum of the hopping is therefore the set of values of the band on this simplex.

## ii. Key results

- `hypercubicZone` : the simplex `0 ≤ k_{d-1} ≤ … ≤ k_0 ≤ 1/2`.
- `coversOrbits_hypercubic` : every momentum is equivalent to a momentum in the simplex.
- `exists_signedPerm_to_cone` : an explicit signed permutation carrying a momentum into the
  simplex.
- `hypercubicBand`, `hoppingSymbol_hypercubic` : the Bloch matrix of nearest-neighbour hopping.
- `iUnion_spectrum_hypercubic` : the spectrum is the set of values of the band on the simplex.
- `littleGroup_gamma`, `littleGroup_corner` : the centre and the corner of the zone are fixed by
  every symmetry.
- `iUnion_spectrum_hypercubic_eq_Icc` : the spectrum is the interval `[-2 d |t|, 2 d |t|]`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The irreducible zone
- B. The nearest-neighbour band
- C. The spectrum is an interval
- D. The fully symmetric momenta

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 8.

sections.text: ## C. The spectrum is an interval

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.hypercubicCone
declarations.doc: The cone `0 ≤ k_{d-1} ≤ … ≤ k_0 ≤ 1/2` of coordinates.
declarations.statement: def hypercubicCone (d : ℕ) : Set (Fin d → ℝ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.hypercubicZone
declarations.doc: The irreducible zone of the hypercubic lattice: the momenta with coordinates in the cone.
declarations.statement: def hypercubicZone (d : ℕ) : Set (BrillouinZone (Fin d → ℤ))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.signedPerm_mem_symmetries
declarations.doc: **A signed permutation is a bond-preserving symmetry of the hypercubic lattice.**
declarations.statement:
lemma signedPerm_mem_symmetries (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) (ε : Fin d → Bool) :
    (⟨signedPerm π ε, 1, 0⟩ : CellSymmetry (Fin d → ℤ) Unit) ∈
      (hypercubicGraph d).symmetries

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.smul_brillouinPoint_of_linear
declarations.doc:
The coordinates of the image of a momentum under a symmetry whose linear part is a signed
permutation.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_brillouinPoint_of_linear {F : Type*} (s : CellSymmetry (Fin d → ℤ) F)
    (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) (ε : Fin d → Bool) (h : s.linear = signedPerm π ε)
    (k : Fin d → ℝ) :
    s • brillouinPoint k = brillouinPoint (fun j => (signOf (ε j) : ℝ) * k (π.symm j))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.smul_brillouinPoint_signedPerm
declarations.doc: The coordinates of the image of a momentum under a signed permutation.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_brillouinPoint_signedPerm (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) (ε : Fin d → Bool) (k : Fin d → ℝ) :
    (⟨signedPerm π ε, 1, 0⟩ : CellSymmetry (Fin d → ℤ) Unit) • brillouinPoint k =
      brillouinPoint (fun j => (signOf (ε j) : ℝ) * k (π.symm j))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.exists_signedPerm_to_cone
declarations.doc: **Every momentum is carried into the irreducible zone by a signed permutation.**
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_signedPerm_to_cone (k : Fin d → ℝ) :
    ∃ (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) (ε : Fin d → Bool) (k' : Fin d → ℝ), k' ∈ hypercubicCone d ∧
      (⟨signedPerm π ε, 1, 0⟩ : CellSymmetry (Fin d → ℤ) Unit) • brillouinPoint k =
        brillouinPoint k'

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.coversOrbits_hypercubic
declarations.doc: **The hypercubic zone covers the orbits of the point group.**
declarations.statement:
lemma coversOrbits_hypercubic :
    CoversOrbits (hypercubicGraph d) (hypercubicZone d)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.hypercubicBand
declarations.doc:
The band of nearest-neighbour hopping with amplitude `t` on the hypercubic lattice, at the
momentum with coordinates `k`: `2 t ∑_j cos (2π k_j)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hypercubicBand (t : ℝ) (k : Fin d → ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.hoppingSymbol_hypercubic
declarations.doc:
**The Bloch matrix of nearest-neighbour hopping on the hypercubic lattice** is the `1 × 1`
matrix with the entry `2 t ∑_j cos (2π k_j)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hoppingSymbol_hypercubic (t : ℝ) (k : Fin d → ℝ) :
    hoppingSymbol (uniformHopping (hypercubicGraph d) (t : ℂ)) (brillouinPoint k) =
      Matrix.of fun _ _ => ((hypercubicBand t k : ℝ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.iUnion_spectrum_hypercubic
declarations.doc:
**The spectrum of nearest-neighbour hopping on the hypercubic lattice** is the set of values
of the band `2 t ∑_j cos (2π k_j)` on the irreducible zone `0 ≤ k_{d-1} ≤ … ≤ k_0 ≤ 1/2`, which is
`1 / (2^d d!)` of the Brillouin zone.
declarations.statement:
lemma iUnion_spectrum_hypercubic (t : ℝ) :
    (⋃ χ : BrillouinZone (Fin d → ℤ),
        spectrum ℂ (hoppingSymbol (uniformHopping (hypercubicGraph d) (t : ℂ)) χ)) =
      {z : ℂ | ∃ k ∈ hypercubicCone d, z = ((hypercubicBand t k : ℝ) : ℂ)}

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.convex_hypercubicCone
declarations.statement: lemma convex_hypercubicCone : Convex ℝ (hypercubicCone d)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.continuous_hypercubicBand
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_hypercubicBand (t : ℝ) : Continuous (hypercubicBand (d := d) t)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.abs_hypercubicBand_le
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_hypercubicBand_le (t : ℝ) (k : Fin d → ℝ) :
    |hypercubicBand t k| ≤ 2 * d * |t|

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.hypercubicBand_image
declarations.doc:
**The band of nearest-neighbour hopping takes exactly the values in `[-2 d |t|, 2 d |t|]` on
the irreducible zone.**
declarations.statement:
lemma hypercubicBand_image (t : ℝ) :
    hypercubicBand t '' hypercubicCone d = Set.Icc (-(2 * d * |t|)) (2 * d * |t|)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.iUnion_spectrum_hypercubic_eq_Icc
declarations.doc:
**The spectrum of nearest-neighbour hopping on the hypercubic lattice is the interval
`[-2 d |t|, 2 d |t|]`.**
declarations.statement:
lemma iUnion_spectrum_hypercubic_eq_Icc (t : ℝ) :
    (⋃ χ : BrillouinZone (Fin d → ℤ),
        spectrum ℂ (hoppingSymbol (uniformHopping (hypercubicGraph d) (t : ℂ)) χ)) =
      ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) '' Set.Icc (-(2 * d * |t|)) (2 * d * |t|)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.littleGroup_gamma
declarations.doc: **The centre `Γ` of the Brillouin zone is fixed by every symmetry.**
declarations.statement:
lemma littleGroup_gamma (d : ℕ) :
    (hypercubicGraph d).littleGroup (brillouinPoint (0 : Fin d → ℝ)) = ⊤

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.littleGroup_corner
declarations.doc:
**The corner `R = (1/2, …, 1/2)` of the Brillouin zone is fixed by every symmetry**: its
little group is the whole group.
declarations.statement:
lemma littleGroup_corner (d : ℕ) :
    (hypercubicGraph d).littleGroup (brillouinPoint (fun _ : Fin d => (1 / 2 : ℝ))) = ⊤

modules.title: Symmetry of the Bloch matrices of a crystal
modules.doc:
The Bloch matrices of a symmetric crystal at momenta in one orbit of the point group are
conjugate, and at a momentum fixed by a symmetry they commute with it.

## i. Overview

Take a crystal with translation group `G` and the finite set `F` of sites in a cell, and a
translation-invariant Hamiltonian on `ℓ²(G, ℂ^F)` given by hopping matrices `T r`. Its Bloch
matrix at a momentum `χ` is `b(χ) = ∑_r χ(r) T r`. A symmetry `s = (A, σ, b)` moves the site `i`
of the cell `n` to the site `σ i` of the cell `A n + b i`. On the Fourier transform
`ψ̂(χ) = ∑_n χ(n) ψ(n)` it acts by
`(U_s ψ)^(χ) = V_s(χ) ψ̂(χ ∘ A)`, where the fibre matrix `V_s(χ)` is the monomial matrix with the
entry `χ(b i)` at `(σ i, i)`. The symmetry carries the fibre at `χ ∘ A` to the fibre at
`s • χ = χ ∘ A⁻¹`. The fibre matrices satisfy the cocycle identity
`V_{st}(χ) = V_s(χ) V_t(s⁻¹ • χ)`, and they are unitary. The phases `χ(b i)` come from the
offsets `b i` of the sites: for a symmetry that is a pure rotation or reflection of a crystal
with one site per cell they are absent, and a screw axis or glide plane is what makes them
momentum dependent.

The Hamiltonian commutes with `U_s` exactly when `V_s(s • χ) b(χ) = b(s • χ) V_s(s • χ)` for all
`χ`, which is what *covariance* of the symbol means. It holds when the hopping is invariant
under the symmetry, `T (A r + b i - b j) (σ i) (σ j) = T r i j`. Two consequences follow. Along
an orbit of the point group, the Bloch matrices are unitarily equivalent, so their eigenvalues
are the same: the bands are functions on the irreducible zone. At a momentum fixed by `s`, the
Bloch matrix commutes with `V_s(χ)`, so its eigenspaces are representation spaces of the little
group, and an eigenvalue of a Hermitian Bloch matrix has multiplicity at least the least
dimension of an invariant subspace: the degeneracies forced by symmetry.

## ii. Key results

- `fibreMatrix` : the monomial matrix of a symmetry at a momentum.
- `fibreMatrix_mul` : the cocycle identity.
- `fibreMatrix_unitary` : the fibre matrices are unitary.
- `hoppingSymbol` : the Bloch matrix of a family of hopping matrices.
- `IsCovariant`, `isCovariant_of_invariant` : invariant hopping has a covariant symbol.
- `eigenvalues_eq_of_covariant` : the bands agree at momenta related by a symmetry.
- `bandsOnZone` : the bands are functions on the irreducible zone.
- `uniformHopping`, `isCovariant_uniformHopping` : uniform hopping on a periodic graph is covariant
  under all its bond-preserving symmetries.
- `iUnion_spectrum_eq_of_covers` : the spectrum is the union over an irreducible zone.
- `two_le_finrank_of_no_common_eigenvector` : a criterion for twofold degeneracy.
- `le_finrank_eigenspace`, `le_finrank_eigenspace_of_littleGroup` : the multiplicity of an
  eigenvalue at a momentum fixed by the symmetries is at least the least dimension of an
  invariant subspace.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The fibre matrices
- B. The symbol of a hopping family
- C. Bands on the irreducible zone
- D. The little group at a momentum
- E. Hopping from a graph and its symmetries
- F. Restricting to a set of representatives

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.fibreMatrix
declarations.doc:
The fibre matrix of a symmetry `s = (A, σ, b)` at the momentum `χ`: the monomial matrix with
the entry `χ(b i)` at `(σ i, i)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fibreMatrix (s : CellSymmetry G F) (χ : BrillouinZone G) :
    Matrix F F ℂ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.fibreMatrix_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fibreMatrix_apply (s : CellSymmetry G F) (χ : BrillouinZone G) (j i : F) :
    fibreMatrix s χ j i = if j = s.perm i then (χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd (s.shift i)) : ℂ) else 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.fibreMatrix_mul
declarations.doc: **The cocycle identity** for the fibre matrices: `V_{st}(χ) = V_s(χ) V_t(s⁻¹ • χ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fibreMatrix_mul (s t : CellSymmetry G F) (χ : BrillouinZone G) :
    fibreMatrix (s * t) χ = fibreMatrix s χ * fibreMatrix t (s⁻¹ • χ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.fibreMatrix_mul_conjTranspose
declarations.doc: The fibre matrices are unitary.
declarations.statement:
lemma fibreMatrix_mul_conjTranspose (s : CellSymmetry G F) (χ : BrillouinZone G) :
    fibreMatrix s χ * (fibreMatrix s χ)ᴴ = 1

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.fibreMatrix_conjTranspose_mul
declarations.doc: The fibre matrices are unitary.
declarations.statement:
lemma fibreMatrix_conjTranspose_mul (s : CellSymmetry G F) (χ : BrillouinZone G) :
    (fibreMatrix s χ)ᴴ * fibreMatrix s χ = 1

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.hoppingSymbol
declarations.doc: The Bloch matrix `b(χ) = ∑_r χ(r) T r` of a finite family of hopping matrices.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hoppingSymbol (T : G →₀ Matrix F F ℂ) (χ : BrillouinZone G) : Matrix F F ℂ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.IsInvariant
declarations.doc:
A family of hopping matrices is invariant under a symmetry `(A, σ, b)` when
`T (A r + b i - b j) (σ i) (σ j) = T r i j`: the amplitude to hop from `j` to `i` across `r`
equals the amplitude between the transformed sites across the transformed displacement.
declarations.statement: def IsInvariant (T : G →₀ Matrix F F ℂ) (s : CellSymmetry G F) : Prop

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.IsCovariant
declarations.doc:
A symbol `b` on the Brillouin zone is covariant under a symmetry when the fibre matrix
intertwines it: `V_s(s • χ) b(χ) = b(s • χ) V_s(s • χ)`.
declarations.statement: def IsCovariant (b : BrillouinZone G → Matrix F F ℂ) (s : CellSymmetry G F) : Prop

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.entry
declarations.doc:
The entries of a hopping family at a fixed pair of orbitals, as a finitely supported function
of the displacement.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def entry (T : G →₀ Matrix F F ℂ) (i j : F) : G →₀ ℂ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.hoppingSymbol_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma hoppingSymbol_apply (T : G →₀ Matrix F F ℂ) (χ : BrillouinZone G) (i j : F) :
    hoppingSymbol T χ i j = (entry T i j).sum fun r m => (χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd r) : ℂ) * m

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.smul_apply_linear
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_apply_linear (s : CellSymmetry G F) (χ : BrillouinZone G) (r : G) :
    (s • χ) (Multiplicative.ofAdd (s.linear r)) = χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd r)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.isCovariant_of_invariant
declarations.doc: **Invariant hopping has a covariant Bloch symbol.**
declarations.statement:
lemma isCovariant_of_invariant {T : G →₀ Matrix F F ℂ} {s : CellSymmetry G F}
    (hT : IsInvariant T s) : IsCovariant (hoppingSymbol T) s

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.conj_of_covariant
declarations.doc: A covariant symbol is conjugated by the fibre matrix between a momentum and its image.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.charpoly_eq_of_covariant
declarations.doc: The Bloch matrices at related momenta have the same characteristic polynomial.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.eigenvalues_eq_of_covariant
declarations.doc:
**The bands agree at momenta related by a symmetry.** If the Bloch matrices are Hermitian,
their eigenvalues at `χ` and `s • χ` coincide.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.bandsOnZone
declarations.doc:
**The bands are functions on the irreducible zone.** For a symbol that is covariant under all
bond-preserving symmetries of a crystal, the eigenvalues of the Bloch matrices depend only on the
orbit of the momentum under the point group.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.commute_of_smul_eq
declarations.doc: At a momentum fixed by a symmetry, the Bloch matrix commutes with its fibre matrix.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.le_finrank_eigenspace
declarations.doc:
**Symmetry-enforced degeneracy.** If `M` commutes with a set of matrices and every nonzero
subspace invariant under them has dimension at least `m`, every eigenspace of `M` has dimension
at least `m`.
declarations.statement:
lemma le_finrank_eigenspace (M : Matrix F F ℂ) (S : Set (Matrix F F ℂ))
    (hcomm : ∀ V ∈ S, V * M = M * V) {m : ℕ}
    (hS : ∀ W : Submodule ℂ (F → ℂ), W ≠ ⊥ → (∀ V ∈ S, ∀ w ∈ W, V.mulVec w ∈ W) →
      m ≤ Module.finrank ℂ W) (μ : ℂ) (hμ : ∃ v : F → ℂ, v ≠ 0 ∧ M.mulVec v = μ • v) :
    m ≤ Module.finrank ℂ (Module.End.eigenspace (Matrix.toLin' M) μ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.le_finrank_eigenspace_of_littleGroup
declarations.doc:
**Degeneracy forced by the little group.** For a symbol covariant under the bond-preserving
symmetries of a crystal, if every nonzero subspace of `ℂ^F` invariant under the fibre matrices of
the little group at `χ` has dimension at least `m`, every eigenspace of the Bloch matrix at `χ` has
dimension at least `m`.
declarations.statement:
lemma le_finrank_eigenspace_of_littleGroup {g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)}
    {b : BrillouinZone G → Matrix F F ℂ} (hb : ∀ s : g.symmetries, IsCovariant b s)
    (χ : BrillouinZone G) {m : ℕ}
    (hS : ∀ W : Submodule ℂ (F → ℂ), W ≠ ⊥ →
      (∀ s ∈ g.littleGroup χ, ∀ w ∈ W, (fibreMatrix (s : CellSymmetry G F) χ).mulVec w ∈ W) →
      m ≤ Module.finrank ℂ W) (μ : ℂ) (hμ : ∃ v : F → ℂ, v ≠ 0 ∧ (b χ).mulVec v = μ • v) :
    m ≤ Module.finrank ℂ (Module.End.eigenspace (Matrix.toLin' (b χ)) μ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.uniformHopping
declarations.doc:
Hopping with the amplitude `t` between any two bonded sites of a periodic graph: the entry
`(i, j)` of the matrix at the displacement `r` is `t` when the site `j` of a cell is bonded to the
site `i` of the cell displaced by `r`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def uniformHopping (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) (t : ℂ) :
    G →₀ Matrix F F ℂ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.uniformHopping_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma uniformHopping_apply (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) (t : ℂ) (r : G) (i j : F) :
    uniformHopping g t r i j = if g.Bonded j i r then t else 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.isInvariant_uniformHopping
declarations.doc: **Uniform hopping is invariant under every bond-preserving symmetry.**
declarations.statement:
lemma isInvariant_uniformHopping (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) (t : ℂ)
    {s : CellSymmetry G F} (hs : s ∈ g.symmetries) : IsInvariant (uniformHopping g t) s

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.isCovariant_uniformHopping
declarations.doc: **Uniform hopping has a covariant Bloch symbol under every bond-preserving symmetry.**
declarations.statement:
lemma isCovariant_uniformHopping (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) (t : ℂ)
    (s : g.symmetries) : IsCovariant (hoppingSymbol (uniformHopping g t)) s

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.isHermitian_hoppingSymbol
declarations.doc: If `(T r)ᴴ = T (-r)` for all `r`, the Bloch matrices are Hermitian.
declarations.statement:
lemma isHermitian_hoppingSymbol {T : G →₀ Matrix F F ℂ} (hT : ∀ r, (T r)ᴴ = T (-r))
    (χ : BrillouinZone G) : (hoppingSymbol T χ).IsHermitian

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.bonded_symm
declarations.doc:
Bonds are symmetric: the bond from `i` to `j` across `d` is the bond from `j` to `i` across
`-d`.
declarations.statement:
lemma bonded_symm (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) (i j : F) (d : G) :
    g.Bonded i j d ↔ g.Bonded j i (-d)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.isHermitian_hoppingSymbol_uniform
declarations.doc: Uniform real hopping gives Hermitian Bloch matrices at every momentum.
declarations.statement:
lemma isHermitian_hoppingSymbol_uniform (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) (t : ℝ)
    (χ : BrillouinZone G) : (hoppingSymbol (uniformHopping g (t : ℂ)) χ).IsHermitian

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.CoversOrbits
declarations.doc:
A set of momenta covers the orbits of the point group when every momentum is carried into it by
some element of the point group. An irreducible zone is a set that covers the orbits.
declarations.statement: def CoversOrbits (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) (D : Set (BrillouinZone G)) : Prop

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.spectrum_eq_range_eigenvalues
declarations.doc: The spectrum of a Bloch matrix is the set of its eigenvalues.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectrum_eq_range_eigenvalues {M : Matrix F F ℂ} (hM : M.IsHermitian) :
    spectrum ℂ M = ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ) '' Set.range hM.eigenvalues

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.spectrum_eq_of_covariant
declarations.doc: **The spectra of the Bloch matrices at related momenta agree.**

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.iUnion_spectrum_eq_of_covers
declarations.doc:
**The spectrum over the whole Brillouin zone is the spectrum over an irreducible zone.** If a
symbol is covariant under the bond-preserving symmetries, it suffices to take the union of the
spectra of its Bloch matrices over a set of momenta that covers the orbits of the point group.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.two_le_finrank_of_no_common_eigenvector
declarations.doc:
**A criterion for twofold degeneracy.** If the matrices in `S` have no common eigenvector, every
nonzero invariant subspace has dimension at least `2`. Combined with
`le_finrank_eigenspace_of_littleGroup`, this forces every eigenvalue of the Bloch matrix at a
momentum whose little group has no common eigenvector in `ℂ^F` to be at least twofold degenerate.
declarations.statement:
lemma two_le_finrank_of_no_common_eigenvector (S : Set (Matrix F F ℂ))
    (h : ¬∃ v : F → ℂ, v ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ V ∈ S, ∃ c : ℂ, V.mulVec v = c • v)
    (W : Submodule ℂ (F → ℂ)) (hW : W ≠ ⊥) (hinv : ∀ V ∈ S, ∀ w ∈ W, V.mulVec w ∈ W) :
    2 ≤ Module.finrank ℂ W

modules.title: The space of wavefunctions on a lattice with internal states
modules.doc:
`ℓ²(G, ℂ^N)` with its translation representation and its internal matrix algebra.

## i. Overview

The Hilbert space `ℓ²(G, ℂ^N)` of square-summable functions on a countable abelian group `G` with
values in `ℂ^N` carries two commuting structures: the translations `(U_g ψ)(x) = ψ(x - g)`, a
unitary representation of `G`, and the pointwise action of the matrices `M_N(ℂ)` on the internal
index. This is the setting of band theory: `G` is the lattice of translations of a crystal, and `N`
the number of internal states per primitive cell. The space is realized as `L²` of the counting
measure so that the Koopman representation of the translation action applies.

## ii. Key results

- `RegularRep.translation` : the translation representation on `ℓ²(G, ℂ^N)`.
- `RegularRep.internal` : the internal ⋆-homomorphism `M_N(ℂ) → B(ℓ²)`.
- `RegularRep.commute` : the translations commute with the internal algebra.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Counting measure and translations
- B. The internal algebra
- C. The translation commutes with the internal algebra
- D. Localized states and their momentum distribution
- E. The momentum distribution of localized states

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## C. The translation commutes with the internal algebra
## D. Localized states and their momentum distribution
## E. The momentum distribution of localized states

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.measurePreserving_addRight
declarations.doc: Translation of a discrete group preserves the counting measure.
declarations.statement:
lemma measurePreserving_addRight (g : G) :
    MeasurePreserving (fun x : G => x + g) (Measure.count : Measure G) Measure.count

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.shift
declarations.doc: Translation by `a`, as a permutation of the group.
declarations.statement: def shift (a : G) : Equiv.Perm G

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.translations
declarations.doc: The translation action of the group on itself, as permutations.
declarations.statement: def translations : Multiplicative G →* Equiv.Perm G

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.measurePreserving_translations
declarations.statement:
lemma measurePreserving_translations (g : Multiplicative G) :
    MeasurePreserving (translations g) (Measure.count : Measure G) Measure.count

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.Space
declarations.doc:
The Hilbert space `ℓ²(G, ℂ^N)` of square-summable functions on `G` with values in the internal
space `ℂ^N`, as `L²` of the counting measure.
declarations.statement: abbrev Space

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.translation
declarations.doc: **The translation representation** on `ℓ²(G, ℂ^N)`: `(U_g ψ)(x) = ψ(x - g)`.
declarations.statement: def translation : Multiplicative G →* unitary (Space G N →L[ℂ] Space G N)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.pointwise
declarations.doc: Pointwise action of an operator of the internal space on `ℓ²(G, ℂ^N)`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev pointwise (L : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N) →L[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) :
    Space G N →L[ℂ] Space G N

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.pointwise_apply_ae
declarations.statement:
lemma pointwise_apply_ae (L : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N) →L[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N))
    (f : Space G N) : pointwise G N L f =ᵐ[Measure.count] fun x => L (f x)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.pointwise_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma pointwise_mul (A B : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N) →L[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) :
    pointwise G N (A * B) = pointwise G N A * pointwise G N B

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.pointwise_one
declarations.statement:
lemma pointwise_one : pointwise G N (1 : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N) →L[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) =
    1

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.pointwise_star
declarations.statement:
lemma pointwise_star (L : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N) →L[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) :
    pointwise G N (star L) = star (pointwise G N L)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.internal
declarations.doc: **The internal algebra**: a matrix acts on the internal index of a wavefunction, pointwise.
declarations.statement: def internal : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ →⋆ₐ[ℂ] (Space G N →L[ℂ] Space G N)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.translation_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma translation_apply (g : Multiplicative G) (f : Space G N) :
    ((translation G N g : unitary (Space G N →L[ℂ] Space G N)) : Space G N →L[ℂ] Space G N) f =
      Lp.compMeasurePreserving (translations g⁻¹) (measurePreserving_translations g⁻¹) f

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.commute_translation_internal
declarations.doc:
The translations commute with the internal algebra: the matrices act on the internal index and
the translations move the site.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_translation_internal (g : Multiplicative G) (M : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) :
    Commute ((translation G N g : unitary (Space G N →L[ℂ] Space G N)) :
      Space G N →L[ℂ] Space G N) (internal M)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.localized
declarations.doc: The state localized at the origin with internal state `e`.
declarations.statement: def localized (e : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) : Space G N

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.count_preimage_ne_top
declarations.statement:
lemma count_preimage_ne_top (g : Multiplicative G) :
    (Measure.count : Measure G) ((translations g⁻¹) ⁻¹' {(0 : G)}) ≠ ⊤

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.translation_localized
declarations.doc: Translating a localized state moves it to the translated site.
declarations.statement:
lemma translation_localized (g : Multiplicative G) (e : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) :
    ((translation G N g : unitary (Space G N →L[ℂ] Space G N)) : Space G N →L[ℂ] Space G N)
        (localized e) =
      indicatorConstLp 2 ((measurableSet_singleton (0 : G)).preimage
        (measurable_of_countable (translations g⁻¹))) (count_preimage_ne_top g) e

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.inner_localized_translation
declarations.doc: **The matrix coefficients of a localized state are the Kronecker delta.**
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_localized_translation (g : Multiplicative G) (e e' : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) :
    ⟪localized (G := G) e, ((translation G N g : unitary (Space G N →L[ℂ] Space G N)) :
      Space G N →L[ℂ] Space G N) (localized e')⟫_ℂ = if g = 1 then ⟪e, e'⟫_ℂ else 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.pointwise_localized
declarations.statement:
lemma pointwise_localized (L : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N) →L[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N))
    (e : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) : pointwise G N L (localized e) = localized (L e)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.localized_add
declarations.statement:
lemma localized_add (e e' : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) :
    localized (G := G) (e + e') = localized e + localized e'

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.localized_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma localized_smul (c : ℂ) (e : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) :
    localized (G := G) (c • e) = c • localized e

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.vectorMeasure_localized
declarations.doc:
**A localized state has a uniform momentum distribution**: its spectral measure for the
translations is the Haar measure of the dual group, weighted by the squared norm of the internal
state.
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorMeasure_localized (e : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) :
    UnitaryRep.vectorMeasure (translation G N) (localized e) =
      ENNReal.ofReal (‖e‖ ^ 2) • dualHaar (G := G)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.projection_localized_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
The spectral projection of a nonempty open set of crystal momenta does not annihilate a
localized state of nonzero internal state.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.hasFullSupport
declarations.doc:
**The regular representation has full support**: every crystal momentum occurs in every
internal state.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasFullSupport :
    UnitaryRep.HasFullSupport (translation G N) (internal (G := G) (N := N))

modules.title: The translations and symmetries of a crystal on `ℓ²` of its sites
modules.doc:
The space of square-summable functions on the sites of a crystal carries the translations and the
bond-preserving symmetries as a covariant unitary representation.

## i. Overview

The Hilbert space `ℓ²(C.Site)` of a crystal is `L²` of the counting measure on its sites. The
translations act on the sites by permutations, and so do the bond-preserving symmetries. Every
permutation preserves the counting measure, so each group acts unitarily by composition: the
Koopman representation. The two actions are compatible: a symmetry with linear part `A` carries
the translation by `a` to the translation by `A a`. This is exactly the covariance of
`PointCovariance`. The Hilbert space needs no choice of orbitals, and covers any number of sites
per cell.

Consequently the sector reduction of `SectorReduction` applies to every bounded operator on
`ℓ²(C.Site)` that commutes with the translations and the symmetries: the adjacency operator of the
bond graph, any hopping Hamiltonian with symmetric amplitudes, or the unitary group of a
Schrödinger evolution.

## ii. Key results

- `siteTranslation`, `siteSymmetry` : the actions on `ℓ²(C.Site)`.
- `siteTranslation_covariant` : the covariance of the two representations.
- `spectrum_sectorOp_eq_site` : the symmetry reduction of the spectrum of an invariant operator
  to the sectors of momentum.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Counting measure on the sites
- B. The representations
- C. Symmetry reduction

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Counting measure on the sites

declarations.doc: Every set of sites is measurable.
declarations.statement: instance : MeasurableSpace (CellSite G F)

declarations.statement: def latticeAut : g.symmetries →* MulAut (Multiplicative G)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.siteSymmetryPerm_translation
declarations.doc:
A symmetry moves a translated site to the correspondingly translated image: the permutations
of the sites satisfy `s ∘ τ_a = τ_{A a} ∘ s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma siteSymmetryPerm_translation (s : g.symmetries) (a : Multiplicative G) :
    siteSymmetryPerm g s * siteTranslationPerm G F a =
      siteTranslationPerm G F (latticeAut g s a) * siteSymmetryPerm g s

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.siteTranslation_covariant
declarations.doc:
**The translations and the bond-preserving symmetries form a covariant representation on
`ℓ²` of the sites.**
declarations.statement:
lemma siteTranslation_covariant :
    UnitaryRep.IsCovariantRep (latticeAut g) (siteTranslation G F) (siteSymmetry g)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.spectrum_sectorOp_eq_site
declarations.doc:
**Symmetry reduction on a crystal.** Let `T` be a bounded operator on `ℓ²` of the sites of a
crystal, commuting with the translations and with the bond-preserving symmetries. Its restriction
to the sector of total momenta in a set `S` of characters is unitarily equivalent to its restriction
to the sector of momenta in the image of `S` under any symmetry, by the symmetry itself. In
particular their spectra agree.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectrum_sectorOp_eq_site {T : SiteSpace G F →L[ℂ] SiteSpace G F}
    (hTπ : ∀ a, Commute ((siteTranslation G F a : unitary _) : SiteSpace G F →L[ℂ] SiteSpace G F) T)
    (hTρ : ∀ s, Commute ((siteSymmetry g s : unitary _) : SiteSpace G F →L[ℂ] SiteSpace G F) T)
    (s : g.symmetries) {S : Set (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))} (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    spectrum ℂ (UnitaryRep.sectorOp hTπ S) =
      spectrum ℂ (UnitaryRep.sectorOp hTπ (UnitaryRep.dualAct (latticeAut g) s '' S))

modules.title: The spectrum of a translation-invariant operator is the union of the Bloch bands
modules.doc:
For the space `ℓ²(G, ℂ^N)`, the spectrum of the operator of a continuous symbol is exactly the union
of the spectra of its values.

## i. Overview

Let `b` be a continuous function from the Brillouin zone `Ĝ` to the `N × N` matrices, and let
`B = ∫ b dP` be the corresponding translation-invariant operator on `ℓ²(G, ℂ^N)`. We showed that
`spec B ⊆ ⋃_χ spec b(χ)`. The converse holds on `ℓ²(G, ℂ^N)`. If `λ` is an eigenvalue of `b(χ₀)`
with eigenvector `e₀`, the state localized at the origin with internal state `e₀` has the uniform
momentum distribution given by Haar measure, so its component in a small neighbourhood `W` of `χ₀`
is nonzero, and on `W` the symbol maps `e₀` to within `δ` of `λ e₀`. These components are
approximate eigenvectors of `B` with eigenvalue `λ`, so `λ` is in the spectrum. Hence
`spec B = ⋃_χ spec b(χ)`: the spectrum of a translation-invariant operator is the union of the
bands.

## ii. Key results

- `RegularRep.norm_sq_calculus_projection_localized` : the norm of a symbol applied to the
  momentum-`W` component of a localized state.
- `RegularRep.spectrum_blochHom` : `spec ∫ b dP = ⋃_χ spec b(χ)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Norms of spectral components of localized states
- B. The spectrum

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Norms of spectral components of localized states

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.norm_sq_calculus_projection_localized
declarations.doc:
The norm of a continuous function of the translations applied to the momentum-`W` component of
a localized state: the `L²` norm of the function over `W`, for the Haar measure.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_sq_calculus_projection_localized (g : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), ℂ))
    {W : Set (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))} (hW : MeasurableSet W)
    (e : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) :
    ‖UnitaryRep.calculus (translation G N) g
        (UnitaryRep.projection (translation G N) W (localized e))‖ ^ 2 =
      ‖e‖ ^ 2 * ∫ χ in W, ‖g χ‖ ^ 2 ∂(dualHaar (G := G))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.toEuclideanCLM_single_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix unit `E_{ij}` acts on a vector as the `j`-th coordinate carried to the `i`-th.
declarations.statement:
lemma toEuclideanCLM_single_apply (i j : Fin N) (e : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) :
    Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (n := Fin N) (𝕜 := ℂ) (Matrix.single i j (1 : ℂ)) e =
      e j • EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℂ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.internal_single_localized
declarations.doc:
The internal matrix unit `E_{ij}` acts on a localized state by moving the `j`-th component
to the `i`-th.
declarations.statement:
lemma internal_single_localized (i j : Fin N) (e : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) :
    internal (G := G) (Matrix.single i j (1 : ℂ)) (localized e) =
      e j • localized (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℂ))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.blochOperator
declarations.doc: The translation-invariant operator `∫ f dP` of a symbol `f` on `ℓ²(G, ℂ^N)`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev blochOperator (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)) :
    Space G N →L[ℂ] Space G N

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.commute_projection_internal
declarations.doc: The internal matrix units commute with the spectral projections.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_projection_internal (W : Set (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)))
    (M : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) :
    Commute (UnitaryRep.projection (translation G N) W) (internal (G := G) M)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.blochOperator_projection_localized
declarations.doc:
**Action of a symbol on a spectral component of a localized state**: the operator of a symbol
`f` applied to the momentum-`W` component of the state localized at the origin with internal state
`e` is the sum over the internal indices `i` of functions of the translations applied to the
momentum-`W` component of the state localized in the `i`-th internal state.
declarations.statement:
lemma blochOperator_projection_localized
    (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    (W : Set (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))) (e : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) :
    blochOperator f (UnitaryRep.projection (translation G N) W (localized e)) =
      ∑ i, UnitaryRep.calculus (translation G N) (∑ j, e j • UnitaryRep.entry f i j)
        (UnitaryRep.projection (translation G N) W
          (localized (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℂ))))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.entry_combination_apply
declarations.doc: The `i`-th component of a symbol applied to a vector is the combination of its entries.
declarations.statement:
lemma entry_combination_apply
    (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    (e : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) (i : Fin N) (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) :
    (∑ j, e j • UnitaryRep.entry f i j) χ =
      (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (n := Fin N) (𝕜 := ℂ) (f χ) e) i

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.sum_norm_entry_combination
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_norm_entry_combination
    (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    (e : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) :
    ∑ i, ‖(∑ j, e j • UnitaryRep.entry f i j) χ‖ ^ 2 =
      ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (n := Fin N) (𝕜 := ℂ) (f χ) e‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.norm_blochOperator_projection_localized_le
declarations.doc:
**The symbol acts on spectral components of a localized state with the size of the symbol on
those momenta**: if the symbol moves the internal state `e` by at most `δ` at all crystal momenta
in `W`, then the operator of the symbol moves the momentum-`W` component of the localized state by
at most `√N δ` times its norm, up to the norm of `e`.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_blochOperator_projection_localized_le
    (f : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    {W : Set (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))} (hW : MeasurableSet W)
    (e : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) {δ : ℝ}
    (hδ : ∀ χ ∈ W, ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (n := Fin N) (𝕜 := ℂ) (f χ) e‖ ≤ δ) :
    ‖blochOperator f (UnitaryRep.projection (translation G N) W (localized e))‖ ^ 2 ≤
      N * δ ^ 2 * (dualHaar (G := G)).real W

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.norm_sq_projection_localized
declarations.doc: The squared norm of the momentum-`W` component of a localized state.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_sq_projection_localized {W : Set (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))}
    (hW : MeasurableSet W) (e : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin N)) :
    ‖UnitaryRep.projection (translation G N) W (localized e)‖ ^ 2 =
      ‖e‖ ^ 2 * (dualHaar (G := G)).real W

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.spectrum_blochOperator
declarations.doc:
**The spectrum of a translation-invariant operator is the union of its Bloch bands.** For
every continuous symbol `b` on the Brillouin zone, the spectrum of the operator `∫ b dP` on
`ℓ²(G, ℂ^N)` is the union over crystal momenta `χ` of the spectra of the matrices `b(χ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectrum_blochOperator
    (b : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ)) :
    spectrum ℂ (blochOperator b) =
      ⋃ χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), spectrum ℂ (b χ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Bloch.RegularRep.spectrum_blochOperator_eq_bands
declarations.doc:
**The band structure**: for a Hermitian symbol, the spectrum of the translation-invariant
operator on `ℓ²(G, ℂ^N)` is exactly the set of band values `ε_k(χ)`, the ordered eigenvalues of the
Bloch matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectrum_blochOperator_eq_bands
    (b : C(PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G), Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ))
    (hb : ∀ χ, (b χ).IsHermitian) :
    spectrum ℂ (blochOperator b) =
      {z | ∃ (χ : PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G)) (k : Fin (Fintype.card (Fin N))),
        z = ((bandOf (hb χ) k : ℝ) : ℂ)}

modules.title: Balls in the bond graph of a crystal
modules.doc:
The sites within a given number of bonds of a site, and their behaviour under symmetries.

## i. Overview

The *ball* of radius `n` around a site is the set of sites reached by at most `n` bonds. It is a
finite set, as every site has finitely many neighbours. A group acting on the sites and preserving
the bonds carries balls to balls. Balls give the finite regions on which a finite-range
interaction acts: the interactions of a region only reach its bond neighbours.

## ii. Key results

- `PeriodicGraph.ball` : the sites within `n` bonds of a site.
- `PeriodicGraph.mem_ball_add` : following `m` bonds and then `n` bonds stays within `m + n` bonds.
- `PeriodicGraph.mem_ball_smul_iff` : bond preserving group actions carry balls to balls.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Balls

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.statement:

modules.title: Crystals, cells and sites
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A crystal is a perfect periodic arrangement obtained by repeating a unit cell. The unit
cell contains finitely many sites, which may carry atoms, spins or orbitals. A cell is one
translated copy of the unit cell. A label identifies which site within that copy: for
example, A or B in a cell containing two sites. A cell index and a site label together
identify one site in the full crystal.

The translation group `G` determines how the cells repeat. The usual choice is `ℤᵈ`, giving
an infinite discrete crystal. Choosing `(ℤ/mℤ)ᵈ` with positive `m` gives a finite periodic
array with opposite boundaries identified. The definition also permits `ℝᵈ`, describing
continuously translated arrangements.

`Crystal.ofUnitCell G F` constructs the crystal from its translation group `G` and the
finite set `F` of site labels in the unit cell. Taking `F = Fin 2` gives two sites per cell,
labelled `0` and `1`. With `G = Fin 2 → ℤ`, the cells form an infinite two-dimensional
array. With `G = Fin 2 → ZMod 4`, there are four cells in each direction with periodic
identification.

For a crystal `C` built this way, `C.Site` is the type of its sites. The site `⟨n, i⟩` has
cell index `n` and label `i`. Translation by `a`, written `a +ᵥ x`, changes its cell index
to `a + n` and preserves its label. These indices specify site addresses; a geometric
realization supplies physical positions.

## ii. Key results

- `Crystal` : a perfectly repeating arrangement of sites under a translation group.
- `Crystal.ofUnitCell` : the crystal obtained by repeating a unit cell with finitely many labels.
- `CellSite` : the address of a site, a cell index together with a label.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Constructing a crystal from a unit cell

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 4.

sections.text:
## A. Constructing a crystal from a unit cell

Choose site labels `F` for a reference cell. Repeating this cell under translations by `G`
gives one site for each cell index `n : G` and label `i : F`.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal
declarations.doc:
A perfectly repeating arrangement of sites under the translation group `G`.
Every site belongs to one of finitely many families of translated copies.

modules.title: Symmetries of a crystal acting on its Brillouin zone
modules.doc:
The symmetries of a crystal act on the crystal momenta, the translations trivially.

## i. Overview

The crystal momenta of a crystal with translation group `G` are the characters of `G`: the
Brillouin zone. A symmetry `s = (A, σ, b)` sends a plane wave of momentum `χ` to a plane wave of
momentum `χ ∘ A⁻¹`, so the symmetries act on the Brillouin zone through their linear parts. This
is an action of the whole group `CellSymmetry G F` of the crystal, for any number of sites per
cell. Translations have the trivial linear part and act trivially, so the action descends to the
point group, the quotient by the translations.

The stabilizer of a momentum `χ` in the group of symmetries is the *little group* of `χ`. It
contains all translations. Its image in the point group is the *little co-group*. At a generic
momentum the little co-group is trivial, and at a high-symmetry momentum it is large. The orbits of
the point group in the Brillouin zone are the classes of equivalent momenta. The orbit space is the
irreducible Brillouin zone: a band structure of a symmetric crystal is a function on it.

## ii. Key results

- `BrillouinZone` : the group of characters of the translations.
- `CellSymmetry.instMulActionBrillouinZone` : the action of the symmetries on crystal momenta.
- `PeriodicGraph.pointAction` : the action of the point group on the Brillouin zone.
- `PeriodicGraph.littleGroup` : the stabilizer of a momentum among the bond-preserving symmetries.
- `PeriodicGraph.IrreducibleZone` : the orbit space of the Brillouin zone under the point group.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The action of the symmetries
- B. The point group and the little groups
- C. The irreducible zone

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.BrillouinZone
declarations.doc:
The Brillouin zone of a crystal with translation group `G`: the crystal momenta, which are the
characters of `G`.
declarations.statement: abbrev BrillouinZone (G : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] [TopologicalSpace G]

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.dualMap
declarations.doc: A lattice automorphism acts on a character by precomposition.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.dualMap_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma dualMap_apply (A : G ≃+ G) (χ : BrillouinZone G) (a : G) :
    dualMap A χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd a) = χ (Multiplicative.ofAdd (A a))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.dualMap_refl
declarations.statement: lemma dualMap_refl (χ : BrillouinZone G) : dualMap (AddEquiv.refl G) χ = χ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.dualMap_trans
declarations.statement:
lemma dualMap_trans (A B : G ≃+ G) (χ : BrillouinZone G) :
    dualMap B (dualMap A χ) = dualMap (B.trans A) χ

declarations.doc:

`χ` to `χ ∘ A⁻¹`.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.translation_mem_littleGroup
declarations.statement:
lemma translation_mem_littleGroup (χ : BrillouinZone G) (a : G) :
    (⟨CellSymmetry.translation a, g.translation_mem_symmetries a⟩ : g.symmetries) ∈
      g.littleGroup χ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.littleGroup_eq_comap
declarations.doc: The little group is the preimage of the little co-group.
declarations.statement:
lemma littleGroup_eq_comap (χ : BrillouinZone G) :
    g.littleGroup χ = (g.littleCoGroup χ).comap (QuotientGroup.mk' _)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.IrreducibleZone
declarations.doc: The irreducible Brillouin zone: the momenta modulo the point group.
declarations.statement: abbrev IrreducibleZone

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.irreducibleZone_mk_eq_iff
declarations.doc: Momenta in the same orbit of the point group are identified in the irreducible zone.
declarations.statement:
lemma irreducibleZone_mk_eq_iff (χ ψ : BrillouinZone G) :
    (Quotient.mk (MulAction.orbitRel g.pointGroup (BrillouinZone G)) χ : g.IrreducibleZone) =
      Quotient.mk _ ψ ↔ ∃ p : g.pointGroup, p • ψ = χ

modules.title: Coordinates on the Brillouin zone and the action of the symmetries
modules.doc:
The Brillouin zone of `ℤ^d` is the torus of coordinates modulo `1`, and a symmetry acts on the
coordinates by an explicit integer matrix.

## i. Overview

A crystal momentum of the lattice `ℤ^d` is a character `r ↦ exp (2πi k · r)`, determined by the
coordinates `k ∈ ℝ^d` modulo `ℤ^d`: the Brillouin zone is the torus `ℝ^d / ℤ^d`, in coordinates
along the reciprocal basis. A symmetry with linear part `A` sends the momentum of coordinates `k`
to the momentum of coordinates `k'`, with `k'_j = ∑_i k_i (A⁻¹ e_j)_i`: the transpose of the
inverse of the matrix of `A`. Momenta with coordinates in `(1/n) ℤ`, which include the high-symmetry
points of the standard lattices, are the points of finite order. Their equality and the action of a
symmetry on them reduce to divisibility of integers, which can be decided by computation.

Together with `littleGroup` and `IrreducibleZone`, this lets one prove which momenta are equivalent
and what the little group of a momentum is for a given lattice, by integer arithmetic.

## ii. Key results

- `brillouinPoint` : the momentum with given coordinates.
- `brillouinPoint_eq_iff` : two sets of coordinates give the same momentum exactly when they
  differ by integers.
- `brillouinPoint_surjective` : every momentum has coordinates.
- `smul_brillouinPoint` : the action of a symmetry on coordinates.
- `torsionPoint`, `smul_torsionPoint`, `torsionPoint_eq_iff` : momenta of finite order.
- `mem_littleGroup_torsionPoint_iff` : the little group of a momentum of finite order.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Momenta from coordinates
- B. The action of a symmetry on coordinates
- C. Momenta of finite order

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapters 5 and 7.

sections.text: ## B. The action of a symmetry on coordinates

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.brillouinPoint
declarations.doc:
The momentum with coordinates `k` along the reciprocal basis: the character
`r ↦ exp (2πi k · r)` of `ℤ^d`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def brillouinPoint (k : Fin d → ℝ) : BrillouinZone (Fin d → ℤ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.brillouinPoint_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma brillouinPoint_apply (k : Fin d → ℝ) (r : Fin d → ℤ) :
    brillouinPoint k (Multiplicative.ofAdd r) =
      Circle.exp (2 * Real.pi * ∑ j, k j * (r j : ℝ))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.brillouinPoint_single
declarations.statement:
lemma brillouinPoint_single (k : Fin d → ℝ) (j : Fin d) :
    brillouinPoint k (Multiplicative.ofAdd (Pi.single j 1)) = Circle.exp (2 * Real.pi * k j)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.brillouinPoint_eq_iff
declarations.doc: **Two sets of coordinates give the same momentum exactly when they differ by integers.**
declarations.statement:
lemma brillouinPoint_eq_iff (k k' : Fin d → ℝ) :
    brillouinPoint k = brillouinPoint k' ↔ ∀ j, ∃ z : ℤ, k j - k' j = z

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.brillouinZone_ext
declarations.doc: A character of `ℤ^d` is determined by its values on the basis vectors.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.brillouinPoint_surjective
declarations.doc: **Every momentum has coordinates.**
declarations.statement: lemma brillouinPoint_surjective : Function.Surjective (brillouinPoint (d := d))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.apply_eq_sum_single
declarations.doc: A lattice automorphism is determined by its values on the basis vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_sum_single (A : (Fin d → ℤ) ≃+ (Fin d → ℤ)) (r : Fin d → ℤ) (i : Fin d) :
    A r i = ∑ j, r j * A (Pi.single j 1) i

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.smul_brillouinPoint
declarations.doc:
**A symmetry acts on the coordinates of a momentum** by the transpose of the inverse of the
matrix of its linear part.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_brillouinPoint {F : Type*} (s : CellSymmetry (Fin d → ℤ) F) (k : Fin d → ℝ) :
    s • brillouinPoint k =
      brillouinPoint (fun j => ∑ i, k i * (s.linear.symm (Pi.single j 1) i : ℝ))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.torsionPoint
declarations.doc: The momentum with coordinates `m / n`: a point of finite order of the Brillouin zone.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def torsionPoint (n : ℕ) (m : Fin d → ℤ) : BrillouinZone (Fin d → ℤ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.torsionPoint_eq_iff
declarations.doc: **Momenta of finite order are equal exactly when the numerators agree modulo `n`.**
declarations.statement:
lemma torsionPoint_eq_iff {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (m m' : Fin d → ℤ) :
    torsionPoint n m = torsionPoint n m' ↔ ∀ j, (n : ℤ) ∣ m j - m' j

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.smul_torsionPoint
declarations.doc: A symmetry acts on a momentum of finite order by an integer matrix on the numerators.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_torsionPoint {F : Type*} (n : ℕ) (s : CellSymmetry (Fin d → ℤ) F) (m : Fin d → ℤ) :
    s • torsionPoint n m =
      torsionPoint n (fun j => ∑ i, m i * s.linear.symm (Pi.single j 1) i)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.mem_littleGroup_torsionPoint_iff
declarations.doc:
**The little group of a momentum of finite order**, as integer arithmetic: a bond-preserving
symmetry fixes the momentum with numerators `m` modulo `n` exactly when the integer vector
obtained from the matrix of its linear part is congruent to `m` modulo `n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_littleGroup_torsionPoint_iff {F : Type*} [Finite F]
    (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell (Fin d → ℤ) F)) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (m : Fin d → ℤ) (s : g.symmetries) :
    s ∈ g.littleGroup (torsionPoint n m) ↔
      ∀ j, (n : ℤ) ∣ (∑ i, m i * (s : CellSymmetry (Fin d → ℤ) F).linear.symm (Pi.single j 1) i) -
        m j

modules.title: The nearest neighbours of fcc and bcc are words of axis steps
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The bonds `fccBonds` and `bccBonds` are written in the basis of primitive vectors. In the
coordinates of the box, in units of half its sides, a site of the fcc lattice is a point of `ℤ³`
and a nearest neighbour is the sum of two steps of length one along different axes: a face
diagonal. A nearest neighbour of the bcc lattice is the sum of three steps along the three axes:
a body diagonal. Here the converse: every such sum is a nearest neighbour.

A step along an axis is forward or backward, so there are two steps per axis. Steps along
different axes commute, so the two orders of a pair of steps reach the same site. Each face
diagonal is reached by `2` words of two steps and each body diagonal by `6` words of three steps.

## ii. Key results

- `fccBonds_eq_twoStepWords` : the nearest neighbours of fcc, up to sign, are the sums of two
  steps along different axes.
- `bccBonds_eq_threeStepWords` : the nearest neighbours of bcc, up to sign, are the sums of three
  steps along the three axes.
- `card_twoStepWords_fiber`, `card_threeStepWords_fiber` : each neighbour is reached by exactly
  `2`, respectively `6`, words.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Axis steps and their words
- B. Coordinates of the box
- C. The neighbours as words

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 4.

sections.text: ## A. Axis steps and their words

declarations.statement: def axisStep (i : Fin 3) (s : Bool) : Fin 3 → ℤ

declarations.doc: The words of two steps along different axes.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.threeStepWords
declarations.doc: The words of three steps along the three different axes.
declarations.statement: def threeStepWords : Finset ((Fin 3 × Bool) × (Fin 3 × Bool) × (Fin 3 × Bool))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.twoStepSum
declarations.doc: The displacement of a word of two steps.
declarations.statement: def twoStepSum (w : (Fin 3 × Bool) × (Fin 3 × Bool)) : Fin 3 → ℤ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.threeStepSum
declarations.doc: The displacement of a word of three steps.
declarations.statement: def threeStepSum (w : (Fin 3 × Bool) × (Fin 3 × Bool) × (Fin 3 × Bool)) : Fin 3 → ℤ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.twoStepSum_swap
declarations.doc:
Steps along different axes commute: both orders of a word of two steps reach the same
site.
declarations.statement:
lemma twoStepSum_swap (w : (Fin 3 × Bool) × (Fin 3 × Bool)) :
    twoStepSum (w.2, w.1) = twoStepSum w

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.fccCoord
declarations.doc: The coordinates in the box, in units of half its sides, of the cell `n` of the fcc lattice.
declarations.statement: def fccCoord (n : Fin 3 → ℤ) : Fin 3 → ℤ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.bccCoord
declarations.doc: The coordinates in the box, in units of half its sides, of the cell `n` of the bcc lattice.
declarations.statement: def bccCoord (n : Fin 3 → ℤ) : Fin 3 → ℤ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.signedDisplacements
declarations.doc: The displacements of the bonds of a list, with both signs.
declarations.statement: def signedDisplacements (bonds : List (Bond (Fin 3 → ℤ) Unit)) : Finset (Fin 3 → ℤ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.latticeMap_fccVectors
declarations.doc:
The physical position of a cell of the fcc lattice is `fccCoord` in units of half the sides
of the box.
declarations.statement:
lemma latticeMap_fccVectors (a b c : ℝ) (n : Fin 3 → ℤ) (k : Fin 3) :
    latticeMap (fccVectors a b c) n k = ![a, b, c] k / 2 * (fccCoord n k : ℝ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.latticeMap_bccVectors
declarations.doc:
The physical position of a cell of the bcc lattice is `bccCoord` in units of half the sides
of the box.
declarations.statement:
lemma latticeMap_bccVectors (a b c : ℝ) (n : Fin 3 → ℤ) (k : Fin 3) :
    latticeMap (bccVectors a b c) n k = ![a, b, c] k / 2 * (bccCoord n k : ℝ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.fccBonds_eq_twoStepWords
declarations.doc:
The nearest neighbours of the fcc lattice, up to sign, are the sums of two steps along
different axes.
declarations.statement:
lemma fccBonds_eq_twoStepWords :
    (signedDisplacements fccBonds).image fccCoord = twoStepWords.image twoStepSum

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.bccBonds_eq_threeStepWords
declarations.doc:
The nearest neighbours of the bcc lattice, up to sign, are the sums of three steps along the
three axes.
declarations.statement:
lemma bccBonds_eq_threeStepWords :
    (signedDisplacements bccBonds).image bccCoord = threeStepWords.image threeStepSum

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.card_twoStepWords_fiber
declarations.doc: Each nearest neighbour of the fcc lattice is reached by exactly two words of two steps.
declarations.statement:
lemma card_twoStepWords_fiber :
    ∀ v ∈ twoStepWords.image twoStepSum, (twoStepWords.filter (twoStepSum · = v)).card = 2

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.card_threeStepWords_fiber
declarations.doc: Each nearest neighbour of the bcc lattice is reached by exactly six words of three steps.
declarations.statement:
lemma card_threeStepWords_fiber :
    ∀ v ∈ threeStepWords.image threeStepSum,
      (threeStepWords.filter (threeStepSum · = v)).card = 6

modules.title: Standard crystals
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

These examples specify the same three ingredients: a repeated unit cell, its physical
positions and its bonds. The crystal, geometry and graph remain separately accessible.

The hypercubic lattice has one site per cell in any dimension. The chain and square
lattice are its one- and two-dimensional cases. The triangular lattice has six neighbors
per site. The honeycomb lattice has two sites per cell, each with three neighbors.
Their Euclidean geometries use unit nearest-neighbor spacing.

The finite periodic chain places equally spaced sites on a circle of circumference one.
Its bonds connect consecutive cells modulo the period.

## ii. Key results

- `hypercubic`, `square`, `chain` : one site per cell.
- `triangular`, `honeycomb`, `diamond` : standard lattices with their geometries and bond graphs.
- `periodicChain` : a finite periodic chain.
- `honeycomb_neighbors_card`, `diamond_neighbors_card` : coordination numbers.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Hypercubic lattices
- B. Triangular lattice
- C. Honeycomb lattice
- D. Diamond lattice
- E. Finite periodic chain
- F. Coordination numbers
- G. Bond lengths

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 4.

modules.title: Monoclinic and triclinic lattices
modules.doc:
The primitive and base-centred monoclinic lattices and the triclinic lattice, with their
embeddings and the bonds of their first neighbour shells.

## i. Overview

A monoclinic lattice has two axes `a = (a, 0, 0)` and `b = (0, b, 0)` and a third axis
`c = (c₁, 0, c₃)` in the plane of `a` and perpendicular to `b`, at an angle `β ≠ π / 2` with
`a`. The base-centred lattice adds the centres of the `a`–`b` faces. A triclinic lattice has
three axes with no relation between their lengths and angles. Here they are
`(a, 0, 0)`, `(b₁, b₂, 0)`, `(c₁, c₂, c₃)`. As for the orthorhombic lattices, the first shell
alone sees more symmetry than the lattice, and the graph keeps the shells up to the first ones
that pin the point group down. With the lengths below these are:

- primitive monoclinic, `a = 3`, `b = 5`, `c = (1, 0, 3)`: twenty neighbours, the shells at
  squared lengths `9, 10, 13, 25, 34, 35`;
- base-centred monoclinic, `a = 4`, `b = 2`, `c = (1, 0, 3)`: sixteen neighbours, the shells at
  squared lengths `4, 5, 10, 11, 13`;
- triclinic, `(3, 0, 0)`, `(1, 4, 0)`, `(1, 1, 5)`: sixteen neighbours, the shells at squared
  lengths `9, 17, 20, 27, 30, 32, 34, 36`.

## ii. Key results

- `monoclinic`, `baseCentredMonoclinic`, `triclinic` : the lattices, with one site per cell.
- `monoclinicVectors`, `baseCentredMonoclinicVectors`, `triclinicVectors` : primitive vectors.
- `monoclinic_neighbors_card`, `baseCentredMonoclinic_neighbors_card`,
  `triclinic_neighbors_card` : the coordination numbers `20`, `16` and `16`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Primitive monoclinic lattice
- B. Base-centred monoclinic lattice
- C. Triclinic lattice
- D. Coordination numbers

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

modules.title: Orthorhombic lattices
modules.doc:
The primitive, base-centred, body-centred and face-centred orthorhombic lattices, with their
embeddings and the bonds of their first neighbour shells.

## i. Overview

An orthorhombic lattice has three different lengths `a`, `b`, `c` along three orthogonal axes.
The bonds of the first shell alone do not see the three axes as different. For the primitive
lattice the six bonds `±x, ±y, ±z` are those of the simple cubic lattice. A graph with
orthorhombic symmetry needs the shells up to the first ones that tell each axis from the other
two. With the lengths below these are:

- primitive, `(a, b, c) = (3, 4, 7)`: the shells at `3, 4, 5, 6, 7`, twelve neighbours, namely
  `±a x`, `±b y`, `±c z`, the in-plane diagonals `±a x ± b y` and `±2a x`;
- base-centred, `(a, b, c) = (3, 6, 5)`: twelve neighbours, namely `(±a / 2, ±b / 2, 0)`,
  `±a x`, `±c z` and `(±3a / 2, ±b / 2, 0)`;
- body-centred, `(a, b, c) = (2, 7, 5)`: fourteen neighbours, namely the eight
  `(±a / 2, ±b / 2, ±c / 2)`, `±a x`, `±2a x` and `±c z`;
- face-centred, `(a, b, c) = (2, 4, 5)`: eighteen neighbours, namely the twelve face diagonals,
  `±a x` and `(±3a / 2, ±b / 2, 0)`.

As for the cubic lattices, the graph does not depend on the lengths and the embedding does.

## ii. Key results

- `orthorhombic`, `baseCentredOrthorhombic`, `bodyCentredOrthorhombic`,
  `faceCentredOrthorhombic` : the lattices, with one site per cell.
- `baseCentredVectors` : the primitive vectors of the base-centred lattice.
- `orthorhombic_neighbors_card`, `baseCentredOrthorhombic_neighbors_card`,
  `bodyCentredOrthorhombic_neighbors_card`, `faceCentredOrthorhombic_neighbors_card` : the
  coordination numbers `12`, `12`, `14` and `18`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Primitive orthorhombic lattice
- B. Base-centred orthorhombic lattice
- C. Body-centred and face-centred orthorhombic lattices
- D. Coordination numbers

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.
