modules.title: The rhombohedral lattice
modules.doc:
The rhombohedral lattice, with its embedding and the bonds of its first two neighbour shells.

## i. Overview

A rhombohedral lattice has three primitive vectors of the same length with the same angle `α`
between any two of them. Up to a rotation they are `(p, q, q)`, `(q, p, q)` and `(q, q, p)`,
with `cos α = (2 p q + q ²) / (p ² + 2 q ²)`. The six bonds `±aᵢ` of the first shell are those of
the simple cubic lattice, so the first shell alone does not see the threefold axis. When
`-1 / 4 < cos α < 0` the second shell is made of the six vectors `±(aᵢ + aⱼ)`, and the graph with
both shells has twelve neighbours. This holds for instance for `(p, q) = (10, -1)`, with
`cos α = -19 / 102`. The graph is defined by these twelve bonds and does not depend on `p`
and `q`: that they form the two nearest shells is the statement above, not yet a lemma.

## ii. Key results

- `rhombohedral` : the lattice, with one site per cell.
- `rhombohedralVectors` : the primitive vectors `(p, q, q)`, `(q, p, q)`, `(q, q, p)`.
- `rhombohedralGeometry` : the embedding, for `p ≠ q` and `p + 2 q ≠ 0`.
- `rhombohedral_neighbors_card` : the coordination number `12`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The lattice and its embedding
- B. Bonds and coordination number

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

modules.title: Tetragonal and hexagonal lattices
modules.doc:
The primitive and body-centred tetragonal lattices and the primitive hexagonal lattice, with
their embeddings and the bonds of their first neighbour shells.

## i. Overview

A tetragonal lattice is a cubic lattice stretched along one axis: the in-plane length `a` and the
period `c` differ. The bonds of the first shell alone do not see this. For the primitive lattice
the six bonds `±x, ±y, ±z` are those of the simple cubic lattice, and for the body-centred
lattice with `c = a √2` the twelve nearest neighbours are those of the face-centred cubic lattice.
A graph with tetragonal symmetry needs the shells up to the first one that tells `z` from `x`:

- primitive tetragonal, `a < c < a √2`: the shells at `a`, `c` and `a √2`, ten neighbours;
- body-centred tetragonal, `a √2 < c < a √6`: the shells at `a`, `√(a² / 2 + c² / 4)` and
  `a √2`, sixteen neighbours.

The primitive hexagonal lattice has six neighbours at `a` in the plane and two at `c` along the
axis. For `c < a √3` these are the first shells, whatever the order of `a` and `c`.

As for the cubic lattices, the graph does not depend on the lengths and the embedding does.

## ii. Key results

- `tetragonal`, `bodyCentredTetragonal`, `hexagonal` : the lattices, with one site per cell.
- `tetragonalGeometry`, `bodyCentredTetragonalGeometry`, `hexagonalGeometry` : their embeddings.
- `tetragonalGraph`, `bodyCentredTetragonalGraph`, `hexagonalGraph` : their bond graphs.
- `tetragonal_neighbors_card`, `bodyCentredTetragonal_neighbors_card`,
  `hexagonal_neighbors_card` : the coordination numbers `10`, `16` and `8`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Primitive tetragonal lattice
- B. Body-centred tetragonal lattice
- C. Primitive hexagonal lattice
- D. Coordination numbers

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

modules.title: Orthorhombic, cubic and hexagonal close-packed crystals
modules.doc:
The orthorhombic lattice and the face-centred cubic, body-centred cubic and hexagonal
close-packed crystals, with embeddings that allow different lengths along the coordinate axes.

## i. Overview

A cubic lattice has one length, the lattice constant. Stretching the three axes independently
gives the orthorhombic lattice with lengths `a`, `b`, `c`. The face-centred cubic (fcc) lattice
has one site per primitive cell, with primitive vectors from a corner of the conventional cell to
the centres of the three adjacent faces. Each site has twelve nearest neighbours. The body-centred
cubic (bcc) lattice has one site per primitive cell, with primitive vectors from a corner to the
centres of three conventional cells, and eight nearest neighbours. The hexagonal close-packed
(hcp) crystal has two sites per primitive cell, on two interpenetrating hexagonal lattices, and
twelve nearest neighbours for the ideal ratio `c / a = √(8 / 3)`.

Each crystal is a graph, given by the bonds of its nearest neighbours, together with an embedding
in three-dimensional space. The graph does not depend on the lengths. The embedding depends on
`a`, `b` and `c` in the cubic cases, and on `a` and `c` for hcp, and any positive values give an
embedding in which distinct sites have distinct positions. Only for the cubic values `a = b = c`
and the ideal ratio do all bonds of the graph have equal length, so that the graph is the
nearest-neighbour graph of the embedding.

## ii. Key results

- `orthorhombicGeometry` : the hypercubic crystal with a separate length for each axis.
- `fcc`, `bcc`, `hcp` : the crystals, with `fccGraph`, `bccGraph`, `hcpGraph` their bond graphs.
- `fccGeometry`, `bccGeometry`, `hcpGeometry` : their embeddings with free lengths.
- `fcc_neighbors_card`, `bcc_neighbors_card`, `hcp_neighbors_card` : the coordination numbers
  `12`, `8` and `12`.
- `fcc_bond_length`, `bcc_bond_length`, `hcp_bond_length` : bond lengths of the cubic and ideal
  lattices.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Orthorhombic lattices
- B. Face-centred cubic lattice
- C. Body-centred cubic lattice
- D. Hexagonal close-packed crystal
- E. Coordination numbers
- F. Bond lengths

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 4.

modules.title: Boxes of a lattice are asymptotically translation invariant
modules.doc:
The cubes `{0, …, n-1}^d` of the lattice `ℤ^d` satisfy the Følner condition for the translations.

## i. Overview

A translation by `h` moves the cube `B_n = {0, …, n-1}^d` to a cube that overlaps `B_n` in
`∏_j (n - |h_j|)` points, so the fraction of points not shared is `1 - ∏_j (1 - |h_j|/n)`, which
tends to zero. This is the Følner condition (`ProbabilisticTheory.IsRightFolner`) that makes the
averages of a state over the translations by the elements of `B_n` invariant in the limit.

## ii. Key results

- `box` : the cube `{0, …, m-1}^d` of `ℤ^d`.
- `card_box` : it has `m ^ d` points.
- `isRightFolner_boxes` : the cubes are asymptotically invariant under translations along any
  ultrafilter finer than the filter of large cubes.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Cubes and their translates
- B. The Følner property

## iv. References

* F. Greenleaf, Invariant Means on Topological Groups.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.box
declarations.doc: The cube `{0, …, m-1}^d` of the lattice `ℤ^d`.
declarations.statement: def box (d m : ℕ) : Finset (Fin d → ℤ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.card_box
declarations.statement: lemma card_box (d m : ℕ) : (box d m).card = m ^ d

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.image_add_box
declarations.statement:
lemma image_add_box (d m : ℕ) (h : Fin d → ℤ) :
    (box d m).image (· + h) = Fintype.piFinset fun j => Finset.Ico (h j) (m + h j)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.card_image_add_box
declarations.statement: lemma card_image_add_box (d m : ℕ) (h : Fin d → ℤ) : ((box d m).image (· + h)).card = m ^ d

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.card_inter_box
declarations.doc: The overlap of the cube with its translate.
declarations.statement:
lemma card_inter_box (d m : ℕ) (h : Fin d → ℤ) :
    ((box d m).image (· + h) ∩ box d m).card =
      ∏ j, (Finset.Ico (h j) (m + h j) ∩ Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) m).card

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.card_Ico_inter
declarations.statement:
lemma card_Ico_inter (m : ℕ) (a : ℤ) (ha : |a| ≤ m) :
    (Finset.Ico a (m + a) ∩ Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) m).card = m - a.natAbs

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.card_sdiff_add_card_sdiff
declarations.doc: The number of points of the cube not shared with its translate.
declarations.statement:
lemma card_sdiff_add_card_sdiff (d m : ℕ) (h : Fin d → ℤ) :
    (((box d m).image (· + h) \ box d m).card + (box d m \ (box d m).image (· + h)).card : ℝ) =
      2 * ((m : ℝ) ^ d - ∏ j, ((Finset.Ico (h j) (m + h j) ∩ Finset.Ico (0 : ℤ) m).card : ℝ))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.tendsto_box_sdiff
declarations.doc:
**The cubes are asymptotically invariant under translation**: the fraction of the points of
`{0, …, n}^d` that are not shared with a fixed translate tends to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_box_sdiff (d : ℕ) (h : Fin d → ℤ) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (((box d (n + 1)).image (· + h) \ box d (n + 1)).card +
      (box d (n + 1) \ (box d (n + 1)).image (· + h)).card : ℝ) / ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ d)
      atTop (𝓝 0)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.boxes
declarations.doc: The cubes `{0, …, n}^d`, as finite sets of the translation group.
declarations.statement: def boxes (d n : ℕ) : Finset (Multiplicative (Fin d → ℤ))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.image_mul_boxes
declarations.statement:
lemma image_mul_boxes (d n : ℕ) (h : Multiplicative (Fin d → ℤ)) :
    (boxes d n).image (· * h) =
      ((box d (n + 1)).image (· + Multiplicative.toAdd h)).map
        Multiplicative.ofAdd.toEmbedding

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.isRightFolner_boxes
declarations.doc:
**The cubes are a Følner family** for the translations of `ℤ^d`, along any ultrafilter on
`ℕ` finer than the filter of large cubes.
declarations.statement:
lemma isRightFolner_boxes (d : ℕ) (𝒰 : Ultrafilter ℕ) (h𝒰 : (𝒰 : Filter ℕ) ≤ atTop) :
    IsRightFolner (boxes d) 𝒰

modules.title: Crystal geometry
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The geometry of a crystal assigns a physical position to each site. Positions lie in a
metric space `A`, on which the translation group `G` acts by isometries. Translating a
site translates its position by the same group element. Distinct sites occupy distinct
positions.

The physical space may be Euclidean for an infinite crystal,
or a torus for a finite periodic crystal. Its translation action specifies the
physical displacement associated with each cell translation. The periodic and ambient
dimensions need not coincide: a sheet can be embedded in three-dimensional space.

`Geometry C A` supplies the embedding `position` of a crystal `C` into `A`. The physical
distance between sites is the distance between their positions. It is invariant under a
common translation and vanishes exactly when the sites coincide. The same distances
define a metric on the site set through `Geometry.metricSpace`.

## ii. Key results

- `Geometry` : an embedding of a crystal into a metric space compatible with translations.
- `Geometry.ofDisplacements` : positions from lattice displacements and unit-cell offsets.
- `latticeMap` : the linear map from cell indices to physical translations.
- `Geometry.distance_eq_of_adj` : bond lengths depend only on the bond.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Positions and translations
- B. Physical distances
- C. Positions from a unit cell
- D. Bond lengths
- E. Euclidean lattice displacements

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 4.

sections.text:
## C. Positions from a unit cell

Specify the positions of the sites in the reference cell. The position of site `i` in
cell `n` is the translate `n +ᵥ basisPositions i`. These positions must distinguish all
sites, including copies in different cells.

## D. Bond lengths

Translations preserve bond lengths. It therefore suffices to check the bonds starting
in the reference cell to determine the lengths of all graph edges.

## E. Euclidean lattice displacements

Primitive vectors specify the physical displacement of an integer cell index. Their
linear independence ensures that distinct cells have distinct displacements.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Geometry
declarations.doc: An embedding of a crystal into physical space, compatible with translations.
declarations.statement:
structure Geometry {G : Type*} [AddGroup G] (C : Crystal G) (A : Type*)
    [MetricSpace A] where
  /-- Physical translations of the ambient space. -/
  [translations : AddAction G A]
  /-- Physical translations preserve ambient distances. -/
  [isometricTranslations : IsIsometricVAdd G A]
  /-- Physical positions, with distinct sites mapped to distinct points. -/
  position : C.Site ↪ A
  /-- A translated site occupies the corresponding translated position. -/
  position_vadd : ∀ (a : G) (x : C.Site), position (a +ᵥ x) = a +ᵥ position x

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Geometry.distance
declarations.doc: Physical distance between two sites.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def distance (R : Geometry C A) (x y : C.Site) : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Geometry.distance_vadd
declarations.doc: A common cell translation preserves the distance between sites.
declarations.statement:
lemma distance_vadd (R : Geometry C A) (a : G) (x y : C.Site) :
    R.distance (a +ᵥ x) (a +ᵥ y) = R.distance x y

declarations.doc: Zero physical distance identifies the same site.
declarations.statement:
lemma distance_eq_zero (R : Geometry C A) (x y : C.Site) :
    R.distance x y = 0 ↔ x = y

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Geometry.metricSpace
declarations.doc: The metric on crystal sites inherited from their physical positions.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def metricSpace (R : Geometry C A) : MetricSpace C.Site

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Geometry.isometry_position
declarations.doc: The position embedding preserves the induced physical metric.
declarations.statement:
lemma isometry_position (R : Geometry C A) :
    letI := R.metricSpace
    Isometry R.position

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Geometry.ofUnitCell
declarations.doc:
Embed a repeated unit cell by translating its reference positions.
The injectivity condition ensures that no two site addresses occupy the same point.
declarations.statement:
def ofUnitCell (G F : Type*) [AddGroup G] [Finite F] (A : Type*)
    [MetricSpace A] [AddAction G A] [IsIsometricVAdd G A]
    (basisPositions : F → A)
    (injective : Function.Injective (fun x : CellSite G F => x.cell +ᵥ basisPositions x.label)) :
    Geometry (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F) A

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Geometry.ofDisplacements
declarations.doc:
Embed a unit cell using physical displacements and reference positions.
The translation map specifies the displacement of each cell; the injectivity condition
ensures that different sites have different physical positions.
declarations.statement:
def ofDisplacements {G F A : Type*} [AddGroup G] [Finite F] [NormedAddCommGroup A]
    (displacement : G →+ A) (basisPositions : F → A)
    (injective : Function.Injective
      (fun x : CellSite G F => displacement x.cell + basisPositions x.label)) :
    Geometry (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F) A

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Geometry.position_ofDisplacements
declarations.doc: A site's position is its cell displacement plus its position within the reference cell.
declarations.statement:
lemma position_ofDisplacements {G F A : Type*} [AddGroup G] [Finite F]
    [NormedAddCommGroup A] (displacement : G →+ A) (basisPositions : F → A)
    (injective : Function.Injective
      (fun x : CellSite G F => displacement x.cell + basisPositions x.label))
    (x : CellSite G F) :
    (ofDisplacements displacement basisPositions injective).position x =
      displacement x.cell + basisPositions x.label

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Geometry.ofLattice
declarations.doc: A one-site unit cell embedded by an injective physical translation map.
declarations.statement:
def ofLattice {G A : Type*} [AddGroup G] [NormedAddCommGroup A]
    (displacement : G →+ A) (injective : Function.Injective displacement) :
    Geometry (Crystal.ofUnitCell G Unit) A

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Geometry.position_ofLattice
declarations.doc: In a one-site cell, the site's position is its cell displacement.
declarations.statement:
lemma position_ofLattice {G A : Type*} [AddGroup G] [NormedAddCommGroup A]
    (displacement : G →+ A) (injective : Function.Injective displacement)
    (x : CellSite G Unit) : (ofLattice displacement injective).position x =
      displacement x.cell

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Geometry.distance_of_links
declarations.doc: Every translated copy of a bond has its reference-cell length.
declarations.statement:
lemma distance_of_links {G F A : Type*} [AddGroup G] [Finite F] [MetricSpace A]
    (R : Geometry (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F) A) (b : Bond G F)
    {x y : CellSite G F} (h : b.Links x y) :
    R.distance x y = R.distance ⟨0, b.source⟩ ⟨b.displacement, b.target⟩

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Geometry.distance_eq_of_adj
declarations.doc: A common reference bond length gives the length of every generated graph edge.
declarations.statement:
lemma distance_eq_of_adj {G F A : Type*} [AddGroup G] [Finite F] [MetricSpace A]
    (R : Geometry (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F) A) (bonds : List (Bond G F)) (length : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ b ∈ bonds, R.distance ⟨0, b.source⟩ ⟨b.displacement, b.target⟩ = length)
    {x y : CellSite G F} (hxy : (graphFromBonds bonds).Adj x y) : R.distance x y = length

    (Fin d → ℤ) →+ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin D)

declarations.doc: Independent primitive vectors separate the displacements of different cells.

lemma latticeMap_injective {d D : ℕ} {vectors : Fin d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin D)}
    (independent : LinearIndependent ℝ vectors) : Function.Injective (latticeMap vectors)

modules.title: Crystal bonds and connectivity
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A bond specifies a connection between two crystal sites, such as a spin interaction or
an allowed hopping connection. Its endpoints may belong to the same cell or to different
cells. The choice of bonds describes the crystal's connectivity; geometry supplies their
physical positions and lengths.

In a chosen unit cell, a bond is specified by two site labels `i`, `j` and a cell
displacement `δ : G`. It connects site `i` in cell `n` to site `j` in cell `n + δ`, for
every cell `n`. When `δ = 0`, both sites belong to the same cell.

`PeriodicGraph.ofBonds` constructs a connectivity graph from a finite list of bonds.

## ii. Key results

- `PeriodicGraph` : a translation-invariant, locally finite graph on the sites of a crystal.
- `PeriodicGraph.ofBonds` : the graph generated by a finite list of unit-cell bonds.
- `PeriodicGraph.card_neighbors_cell` : the coordination number depends only on the label.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Connections between finite regions
- B. Translation-invariant connectivity
- C. Bonds between finite regions
- D. Bonds in a unit cell
- E. Building the graph from bonds

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## D. Bonds in a unit cell
## E. Building the graph from bonds

declarations.name: SimpleGraph.bondCountBetween
declarations.doc:
Number of connections from sites in `Λ` to sites in `M`. For disjoint regions,
each bond between them is counted once; with `M = Λ`, each internal bond is counted twice.
declarations.statement: def bondCountBetween (g : SimpleGraph X) [DecidableRel g.Adj] (Λ M : Finset X) : ℕ

declarations.name: SimpleGraph.bondCountBetween_le
declarations.doc: A bound on coordination numbers bounds the number of connections from a finite region.
declarations.statement:
lemma bondCountBetween_le (g : SimpleGraph X) [DecidableRel g.Adj] [g.LocallyFinite]
    (Λ M : Finset X) (q : ℕ)
    (hq : ∀ x ∈ Λ, (g.neighborFinset x).card ≤ q) :
    g.bondCountBetween Λ M ≤ q * Λ.card

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph
declarations.doc:
A periodic pattern of undirected connections between crystal sites, with finitely many
neighbors at each site.
declarations.statement:
structure PeriodicGraph {G : Type*} [AddGroup G] (C : Crystal G) where
  /-- The undirected connections between crystal sites. -/
  toSimpleGraph : SimpleGraph C.Site
  /-- Translating both sites preserves their connection. -/
  adj_vadd : ∀ (a : G) (x y : C.Site),
    toSimpleGraph.Adj (a +ᵥ x) (a +ᵥ y) ↔ toSimpleGraph.Adj x y
  /-- Connectivity can be checked for any pair of sites. -/
  [decidableAdj : DecidableRel toSimpleGraph.Adj]
  /-- Each site is connected to only finitely many other sites. -/
  [locallyFinite : toSimpleGraph.LocallyFinite]

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.connected
declarations.doc: Check whether two sites are connected by a crystal bond.
declarations.statement: def connected (g : PeriodicGraph C) (x y : C.Site) : Bool

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.connected_eq_true
declarations.doc: The executable connection test agrees with graph adjacency.
declarations.statement:
lemma connected_eq_true (g : PeriodicGraph C) (x y : C.Site) :
    g.connected x y = true ↔ g.toSimpleGraph.Adj x y

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.connected_vadd
declarations.doc: A common cell translation preserves the executable connection test.
declarations.statement:
lemma connected_vadd (g : PeriodicGraph C) (a : G) (x y : C.Site) :
    g.connected (a +ᵥ x) (a +ᵥ y) = g.connected x y

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.neighbors
declarations.doc: The finite set of sites connected to a given site.
declarations.statement: def neighbors (g : PeriodicGraph C) (x : C.Site) : Finset C.Site

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_neighbors
declarations.doc: Graph neighbors are exactly the sites connected by an edge.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_neighbors (g : PeriodicGraph C) (x y : C.Site) :
    y ∈ g.neighbors x ↔ g.toSimpleGraph.Adj x y

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.translateIso
declarations.doc: A cell translation is an automorphism of the bond graph.
declarations.statement: def translateIso (g : PeriodicGraph C) (a : G) : g.toSimpleGraph ≃g g.toSimpleGraph

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.neighbors_vadd
declarations.doc: Translating a site translates all of its graph neighbors.
declarations.statement:
lemma neighbors_vadd (g : PeriodicGraph C) (a : G) (x : C.Site) :
    g.neighbors (a +ᵥ x) = (g.neighbors x).map (AddAction.toPerm a).toEmbedding

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.card_neighbors_vadd
declarations.doc: The coordination number is constant along translated copies of a site.
declarations.statement:
lemma card_neighbors_vadd (g : PeriodicGraph C) (a : G) (x : C.Site) :
    (g.neighbors (a +ᵥ x)).card = (g.neighbors x).card

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.bondCountBetween
declarations.doc: Count the crystal bonds between finite regions, using its ordinary graph.
declarations.statement: def bondCountBetween (g : PeriodicGraph C) (Λ M : Finset C.Site) : ℕ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond
declarations.doc:
A bond from label `source` in a reference cell to label `target` in the cell indexed
by `displacement`. Translating both endpoints gives the copies of this bond in other cells.
declarations.statement:
structure Bond (G F : Type*) where
  /-- The site label at the start of the bond. -/
  source : F
  /-- The site label at the end of the bond. -/
  target : F
  /-- Translation from the source cell to the target cell. -/
  displacement : G
  deriving DecidableEq

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond.Links
declarations.doc: Site `x` is the source and site `y` is the target of a copy of this bond.
declarations.statement: def Links (b : Bond G F) (x y : CellSite G F) : Prop

declarations.doc: The source and target of a bond can be checked from their site addresses.
declarations.statement: instance [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq F] (b : Bond G F) : DecidableRel b.Links

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond.endpoints
declarations.doc: The sites reached by following this bond in either direction.
declarations.statement:
def endpoints [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq F] (b : Bond G F) (x : CellSite G F) :
    Finset (CellSite G F)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond.mem_endpoints
declarations.doc: A site reached through this bond is connected in one of its two directions.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_endpoints [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq F] (b : Bond G F) (x y : CellSite G F) :
    y ∈ b.endpoints x ↔ b.Links x y ∨ b.Links y x

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond.links_vadd
declarations.doc: Translating the endpoints gives another copy of the same bond.
declarations.statement:
lemma links_vadd (b : Bond G F) (a : G) (x y : CellSite G F) :
    b.Links (a +ᵥ x) (a +ᵥ y) ↔ b.Links x y

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.graphFromBonds
declarations.doc: The undirected graph generated by translating every supplied bond.
declarations.statement:
def graphFromBonds {G F : Type*} [AddGroup G] (bonds : List (Bond G F)) :
    SimpleGraph (CellSite G F)

declarations.doc: Connections generated by a finite bond list can be decided.
declarations.statement:
instance {G F : Type*} [AddGroup G] [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq F]
    (bonds : List (Bond G F)) : DecidableRel (graphFromBonds bonds).Adj

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.bondEndpoints
declarations.doc: The sites reached from `x` by following any of the listed bonds in either direction.
declarations.statement:
def bondEndpoints {G F : Type*} [AddGroup G] [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq F]
    (bonds : List (Bond G F)) (x : CellSite G F) : Finset (CellSite G F)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.mem_bondEndpoints
declarations.doc: Every reached site is an endpoint of one of the listed bonds.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_bondEndpoints {G F : Type*} [AddGroup G] [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq F]
    (bonds : List (Bond G F)) (x y : CellSite G F) :
    y ∈ bondEndpoints bonds x ↔ ∃ b ∈ bonds, b.Links x y ∨ b.Links y x

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.graphFromBonds_adj_vadd
declarations.doc: Adjacency generated by bonds is unchanged by a common cell translation.
declarations.statement:
lemma graphFromBonds_adj_vadd {G F : Type*} [AddGroup G]
    (bonds : List (Bond G F)) (a : G) (x y : CellSite G F) :
    (graphFromBonds bonds).Adj (a +ᵥ x) (a +ᵥ y) ↔ (graphFromBonds bonds).Adj x y

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.neighborsFromBonds
declarations.doc: The distinct neighboring sites connected by the listed bonds, excluding `x` itself.
declarations.statement:
def neighborsFromBonds {G F : Type*} [AddGroup G] [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq F]
    (bonds : List (Bond G F)) (x : CellSite G F) : Finset (CellSite G F)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.mem_neighborsFromBonds
declarations.doc: Bond enumeration gives exactly the neighbors of the generated simple graph.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_neighborsFromBonds {G F : Type*} [AddGroup G]
    [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq F] (bonds : List (Bond G F)) (x y : CellSite G F) :
    y ∈ neighborsFromBonds bonds x ↔ (graphFromBonds bonds).Adj x y

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.ofBonds
declarations.doc:
Construct the periodic graph of a repeated unit cell from its bonds.
Each bond connects its source label to its target label at the specified cell displacement,
in every cell. Connections are undirected; repeated connections and self-loops do not add
neighbors.
declarations.statement:
def PeriodicGraph.ofBonds {G F : Type*} [AddGroup G] [Finite F]
    [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq F] (bonds : List (Bond G F)) :
    PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.neighbors_ofBonds
declarations.doc:
The neighbors in the graph of a bond list are the endpoints of its bonds, without the site
itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma PeriodicGraph.neighbors_ofBonds {G F : Type*} [AddGroup G] [Finite F]
    [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq F] (bonds : List (Bond G F)) (x : CellSite G F) :
    (PeriodicGraph.ofBonds bonds).neighbors x = neighborsFromBonds bonds x

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.card_neighbors_cell
declarations.doc: The coordination number of a cell site equals that of its reference-cell copy.
declarations.statement:
lemma PeriodicGraph.card_neighbors_cell {G F : Type*} [AddGroup G] [Finite F]
    (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) (n : G) (i : F) :
    (g.neighbors ⟨n, i⟩).card = (g.neighbors ⟨0, i⟩).card

modules.title: Translation invariant states of an infinite crystal
modules.doc:
Every state of the quasi-local algebra of the crystal `ℤ^d` with a finite unit cell has a
translation invariant limit state, and so does every thermodynamic limit state of an interaction.

## i. Overview

The translations of the crystal `ℤ^d` act on its quasi-local algebra by `*`-automorphisms
(`translationAction`). The averages of a state over the translations by the points of the cube
`{0, …, n}^d` become invariant as `n → ∞`, because the cubes satisfy the Følner condition
(`isRightFolner_boxes`). A limit point of the averages along an ultrafilter is therefore an
invariant state of the infinite crystal. Applied to the thermodynamic limit state of a canonical
ensemble, this gives a translation invariant state of the interacting infinite system, which is
the input to the reduction of the many-body problem to momentum sectors.

## ii. Key results

- `exists_translation_invariant_state` : every state has a translation invariant limit state.
- `Interaction.translationInvariantState` : the translation invariant state of the canonical
  ensemble of an interaction.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Invariant states of the crystal

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 1,
  Section 4.3.

sections.text: ## A. Invariant states of the crystal

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.cubeUltrafilter
declarations.doc: An ultrafilter on the sizes of the cubes, finer than the filter of large cubes.
declarations.statement: def cubeUltrafilter : Ultrafilter ℕ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.cubeUltrafilter_le
declarations.statement: lemma cubeUltrafilter_le : (cubeUltrafilter : Filter ℕ) ≤ atTop

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.translationInvariantLimit
declarations.doc:
**The translation invariant limit of a state of the crystal `ℤ^d`**: the limit of its
averages over the translations by the points of the cubes.
declarations.statement:
def translationInvariantLimit (φ : AlgState (crystalAlgebra Ω₀ (Fin d → ℤ) F)) :
    AlgState (crystalAlgebra Ω₀ (Fin d → ℤ) F)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.translationInvariantLimit_invariant
declarations.doc: **The translation invariant limit of a state is invariant under the translations.**
declarations.statement:
lemma translationInvariantLimit_invariant (φ : AlgState (crystalAlgebra Ω₀ (Fin d → ℤ) F))
    (a : Fin d → ℤ) (x : crystalAlgebra Ω₀ (Fin d → ℤ) F) :
    translationInvariantLimit Ω₀ φ (translationAction Ω₀ (Multiplicative.ofAdd a) x) =
      translationInvariantLimit Ω₀ φ x

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.translationInvariantState
declarations.doc:
**The translation invariant state of the canonical ensemble** of an interaction on the crystal
`ℤ^d`: the translation average of a thermodynamic limit state of the finite boxes.
declarations.statement:
def _root_.CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.translationInvariantState [Nonempty Ω₀]
    (I : Interaction (fun _ : CellSite (Fin d → ℤ) F => Ω₀)) (β : ℝ) :
    AlgState (crystalAlgebra Ω₀ (Fin d → ℤ) F)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.translationInvariantState_invariant
declarations.doc: The translation invariant state of an interaction is invariant under the translations.
declarations.statement:
lemma translationInvariantState_invariant [Nonempty Ω₀]
    (I : Interaction (fun _ : CellSite (Fin d → ℤ) F => Ω₀)) (β : ℝ) (a : Fin d → ℤ)
    (x : crystalAlgebra Ω₀ (Fin d → ℤ) F) :
    I.translationInvariantState β (translationAction Ω₀ (Multiplicative.ofAdd a) x) =
      I.translationInvariantState β x

modules.title: Uncertainty relations in the invariant states of an infinite crystal
modules.doc:
Robertson's relation for several observables holds in the translation invariant state of an
interaction on the crystal `ℤ^d`, and the translations that fix the state fix entries of `Σ`
and `Ω`.

## i. Overview

The translation invariant state of the canonical ensemble of an interaction is a state on the
quasi-local algebra of the crystal, so `AlgState.robertson_det` applies to it: for every finite
family of observables, `|det Ω| ≤ det Σ`.

The state is invariant under every translation `t_a`. If `t_a` fixes an observable `A` and
reverses an observable `B`, as a translation by one site does for the uniform and the staggered
magnetization of a finite block of an antiferromagnet, then `Σ_AB = Ω_AB = 0` by
`AlgState.covariance_eq_zero_of_symm`. A state that breaks the translation by `a`, such as a
Néel state, need not satisfy this.

## ii. Key results

- `robertson_det_translationInvariantState` : `|det Ω| ≤ det Σ` in the translation invariant
  state of an interaction.
- `covariance_translationInvariantState_eq_zero`,
  `bracket_translationInvariantState_eq_zero` : an observable fixed and one reversed by a
  translation have `Σ_AB = Ω_AB = 0`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Uncertainty relations in the invariant state

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 1,
  Section 4.3.

sections.text: ## A. Uncertainty relations in the invariant state

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.robertson_det_translationInvariantState
declarations.doc:
**Robertson's relation for several observables in the translation invariant state** of an
interaction on the crystal `ℤ^d`.
declarations.statement:
lemma robertson_det_translationInvariantState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (a : ι → selfAdjoint (crystalAlgebra Ω₀ (Fin d → ℤ) F)) :
    |((I.translationInvariantState β).bracketMatrix a).det| ≤
      ((I.translationInvariantState β).covarianceMatrix a).det

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.covariance_translationInvariantState_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
In the translation invariant state, an observable fixed and one reversed by a translation
are uncorrelated.
declarations.statement:
lemma covariance_translationInvariantState_eq_zero :
    (I.translationInvariantState β).covariance A B = 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.bracket_translationInvariantState_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
In the translation invariant state, an observable fixed and one reversed by a translation
have a bracket of expectation zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma bracket_translationInvariantState_eq_zero :
    (I.translationInvariantState β).bracket A B = 0

modules.title: Symmetry reduction of a many-body dynamics on an infinite crystal
modules.doc:
The dynamics of an infinite crystal in a symmetric state is reduced by the sectors of total
momentum, and the point symmetries relate the sectors in an orbit.

## i. Overview

Take the quasi-local algebra `𝔄` of an infinite crystal, with its action of the cell symmetries
by `*`-automorphisms, and a state `ω` invariant under a subgroup `H` of the cell symmetries that
contains the translations. The GNS construction represents `H` unitarily on the Hilbert space of
`ω`. The translations are a subgroup of `H` acting by `π`, and `H` acts by `ρ`; a symmetry `s`
carries the translation by `a` to the translation by `A a`, which is the covariance required by
the sector reduction of `SectorReduction`.

Let a group `Δ`, such as the time translations, act on `𝔄` by `*`-automorphisms preserving `ω`
and commuting with `H`: a translation invariant dynamics with the point symmetries. It acts on
the GNS space by unitaries commuting with `π` and `ρ`. Therefore each unitary of the dynamics is
reduced by the sectors of total momentum, and its restrictions to the sector of the momenta in `S`
and to the sector of the momenta in `s • S` are unitarily equivalent, with the same spectrum, for
every symmetry `s` in `H`. The statement is about arbitrary interacting many-body dynamics: it
uses nothing but the symmetry.

## ii. Key results

- `manyBodyRep` : the unitary representation of the symmetries on the GNS space.
- `manyBodyRep_covariant` : the translations and the symmetries are covariant.
- `spectrum_sectorOp_eq_manyBody` : the symmetry reduction of the spectrum of an invariant dynamics
  to the sectors of total momentum.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The representation on the GNS space
- B. The symmetry reduction

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 1,
  Section 2.3.

sections.text: ## A. The representation on the GNS space

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.manyBodyRep
declarations.doc: **The unitary representation of the symmetries on the GNS space** of an invariant state.
declarations.statement: def manyBodyRep : H →* unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.translationIn
declarations.doc: The translations as elements of the symmetry subgroup.
declarations.statement: def translationIn : Multiplicative G →* H

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.manyBodyTranslation
declarations.doc: The translation representation on the GNS space.
declarations.statement: def manyBodyTranslation : Multiplicative G →* unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.manyBodyTranslation_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma manyBodyTranslation_apply (a : Multiplicative G) :
    manyBodyTranslation H ω hω htrans a = manyBodyRep H ω hω (translationIn H htrans a)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.linearAut
declarations.doc: The action of a symmetry on the lattice of translations, through its linear part.
declarations.statement: def linearAut : H →* MulAut (Multiplicative G)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.manyBodyRep_covariant
declarations.doc: **The translations and the symmetries are covariant on the GNS space.**
declarations.statement:
lemma manyBodyRep_covariant :
    UnitaryRep.IsCovariantRep (linearAut H) (manyBodyTranslation H ω hω htrans)
      (manyBodyRep H ω hω)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.commute_manyBodyRep
declarations.doc:
A dynamics commuting with a symmetry is implemented by an operator commuting with the
unitary implementing the symmetry.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_manyBodyRep (s : H) :
    Commute ((manyBodyRep H ω hω s : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)) : ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)
      (AlgState.gnsAut τ hτ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.commute_manyBodyTranslation
declarations.doc: A dynamics commuting with the symmetries commutes with the translation representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_manyBodyTranslation (a : Multiplicative G) :
    Commute ((manyBodyTranslation H ω hω htrans a : unitary (ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS)) :
      ω.GNS →L[ℂ] ω.GNS) (AlgState.gnsAut τ hτ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.spectrum_sectorOp_eq_manyBody
declarations.doc:
**Symmetry reduction of a many-body dynamics on an infinite crystal.** Let `ω` be a state of the
quasi-local algebra invariant under a group `H` of cell symmetries containing the translations,
and `τ` an automorphism preserving `ω` and commuting with `H`: a time evolution. Then the unitary
implementing `τ` is reduced by the sectors of total momentum, and its restriction to the sector of
the momenta in a set `S` has the same spectrum as its restriction to the sector of the momenta in
the image of `S` under any symmetry `s` in `H`.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectrum_sectorOp_eq_manyBody (s : H)
    {S : Set (PontryaginDual (Multiplicative G))} (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
    spectrum ℂ (UnitaryRep.sectorOp
        (commute_manyBodyTranslation H ω hω htrans τ hτ hcomm) S) =
      spectrum ℂ (UnitaryRep.sectorOp
        (commute_manyBodyTranslation H ω hω htrans τ hτ hcomm)
        (UnitaryRep.dualAct (linearAut H) s '' S))

modules.title: Point groups of Bravais lattices
modules.doc:
The point group of a crystal with one site per cell is the group of automorphisms of its
translation lattice that preserve its bonds.

## i. Overview

The point group of a crystal is the group of its bond-preserving symmetries modulo translations.
A symmetry of any crystal acts on the lattice of cell translations by a lattice automorphism, its
linear part, and this gives a homomorphism `pointLinearHom` from the point group to the lattice
automorphisms. It is not injective in general: a symmetry may permute the sites within every cell
and move none of the cells, and such a symmetry is not a translation.

When there is one site per cell, a symmetry is determined, up to a translation, by its linear part.
An automorphism of the lattice then extends to a bond-preserving symmetry exactly when it maps
the set of bonded displacements to itself. In this case the point group is isomorphic to the
group of lattice automorphisms preserving the bonded displacements (`pointGroupEquiv`). This group
is finite when the graph is connected and has finitely many neighbours; it is the group of
rotations and reflections of the lattice that leave it invariant. No geometry is involved: a
square and a rectangular lattice with the same bonds have the same point group as graphs.

## ii. Key results

- `PeriodicGraph.pointLinearHom` : the action of the point group of any crystal on the lattice.
- `PeriodicGraph.pointStabilizer` : the lattice automorphisms preserving the bonded displacements.
- `PeriodicGraph.pointGroupEquiv` : the point group is isomorphic to this group.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Automorphisms preserving the bonds
- B. The point group of a crystal with one site per cell
- C. The action on the lattice of any crystal

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

sections.text: ## B. The point group of a crystal with one site per cell
## C. The action on the lattice of any crystal

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.pointStabilizer
declarations.doc: The lattice automorphisms that map bonded displacements to bonded displacements.
declarations.statement:
def pointStabilizer (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G Unit)) :
    Subgroup (Multiplicative (AddAut G))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.linearHom
declarations.doc: The linear part of a cell symmetry as a homomorphism to the lattice automorphisms.
declarations.statement: def linearHom (G F : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] : CellSymmetry G F →* Multiplicative (AddAut G)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.linear_mem_pointStabilizer
declarations.doc: Bond-preserving symmetries have linear parts in the point stabilizer.
declarations.statement:
lemma linear_mem_pointStabilizer (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G Unit))
    {s : CellSymmetry G Unit} (hs : s ∈ g.symmetries) :
    Multiplicative.ofAdd s.linear ∈ g.pointStabilizer

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.pointHom
declarations.doc:
The homomorphism from bond-preserving symmetries to the point stabilizer taking a symmetry to
its action on the lattice.
declarations.statement:
def pointHom (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G Unit)) :
    g.symmetries →* g.pointStabilizer

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.pointHom_surjective
declarations.statement:
lemma pointHom_surjective (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G Unit)) :
    Function.Surjective (pointHom g)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.ker_pointHom
declarations.statement:
lemma ker_pointHom (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G Unit)) :
    (pointHom g).ker = (CellSymmetry.translations G Unit).subgroupOf g.symmetries

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.pointGroupEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The point group of a crystal with one site per cell is the group of lattice automorphisms
preserving the bonded displacements.**
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointGroupEquiv (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G Unit)) :
    g.pointGroup ≃* g.pointStabilizer

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.pointLinearHom
declarations.doc:
**The point group of any crystal acts on its translation lattice** through the linear parts of
its symmetries.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointLinearHom {F : Type*} [Finite F]
    (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) : g.pointGroup →* Multiplicative (AddAut G)

modules.title: Counting the point group of a Bravais lattice
modules.doc:
The point group of an `n`-dimensional lattice with a finite set `N` of neighbour displacements
is counted by the possible images of the `n` basis vectors.

## i. Overview

An automorphism of `ℤⁿ` that preserves the set `N` of bonded displacements is determined by the
images of the basis vectors, which are neighbour displacements when the basis vectors are
themselves bonded. A tuple of neighbour displacements, one for each basis vector, defines such
an automorphism exactly when the linear map it determines maps `N` into itself, and is injective
on `N`. Injectivity on the finite set `N` makes the map a bijection of `N`, so its image contains
the basis, and a surjective endomorphism of `ℤⁿ` is an automorphism. The point group is therefore
in bijection with the set of such tuples, a finite set that is counted by a direct computation.

## ii. Key results

- `PeriodicGraph.pointStabilizerEquiv` : the point group is in bijection with the admissible
  tuples of neighbour displacements.
- `PeriodicGraph.card_pointGroup` : its cardinality is the number of admissible tuples.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Linear maps determined by the images of the basis
- B. Admissible tuples
- C. The count

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.act
declarations.doc: The linear map of `ℤⁿ` taking the basis vectors to the given vectors.
declarations.statement: def act (v : Fin n → Fin n → ℤ) : (Fin n → ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] (Fin n → ℤ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.act_apply
declarations.statement: lemma act_apply (v : Fin n → Fin n → ℤ) (d : Fin n → ℤ) : act v d = ∑ j, d j • v j

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.act_single
declarations.statement: lemma act_single (v : Fin n → Fin n → ℤ) (j : Fin n) : act v (Pi.single j 1) = v j

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.apply_eq_act
declarations.doc: A lattice automorphism is determined by the images of the basis vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_act (A : AddAut (Fin n → ℤ)) (d : Fin n → ℤ) :
    A d = act (fun j => A (Pi.single j 1)) d

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.Admissible
declarations.doc:
A tuple of neighbour displacements is admissible when its linear map takes the set of
neighbour displacements into itself, injectively.
declarations.statement:
structure Admissible (N : Finset (Fin n → ℤ)) (v : Fin n → Fin n → ℤ) : Prop where
  mem : ∀ j, v j ∈ N
  mapsTo : ∀ d ∈ N, act v d ∈ N
  injOn : Set.InjOn (act v) N

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.Admissible.image_eq
declarations.doc: An admissible tuple maps the set of neighbour displacements onto itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma Admissible.image_eq {v : Fin n → Fin n → ℤ} (hv : Admissible N v) :
    N.image (act v) = N

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.Admissible.surjective
declarations.doc: An admissible tuple gives a surjective linear map.
declarations.statement:
lemma Admissible.surjective {v : Fin n → Fin n → ℤ} (hv : Admissible N v) :
    Function.Surjective (act v)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.Admissible.injective
declarations.doc: An admissible tuple gives an injective linear map.
declarations.statement:
lemma Admissible.injective {v : Fin n → Fin n → ℤ} (hv : Admissible N v) :
    Function.Injective (act v)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.Admissible.act_mem_iff
declarations.doc: A displacement is a neighbour exactly when its image under an admissible tuple is.
declarations.statement:
lemma Admissible.act_mem_iff {v : Fin n → Fin n → ℤ} (hv : Admissible N v) (d : Fin n → ℤ) :
    act v d ∈ N ↔ d ∈ N

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.Admissible.equiv
declarations.doc: The lattice automorphism of an admissible tuple.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Admissible.equiv {v : Fin n → Fin n → ℤ} (hv : Admissible N v) :
    AddAut (Fin n → ℤ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.Admissible.equiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma Admissible.equiv_apply {v : Fin n → Fin n → ℤ} (hv : Admissible N v) (d : Fin n → ℤ) :
    hv.equiv hN d = act v d

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.pointStabilizerEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The point group of a Bravais lattice is in bijection with the admissible tuples of
neighbour displacements.**
declarations.statement: noncomputable def pointStabilizerEquiv : g.pointStabilizer ≃ {v // Admissible N v}

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.card_pointGroup
declarations.doc:
**The order of the point group** is the number of admissible tuples of neighbour
displacements.
declarations.statement: lemma card_pointGroup : Nat.card g.pointGroup = Nat.card {v // Admissible N v}

modules.title: The point groups of the face-centred and body-centred cubic lattices
modules.doc:
The point group of both cubic Bravais lattices with centring has order forty-eight.

## i. Overview

By `PeriodicGraph.card_pointGroup`, the order of the point group of a Bravais lattice is the
number of triples of neighbour displacements that define a lattice automorphism preserving the
neighbours. For the face-centred cubic lattice, with its twelve neighbours, and the body-centred
cubic lattice, with its eight neighbours, this number is `48`, the order of the full octahedral
group, the symmetry group of the cube with reflections.

The count is established by reflection. Vectors in three dimensions are written as triples of
integers, admissibility becomes a Boolean test on a list of such triples, and the number of
admissible tuples is the length of a list that the kernel computes. The finite type of triples of
neighbours, `PeriodicGraph.admissibleEquiv`, is kept as the direct formulation; deciding the count
on it needs far more memory than the reflection, and does not fit on the cubic lattices.

## ii. Key results

- `PeriodicGraph.card_admissible_eq_length` : the number of admissible tuples is the length of
  the list of admissible triples.
- `fcc_card_pointGroup` : the point group of the face-centred cubic lattice has order `48`.
- `bcc_card_pointGroup` : the point group of the body-centred cubic lattice has order `48`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Neighbour displacements
- B. Computing the count
  - B.1. Admissible tuples as a finite type
  - B.2. Vectors as triples of integers
  - B.3. The Boolean test for admissibility
  - B.4. The count as the length of a list
- C. The cubic lattices

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

sections.text: ### B.1. Admissible tuples as a finite type
### B.2. Vectors as triples of integers

### B.3. The Boolean test for admissibility

The test is written so that the kernel can evaluate it cheaply: equality of triples is tested
component by component, and the condition that the map sends neighbours to neighbours is tested
first, as it is the one that fails for most candidate tuples.
### B.4. The count as the length of a list

## C. The cubic lattices

The neighbour lists are written out, with the neighbours that are not basis vectors first: the
Boolean test fails on most candidate tuples at the first neighbour that is not a basis vector, as
the basis vectors are sent to the columns, which are neighbours by construction.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.bondNeighbors
declarations.doc:
The neighbour displacements of a bond list on a one-site cell: the bond displacements and
their negatives, without zero.
declarations.statement: def bondNeighbors (bonds : List (Bond (Fin n → ℤ) Unit)) : Finset (Fin n → ℤ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_bondNeighbors
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_bondNeighbors (bonds : List (Bond (Fin n → ℤ) Unit)) (d : Fin n → ℤ) :
    d ∈ bondNeighbors bonds ↔ d ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ b ∈ bonds, d = b.displacement ∨ d = -b.displacement

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.bonded_ofBonds_unit
declarations.doc: The bonded displacements of a graph generated by bonds on a one-site cell.
declarations.statement:
lemma bonded_ofBonds_unit (bonds : List (Bond (Fin n → ℤ) Unit)) (d : Fin n → ℤ) :
    (PeriodicGraph.ofBonds bonds).Bonded () () d ↔ d ∈ bondNeighbors bonds

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.admissibleEquiv
declarations.doc: The admissible triples can be counted among triples of neighbour displacements.
declarations.statement:
def admissibleEquiv (N : Finset (Fin n → ℤ)) :
    {v // Admissible N v} ≃ {w : Fin n → ↥N // Admissible N (fun j => (w j : Fin n → ℤ))}
instance (N : Finset (Fin n → ℤ)) (v : Fin n → Fin n → ℤ) : Decidable (Admissible N v)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.Vec3
declarations.doc: Integer vectors in three dimensions, as triples of integers.
declarations.statement: abbrev Vec3 : Type

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.toVec3
declarations.doc: A vector in three dimensions as the triple of its components.
declarations.statement: def toVec3 (d : Fin 3 → ℤ) : Vec3

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.ofVec3
declarations.doc: The vector in three dimensions with the given components.
declarations.statement: def ofVec3 (t : Vec3) : Fin 3 → ℤ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.vec3_eq
declarations.doc: A function on `Fin 3` is the vector of its three values.
declarations.statement: lemma vec3_eq {α : Type*} (v : Fin 3 → α) : ![v 0, v 1, v 2] = v

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.ofVec3_toVec3
declarations.statement: lemma ofVec3_toVec3 (d : Fin 3 → ℤ) : ofVec3 (toVec3 d) = d

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.toVec3_ofVec3
declarations.statement: lemma toVec3_ofVec3 (t : Vec3) : toVec3 (ofVec3 t) = t

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.toVec3_injective
declarations.statement: lemma toVec3_injective : Function.Injective toVec3

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.ofVec3_injective
declarations.statement: lemma ofVec3_injective : Function.Injective ofVec3

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.act3
declarations.doc: The linear map with columns `a`, `b` and `c` applied to `d`, written out in components.
declarations.statement: def act3 (a b c d : Vec3) : Vec3

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.toVec3_act
declarations.doc: The linear map determined by a tuple of columns, in components.
declarations.statement:
lemma toVec3_act (v : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℤ) (d : Fin 3 → ℤ) :
    toVec3 (act v d) = act3 (toVec3 (v 0)) (toVec3 (v 1)) (toVec3 (v 2)) (toVec3 d)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.beq3
declarations.doc: Equality of two triples of integers, component by component.
declarations.statement: def beq3 (a b : Vec3) : Bool

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.beq3_iff
declarations.statement: lemma beq3_iff (a b : Vec3) : beq3 a b = true ↔ a = b

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem3
declarations.doc: Membership of a triple of integers in a list of triples.
declarations.statement: def mem3 (x : Vec3) (l : List Vec3) : Bool

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem3_iff
declarations.statement: lemma mem3_iff (x : Vec3) (l : List Vec3) : mem3 x l = true ↔ x ∈ l

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.admissibleB
declarations.doc:
Whether the columns `a`, `b` and `c` form an admissible tuple for the neighbour list `l`:
the map sends neighbours to neighbours, the columns are neighbours, and the map is injective
on the neighbours.
declarations.statement: def admissibleB (l : List Vec3) (a b c : Vec3) : Bool

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.admissibleTriples
declarations.doc: The admissible triples of neighbours from the list `l`.
declarations.statement: def admissibleTriples (l : List Vec3) : List (Vec3 × Vec3 × Vec3)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.admissible_iff_admissibleB
declarations.doc:
Admissibility with respect to the finset `N` is the Boolean test on a list `l` of the same
vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma admissible_iff_admissibleB (hl : ∀ t, t ∈ l ↔ ofVec3 t ∈ N) (v : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℤ) :
    Admissible N v ↔ admissibleB l (toVec3 (v 0)) (toVec3 (v 1)) (toVec3 (v 2)) = true

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_admissibleTriples
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_admissibleTriples (hl : ∀ t, t ∈ l ↔ ofVec3 t ∈ N) (a b c : Vec3) :
    (a, b, c) ∈ admissibleTriples l ↔ Admissible N ![ofVec3 a, ofVec3 b, ofVec3 c]

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.admissibleTriplesEquiv
declarations.doc: Admissible tuples correspond to the admissible triples of the neighbour list.
declarations.statement:
def admissibleTriplesEquiv (hl : ∀ t, t ∈ l ↔ ofVec3 t ∈ N) :
    {v // Admissible N v} ≃ {t // t ∈ admissibleTriples l}

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.card_admissible_eq_length
declarations.doc:
**The number of admissible tuples** is the length of the list of admissible triples of a
list of the neighbours without repetition.
declarations.statement:
lemma card_admissible_eq_length (hl : ∀ t, t ∈ l ↔ ofVec3 t ∈ N) (hnd : l.Nodup) :
    Nat.card {v // Admissible N v} = (admissibleTriples l).length

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.bondNeighborsList
declarations.doc: The neighbour displacements of a bond list on a one-site cell, as a list of triples.
declarations.statement: def bondNeighborsList (bonds : List (Bond (Fin 3 → ℤ) Unit)) : List Vec3

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.nodup_bondNeighborsList
declarations.statement:
lemma nodup_bondNeighborsList (bonds : List (Bond (Fin 3 → ℤ) Unit)) :
    (bondNeighborsList bonds).Nodup

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_bondNeighborsList
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_bondNeighborsList (bonds : List (Bond (Fin 3 → ℤ) Unit)) (t : Vec3) :
    t ∈ bondNeighborsList bonds ↔ ofVec3 t ∈ bondNeighbors bonds

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_iff_of_perm
declarations.doc:
A list of triples that is a permutation of the computed neighbour list enumerates the
neighbours. Writing the neighbours out, rather than computing them, keeps the kernel's work on
literal integers.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_iff_of_perm {bonds : List (Bond (Fin 3 → ℤ) Unit)} {l : List Vec3}
    (h : l.Perm (bondNeighborsList bonds)) (t : Vec3) : t ∈ l ↔ ofVec3 t ∈ bondNeighbors bonds

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.fccNeighbors
declarations.doc: The twelve neighbours of the face-centred cubic lattice in lattice coordinates.
declarations.statement: def fccNeighbors : List PeriodicGraph.Vec3

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.fcc_card_pointGroup
declarations.doc: **The point group of the face-centred cubic lattice has order `48`.**
declarations.statement: lemma fcc_card_pointGroup : Nat.card fccGraph.pointGroup = 48

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.bccNeighbors
declarations.doc: The eight neighbours of the body-centred cubic lattice in lattice coordinates.
declarations.statement: def bccNeighbors : List PeriodicGraph.Vec3

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.bcc_card_pointGroup
declarations.doc: **The point group of the body-centred cubic lattice has order `48`.**
declarations.statement: lemma bcc_card_pointGroup : Nat.card bccGraph.pointGroup = 48

modules.title: The point group of the hypercubic lattice in every dimension
modules.doc:
The point group of the hypercubic lattice in `d` dimensions consists of the signed permutations
of the axes and has order `2 ^ d * d !`.

## i. Overview

The nearest neighbours of a site of the hypercubic lattice `ℤ^d` are the displacements `±e_j`,
which are the integer vectors whose coordinates have absolute values summing to one. A lattice
automorphism preserves the set of these displacements exactly when it maps each basis vector to
`±e_k` for a distinct axis `k`: it is a permutation of the axes together with a choice of sign
for each axis. All of these signed permutations preserve the bonds. The point group is therefore
the hyperoctahedral group, the symmetry group of the `d`-dimensional cube, which has `2 ^ d`
sign choices and `d !` permutations. For `d = 2` it is the dihedral group of order eight and for
`d = 3` the octahedral group of order forty-eight.

## ii. Key results

- `signedPerm` : the lattice automorphism given by a permutation of the axes and signs.
- `mem_pointStabilizer_hypercubic_iff` : a lattice automorphism preserves the bonds of the
  hypercubic lattice exactly when it is a signed permutation.
- `card_pointGroup_hypercubic` : the point group has order `2 ^ d * d !`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Bonds of the hypercubic lattice
- B. Signed permutations
- C. The point group

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

sections.text: ## A. Bonds of the hypercubic lattice

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.l1
declarations.doc: The sum of the absolute values of the coordinates.
declarations.statement: def l1 (r : Fin d → ℤ) : ℤ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.l1_neg
declarations.statement: lemma l1_neg (r : Fin d → ℤ) : l1 (-r) = l1 r

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.l1_single
declarations.statement: lemma l1_single (j : Fin d) : l1 (Pi.single j (1 : ℤ) : Fin d → ℤ) = 1

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.hypercubic_bonded_iff_exists
declarations.doc: The bonded displacements of the hypercubic lattice are the vectors `±e_j`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hypercubic_bonded_iff_exists (r : Fin d → ℤ) :
    (hypercubicGraph d).Bonded () () r ↔ ∃ j, r = Pi.single j 1 ∨ r = -Pi.single j 1

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.hypercubic_bonded_iff
declarations.doc:
**Two sites of the hypercubic lattice are bonded exactly when their cells differ by a vector
whose coordinates have absolute values summing to one.**
declarations.statement:
lemma hypercubic_bonded_iff (r : Fin d → ℤ) :
    (hypercubicGraph d).Bonded () () r ↔ l1 r = 1

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.signOf
declarations.doc: The sign `+1` for `true` and `-1` for `false`.
declarations.statement: def signOf (b : Bool) : ℤ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.signOf_mul_self
declarations.statement: lemma signOf_mul_self (b : Bool) : signOf b * signOf b = 1

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.abs_signOf
declarations.statement: lemma abs_signOf (b : Bool) : |signOf b| = 1

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.signOf_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma signOf_ne_zero (b : Bool) : signOf b ≠ 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.signOf_injective
declarations.statement: lemma signOf_injective : Function.Injective signOf

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.signedPerm
declarations.doc:
The lattice automorphism that permutes the axes by `π` and multiplies the `i`-th coordinate
by the sign `ε i`.
declarations.statement: def signedPerm (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) (ε : Fin d → Bool) : (Fin d → ℤ) ≃+ (Fin d → ℤ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.signedPerm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma signedPerm_apply (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) (ε : Fin d → Bool) (r : Fin d → ℤ) (i : Fin d) :
    signedPerm π ε r i = signOf (ε i) * r (π.symm i)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.l1_signedPerm
declarations.doc: A signed permutation preserves the sum of the absolute values of the coordinates.
declarations.statement:
lemma l1_signedPerm (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) (ε : Fin d → Bool) (r : Fin d → ℤ) :
    l1 (signedPerm π ε r) = l1 r

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.signedPerm_single
declarations.statement:
lemma signedPerm_single (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) (ε : Fin d → Bool) (j : Fin d) :
    signedPerm π ε (Pi.single j 1) = Pi.single (π j) (signOf (ε (π j)))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.signedPerm_injective
declarations.statement:
lemma signedPerm_injective :
    Function.Injective fun p : Equiv.Perm (Fin d) × (Fin d → Bool) => signedPerm p.1 p.2

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.signedPerm_mem_pointStabilizer
declarations.doc: **A signed permutation preserves the bonds of the hypercubic lattice.**
declarations.statement:
lemma signedPerm_mem_pointStabilizer (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) (ε : Fin d → Bool) :
    Multiplicative.ofAdd (signedPerm π ε) ∈ (hypercubicGraph d).pointStabilizer

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.mem_pointStabilizer_hypercubic_iff
declarations.doc:
**The lattice automorphisms preserving the bonds of the hypercubic lattice are exactly the
signed permutations.**
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_pointStabilizer_hypercubic_iff (A : Multiplicative (AddAut (Fin d → ℤ))) :
    A ∈ (hypercubicGraph d).pointStabilizer ↔
      ∃ (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin d)) (ε : Fin d → Bool), Multiplicative.toAdd A = signedPerm π ε

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.pointStabilizerEquivSignedPerm
declarations.doc:
**The point group of the hypercubic lattice is the group of signed permutations of the
axes**: it is in bijection with the pairs of a permutation and a choice of signs.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointStabilizerEquivSignedPerm :
    (Equiv.Perm (Fin d) × (Fin d → Bool)) ≃ (hypercubicGraph d).pointStabilizer

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.card_pointGroup_hypercubic
declarations.doc: **The point group of the hypercubic lattice in `d` dimensions has order `2 ^ d * d !`.**
declarations.statement:
lemma card_pointGroup_hypercubic (d : ℕ) :
    Nat.card (hypercubicGraph d).pointGroup = 2 ^ d * d.factorial

modules.title: The point groups of the monoclinic and triclinic lattices
modules.doc:
The point groups of the two monoclinic lattices have order four, the holohedry `2/m`, and the
point group of the triclinic lattice has order two, the holohedry `-1`.

## i. Overview

The admissible triples are located by tests, as for the orthorhombic lattices. For the primitive
monoclinic lattice the four point operations are the identity, the reflection `b ↦ -b` in the
plane of `a` and `c`, the rotation by `π` about `b`, and the inversion. For the base-centred
lattice the reflection exchanges the two primitive vectors in the `a`–`b` plane. The triclinic
lattice keeps only the identity and the inversion, the symmetry of every lattice.

## ii. Key results

- `monoclinic_admissible_iff`, `baseCentredMonoclinic_admissible_iff`,
  `triclinic_admissible_iff` : the admissible triples.
- `monoclinic_card_pointGroup`, `baseCentredMonoclinic_card_pointGroup` : order `4`.
- `triclinic_card_pointGroup` : order `2`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The admissible triples
- B. The orders

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.monoclinicPointTriples
declarations.doc:
The four point operations of the primitive monoclinic lattice: the identity, the reflection
`b ↦ -b`, the rotation by `π` about `b` and the inversion.
declarations.statement: def monoclinicPointTriples : Finset (Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℤ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.monoclinic_admissible_iff
declarations.doc:
The point operations of the primitive monoclinic lattice are the four of
`monoclinicPointTriples`.
declarations.statement:
lemma monoclinic_admissible_iff (v : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℤ) :
    Admissible (bondNeighbors monoclinicBonds) v ↔ v ∈ monoclinicPointTriples

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.baseCentredMonoclinicPointTriples
declarations.doc:
The four point operations of the base-centred monoclinic lattice, in the basis
`baseCentredMonoclinicVectors`.
declarations.statement: def baseCentredMonoclinicPointTriples : Finset (Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℤ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.baseCentredMonoclinic_admissible_iff
declarations.doc:
The point operations of the base-centred monoclinic lattice are the four of
`baseCentredMonoclinicPointTriples`.
declarations.statement:
lemma baseCentredMonoclinic_admissible_iff (v : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℤ) :
    Admissible (bondNeighbors baseCentredMonoclinicBonds) v ↔
      v ∈ baseCentredMonoclinicPointTriples

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.triclinicPointTriples
declarations.doc: The two point operations of the triclinic lattice: the identity and the inversion.

modules.title: The point groups of the orthorhombic lattices
modules.doc:
The point groups of the four orthorhombic lattices have order eight: they are the reflections in
the three coordinate planes and their products, the holohedry `mmm`.

## i. Overview

An element of the point group is determined by the images of the three basis vectors, an
admissible triple. Instead of checking all triples of neighbour displacements, each basis vector
is located by a few tests: a displacement `d` is a neighbour exactly when its image is. For the
primitive lattice:

- `x` is the only neighbour, up to sign, whose double is a neighbour, so it goes to `±x`;
- `y` is the only neighbour on both diagonals `x ± y` through `x`, so it goes to `±y`;
- `z` is on no diagonal through `x`, so it goes to `±z`.

The centred lattices are located in the same way by sums of two and three basis vectors. Each
lattice then has exactly eight admissible triples, listed explicitly in the basis of its graph.

## ii. Key results

- `PeriodicGraph.admissible_iff_of_tests` : the admissible triples are a given set, if only its
  triples pass the tests.
- `orthorhombic_admissible_iff`, `baseCentredOrthorhombic_admissible_iff`,
  `bodyCentredOrthorhombic_admissible_iff`, `faceCentredOrthorhombic_admissible_iff` : the eight
  admissible triples of each lattice.
- `orthorhombic_card_pointGroup`, `baseCentredOrthorhombic_card_pointGroup`,
  `bodyCentredOrthorhombic_card_pointGroup`, `faceCentredOrthorhombic_card_pointGroup` :
  order `8`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Tests on admissible triples
- B. The admissible triples
- C. The orders

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

modules.title: The point group of the rhombohedral lattice
modules.doc:
The point group of the rhombohedral lattice has order twelve: it permutes the three primitive
vectors and may reverse all of them, the holohedry `-3m`.

## i. Overview

The admissible triples are located by tests, as for the orthorhombic lattices. A neighbour `a`
goes to a neighbour, and the sums `a + b`, `a + c`, `b + c` and `2a + 2b + c` decide which
triples of neighbours are images of the basis. Exactly twelve triples pass: the six permutations
of the primitive vectors, and the same with all signs reversed. The permutations are the
rotations about the threefold axis `a₁ + a₂ + a₃` and the reflections in the planes through it;
the sign reversal is the inversion.

## ii. Key results

- `rhombohedral_admissible_iff` : the twelve admissible triples.
- `rhombohedral_card_pointGroup` : order `12`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The admissible triples
- B. The order

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

modules.title: The point group of a crystal with several sites per cell
modules.doc:
The point group of a crystal with several sites per cell is compared with the point group of a
Bravais lattice, the lattice of differences of its bonds.

## i. Overview

For a graph given by a list of bonds, the displacements `d` for which site `i` of the reference
cell is bonded to site `j` of the cell `d` form a finite set `E i j`. A cell symmetry `(A, σ, b)`
preserves the bonds exactly when it maps each `E i j` onto `E (σ i) (σ j)` by
`d ↦ A d + b j - b i`, a finite condition.

If site `i` is bonded to site `j` in the cells `d₁` and `d₂`, the difference `d₁ - d₂` is a
translation between two sites with the same label. A symmetry maps both bonds to bonds with
common labels, so its linear part maps these differences to differences. When the differences are
the neighbours of a Bravais lattice, for instance the face-centred cubic lattice for diamond or the
triangular lattice for the honeycomb, the linear parts of the symmetries lie in the point group
of that lattice. If moreover only translations have the identity as linear part, and every point
operation of the lattice lifts to a symmetry, the two point groups are isomorphic. Both conditions
reduce to finite checks.

## ii. Key results

- `PeriodicGraph.bondDisplacements` : the finite sets `E i j` of a bond list.
- `PeriodicGraph.mem_symmetries_ofBonds_iff` : the finite criterion for symmetries.
- `PeriodicGraph.bondDifferences` : the differences `d₁ - d₂` of displacements in a common `E i j`.
- `PeriodicGraph.linear_mem_bondDifferences_iff` : linear parts of symmetries preserve them.
- `PeriodicGraph.pointGroupMulEquivOfLift` : the point group is that of the lattice of
  differences, when the linear part is injective modulo translations and every point operation
  lifts.
- `PeriodicGraph.mem_translations_of_linear_eq` and `PeriodicGraph.lift_of_admissible` : the
  finite checks of these two conditions.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Bonded displacements of a bond list
- B. Differences of bonds
- C. Comparison of point groups
- D. Finite checks

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.
