declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.bondDisplacements
declarations.doc:
The displacements `d` such that site `i` of the reference cell is bonded to site `j` of the
cell `d`, in the graph of a bond list.
declarations.statement: def bondDisplacements (bonds : List (Bond G F)) (i j : F) : Finset G

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.bonded_ofBonds_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma bonded_ofBonds_iff (bonds : List (Bond G F)) (i j : F) (d : G) :
    (ofBonds bonds).Bonded i j d ↔ d ∈ bondDisplacements bonds i j

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_symmetries_ofBonds_iff
declarations.doc:
**A finite criterion for the symmetries of the graph of a bond list**: `(A, σ, b)` is a
symmetry exactly when `d ↦ A d + b j - b i` maps `E i j` onto `E (σ i) (σ j)` for all labels.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_symmetries_ofBonds_iff (bonds : List (Bond G F)) (s : CellSymmetry G F) :
    s ∈ (ofBonds bonds).symmetries ↔ ∀ i j, (bondDisplacements bonds i j).image
      (fun d => s.linear d + s.shift j - s.shift i) =
        bondDisplacements bonds (s.perm i) (s.perm j)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.bondDifferences
declarations.doc:
The nonzero differences `d₁ - d₂` of two displacements in a common `E i j`: translations
between two sites with the same label that are bonded to a common site.
declarations.statement: def bondDifferences (bonds : List (Bond G F)) : Finset G

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_bondDifferences
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_bondDifferences (bonds : List (Bond G F)) (e : G) :
    e ∈ bondDifferences bonds ↔ e ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ i j, ∃ d₁ ∈ bondDisplacements bonds i j,
      ∃ d₂ ∈ bondDisplacements bonds i j, e = d₁ - d₂

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.linear_mem_bondDifferences
CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.linear_mem_bondDifferences_iff
declarations.doc: **The linear part of a symmetry preserves the differences of bonds.**

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.linearToLattice
declarations.doc:
The linear part of a symmetry, as an element of the point stabilizer of the lattice of
differences.
declarations.statement:
def linearToLattice (hΔ : bondDifferences bonds = bondNeighbors bonds') :
    (ofBonds bonds).symmetries →* (ofBonds bonds').pointStabilizer

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.ker_linearToLattice
declarations.statement:
lemma ker_linearToLattice (hΔ : bondDifferences bonds = bondNeighbors bonds')
    (hker : ∀ s ∈ (ofBonds bonds).symmetries, s.linear = AddEquiv.refl _ →
      s ∈ CellSymmetry.translations (Fin n → ℤ) F) :
    (linearToLattice hΔ).ker =
      (CellSymmetry.translations (Fin n → ℤ) F).subgroupOf (ofBonds bonds).symmetries

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.pointGroupMulEquivOfLift
declarations.doc:
**The point group of a crystal with several sites per cell is the point group of its lattice
of differences**, if only translations have the identity as linear part and every point
operation of the lattice lifts to a symmetry.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pointGroupMulEquivOfLift (hΔ : bondDifferences bonds = bondNeighbors bonds')
    (hker : ∀ s ∈ (ofBonds bonds).symmetries, s.linear = AddEquiv.refl _ →
      s ∈ CellSymmetry.translations (Fin n → ℤ) F)
    (hlift : Function.Surjective (linearToLattice hΔ)) :
    (ofBonds bonds).pointGroup ≃* (ofBonds bonds').pointGroup

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.shiftCandidates
declarations.doc: The candidates for the cell offsets of a symmetry, relative to the label `i₀`.
declarations.statement: def shiftCandidates (bonds : List (Bond (Fin n → ℤ) F)) (i₀ : F) : Finset (Fin n → ℤ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_translations_of_linear_eq
declarations.doc:
**Only translations have the identity as linear part**, if every label is bonded to `i₀` and
this holds for the finitely many candidate offsets.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_translations_of_linear_eq (i₀ : F)
    (hconn : ∀ i, i = i₀ ∨ (bondDisplacements bonds i₀ i).Nonempty)
    (h : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm F, ∀ r ∈ Fintype.piFinset fun _ => shiftCandidates bonds i₀,
      r i₀ = 0 → (∀ i j, (bondDisplacements bonds i j).image (fun d => d + r j - r i) =
        bondDisplacements bonds (σ i) (σ j)) → σ = 1 ∧ r = 0)
    (s : CellSymmetry (Fin n → ℤ) F) (hs : s ∈ (ofBonds bonds).symmetries)
    (hL : s.linear = AddEquiv.refl _) : s ∈ CellSymmetry.translations (Fin n → ℤ) F

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.lift_of_admissible
declarations.doc:
**Every point operation of the lattice of differences lifts to a symmetry**, if every
admissible tuple of neighbours does, with a permutation and offsets `b i ∈ T i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lift_of_admissible (hΔ : bondDifferences bonds = bondNeighbors bonds')
    (hN : ∀ j, (Pi.single j 1 : Fin n → ℤ) ∈ bondNeighbors bonds') (T : F → Finset (Fin n → ℤ))
    (h : ∀ w : Fin n → bondNeighbors bonds', Admissible (bondNeighbors bonds') (fun j => w j) →
      ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm F, ∃ b ∈ Fintype.piFinset T, ∀ i j, (bondDisplacements bonds i j).image
        (fun d => act (fun j => w j) d + b j - b i) = bondDisplacements bonds (σ i) (σ j)) :
    Function.Surjective (linearToLattice hΔ)

modules.title: The point groups of the tetragonal and hexagonal lattices
modules.doc:
The point groups of the primitive and body-centred tetragonal lattices have order sixteen, and
the point group of the primitive hexagonal lattice has order twenty-four.

## i. Overview

The orders are counted as for the cubic lattices, by `PeriodicGraph.card_pointGroup` and the
reflection of admissibility into a Boolean test on lists of triples of integers. They are those of
the holohedries `4/mmm` and `6/mmm`. With the bonds of the first shell only, the primitive
tetragonal graph is the simple cubic graph, and its point group has order `48`.

The exponent of each group is computed in the same way: an element of the point stabilizer is
determined by the images of the three basis vectors, so it is enough to check its powers on the
basis, for each admissible triple, which is again a Boolean test on the list of admissible
triples. Every element of the primitive tetragonal point group satisfies `A ^ 4 = 1`, and every
element of the hexagonal point group satisfies `A ^ 6 = 1`. So the primitive tetragonal group has
no rotation of order three, and the hexagonal group none of order four.

## ii. Key results

- `tetragonal_card_pointGroup`, `bodyCentredTetragonal_card_pointGroup` : order `16`.
- `hexagonal_card_pointGroup` : order `24`.
- `tetragonal_pow_four` : `A ^ 4 = 1` on the point stabilizer.
- `hexagonal_pow_six` : `A ^ 6 = 1` on the point stabilizer.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Powers from admissible triples
- B. The orders
- C. The exponents

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

sections.text:
## B. The orders

The neighbour lists are written out with the neighbours that are not basis vectors first, so
that the Boolean test fails early on most candidate tuples.

modules.title: The quasi-local algebra of an infinite crystal
modules.doc:
The quasi-local algebra of a crystal carries an action of its cell symmetries, the translations
among them.

## i. Overview

The sites of a crystal are the sites `⟨n, i⟩` of the cells `n`, a countable set, infinite for the
translation group `ℤ^d`. If every site carries the same finite configuration space `Ω₀`, such as
the two states of a spin, the observables of a finite set of sites form a matrix algebra, and the
quasi-local algebra of the crystal is the direct limit over the finite regions.

The group `CellSymmetry G F` of the crystal acts on its sites, so it acts on the quasi-local
algebra by `*`-automorphisms. This group contains the translations as a normal subgroup, so the
translations act as a subgroup of the automorphisms. A symmetry `s` and a translation `t_a`
satisfy `s t_a s⁻¹ = t_{A a}` in the group, and the action respects this relation. Every bond
preserving symmetry of a periodic graph is among the cell symmetries.

## ii. Key results

- `crystalAlgebra` : the quasi-local algebra of a crystal.
- `cellSymmetryAction` : the action of the cell symmetries by `*`-automorphisms.
- `translationAction` : the action of the translations.
- `cellSymmetryAction_translation_conj` : a symmetry carries the translation by `a` to the
  translation by `A a`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The quasi-local algebra of a crystal
- B. The symmetries and the translations

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 2,
  Section 6.1.

sections.text: ## A. The quasi-local algebra of a crystal
## B. The symmetries and the translations

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.crystalAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**The quasi-local algebra of an infinite crystal** whose sites all carry the finite
configuration space `Ω₀`.
declarations.statement: abbrev crystalAlgebra (G F : Type*) [DecidableEq (CellSite G F)]

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.cellSymmetryAction
declarations.doc: **The cell symmetries of a crystal act on its quasi-local algebra** by `*`-automorphisms.
declarations.statement: def cellSymmetryAction : CellSymmetry G F →* (crystalAlgebra Ω₀ G F ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] crystalAlgebra Ω₀ G F)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.translationHom
declarations.doc: The translations as cell symmetries.
declarations.statement: def translationHom (G F : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] : Multiplicative G →* CellSymmetry G F

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.translationAction
declarations.doc: **The translations act on the quasi-local algebra** by `*`-automorphisms.
declarations.statement: def translationAction : Multiplicative G →* (crystalAlgebra Ω₀ G F ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] crystalAlgebra Ω₀ G F)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.cellSymmetryAction_translation_conj
declarations.doc: **Covariance**: a cell symmetry carries the translation by `a` to the translation by `A a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cellSymmetryAction_translation_conj (s : CellSymmetry G F) (a : G) :
    cellSymmetryAction Ω₀ s * cellSymmetryAction Ω₀ (CellSymmetry.translation a) *
        (cellSymmetryAction Ω₀ s)⁻¹ =
      cellSymmetryAction Ω₀ (CellSymmetry.translation (s.linear a))

modules.title: Reciprocal lattice
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A Bravais lattice with primitive translations `a₁, …, a_d` in Euclidean space acts on
functions of position by translation. A plane wave `r ↦ exp(i k · r)` of wave vector `k`
restricts to the lattice as the character `n ↦ exp(i Σ_j n_j ⟨a_j, k⟩)` of the translation
group `ℤ^d`. Two wave vectors give the same character exactly when they differ by an element of
the reciprocal lattice, the set of `k` with `⟨a_j, k⟩ ∈ 2π ℤ` for every `j`. The Brillouin zone
is the quotient of wave-vector space by this lattice, and it is the Pontryagin dual of the
translation group.

`dualCharacter a k` is the character of `ℤ^d` determined by the wave vector `k`.
`reciprocalLattice a` is its kernel in wave-vector space. For `d` independent vectors in
`ℝ^d`, `reciprocalBasis` is the basis `b_i` with `⟨a_j, b_i⟩ = 2π δ_ij`, and
`dualCharacter_surjective` states that every character of `ℤ^d` arises from a wave vector, so
that wave-vector space modulo the reciprocal lattice is the full dual.

## ii. Key results

- `dualCharacter` : the character of the translation group given by a wave vector.
- `reciprocalLattice` : the wave vectors whose plane wave is trivial on the lattice.
- `dualCharacter_eq_one_iff` : the kernel of `dualCharacter` is the reciprocal lattice.
- `reciprocalBasis` : the basis `b_i` with `⟨a_j, b_i⟩ = 2π δ_ij`.
- `dualCharacter_surjective` : every character of the translation group is a plane wave.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Characters from wave vectors
- B. The reciprocal basis

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 5.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.phase
declarations.doc:
The phase accumulated by a plane wave of wave vector `k` under the lattice translation
`n`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def phase (k : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin D)) (n : Multiplicative (Fin d → ℤ)) : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.dualCharacter
declarations.doc: The character of the translation group `ℤ^d` given by the plane wave of wave vector `k`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dualCharacter (k : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin D)) :
    PontryaginDual (Multiplicative (Fin d → ℤ))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.reciprocalLattice
declarations.doc:
The reciprocal lattice: wave vectors whose plane wave is trivial on every lattice
translation.
declarations.statement: def reciprocalLattice : AddSubgroup (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin D))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.dualCharacter_apply
declarations.doc: Evaluating the character of a wave vector gives the exponential of the phase.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualCharacter_apply (k : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin D)) (n : Multiplicative (Fin d → ℤ)) :
    dualCharacter a k n = Circle.exp (phase a k n)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.phase_add
declarations.doc: The phase of a lattice translation is additive in the wave vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma phase_add (k l : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin D)) (n : Multiplicative (Fin d → ℤ)) :
    phase a (k + l) n = phase a k n + phase a l n

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.dualCharacter_eq_one_iff
declarations.doc: A wave vector gives the trivial character exactly when it lies in the reciprocal lattice.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualCharacter_eq_one_iff (k : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin D)) :
    dualCharacter a k = 1 ↔ k ∈ reciprocalLattice a

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.dualCharacter_add_of_mem
declarations.doc: Wave vectors differing by a reciprocal lattice vector give the same character.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualCharacter_add_of_mem {k l : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin D)}
    (hl : l ∈ reciprocalLattice a) : dualCharacter a (k + l) = dualCharacter a k

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.latticeBasis
declarations.doc: The basis of space formed by independent primitive translations.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def latticeBasis (ha : LinearIndependent ℝ a) :
    Module.Basis (Fin d) ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.reciprocalBasis
declarations.doc: The reciprocal basis `b_i`, characterized by `⟨a_j, b_i⟩ = 2π δ_ij`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def reciprocalBasis (ha : LinearIndependent ℝ a) (i : Fin d) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.inner_reciprocalBasis
declarations.doc: The reciprocal basis is dual to the primitive translations up to the factor `2π`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_reciprocalBasis (ha : LinearIndependent ℝ a) (i j : Fin d) :
    ⟪a j, reciprocalBasis ha i⟫ = if i = j then 2 * Real.pi else 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.dualCharacter_surjective
declarations.doc: Every character of the translation group is the plane wave of some wave vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualCharacter_surjective (ha : LinearIndependent ℝ a) :
    Function.Surjective (dualCharacter a)

modules.title: Symmetries of a crystal graph
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The symmetries of a crystal that map translated copies of the unit cell onto translated copies
are described by finite data. A symmetry `(A, σ, b)` consists of an automorphism `A` of the
translation group, a permutation `σ` of the site labels of the unit cell, and for each label `i`
a cell offset `b i`. It sends the site `i` of cell `n` to the site `σ i` of cell `A n + b i`.
Composing two symmetries composes these data, so they form a group `CellSymmetry G F`.
Translations by `a` are the symmetries with `A = 1`, `σ = 1` and `b = a`. Conjugating a
translation by a symmetry gives the translation by `A a`, so the translations form a normal
subgroup. The quotient is the abstract point group, which need not be a subgroup: a screw axis or
glide plane of a non-symmorphic crystal is a symmetry whose offsets cannot be removed.

A symmetry preserves the bonds of a periodic graph exactly when the relation "site `i` in the
reference cell is bonded to site `j` in the cell `d`" is carried to the same relation for the
transformed data, namely `(σ i, σ j, A d + b j - b i)`. This is a finite condition on the bond
data of one unit cell. Bond-preserving symmetries form a subgroup `PeriodicGraph.symmetries` and
act by automorphisms of the bond graph. Conversely, every graph automorphism that normalises the
translations arises this way.

The graph alone knows nothing of physical lengths and angles. A square lattice has the symmetry
group `ℤ² ⋊ D₄` as a graph, whether or not its two lattice constants are equal. The geometric
point group is the subgroup of these symmetries compatible with a chosen `Geometry`.

## ii. Key results

- `CellSymmetry` : the group of symmetries `(A, σ, b)` of the translation structure.
- `CellSymmetry.translations` : the normal subgroup of translations.
- `PeriodicGraph.symmetries` : the subgroup preserving the bonds of a periodic graph.
- `PeriodicGraph.mem_symmetries_iff` : a finite criterion on the bond data of one unit cell.
- `PeriodicGraph.exists_symmetry_of_equivariant` : every graph automorphism normalising the
  translations is such a symmetry.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The group of cell symmetries
- B. Translations form a normal subgroup
- C. Bond-preserving symmetries

## iv. References

* N. Ashcroft & N. D. Mermin, Solid State Physics, Chapter 7.

sections.text: ## A. The group of cell symmetries
## B. Translations form a normal subgroup

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry
declarations.doc:
A symmetry of the translation structure of a crystal with unit-cell labels `F` and cell
translations `G`: `(A, σ, b)` sends site `i` of cell `n` to site `σ i` of cell `A n + b i`.
declarations.statement:
structure CellSymmetry (G F : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] where
  /-- The action on cell indices. -/
  linear : G ≃+ G
  /-- The permutation of the labels within a unit cell. -/
  perm : Equiv.Perm F
  /-- The cell offset accompanying each label. -/
  shift : F → G
instance : Mul (CellSymmetry G F)
instance : One (CellSymmetry G F)
instance : Inv (CellSymmetry G F)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.linear_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma linear_mul (s t : CellSymmetry G F) (x : G) :
    (s * t).linear x = s.linear (t.linear x)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.perm_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma perm_mul (s t : CellSymmetry G F) (i : F) :
    (s * t).perm i = s.perm (t.perm i)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.shift_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma shift_mul (s t : CellSymmetry G F) (i : F) :
    (s * t).shift i = s.linear (t.shift i) + s.shift (t.perm i)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.linear_one
declarations.statement: lemma linear_one (x : G) : (1 : CellSymmetry G F).linear x = x

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.perm_one
declarations.statement: lemma perm_one (i : F) : (1 : CellSymmetry G F).perm i = i

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.shift_one
declarations.statement: lemma shift_one (i : F) : (1 : CellSymmetry G F).shift i = 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.linear_inv
declarations.statement: lemma linear_inv (s : CellSymmetry G F) (x : G) : (s⁻¹).linear x = s.linear.symm x

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.perm_inv
declarations.statement: lemma perm_inv (s : CellSymmetry G F) (i : F) : (s⁻¹).perm i = s.perm.symm i

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.shift_inv
declarations.statement:
lemma shift_inv (s : CellSymmetry G F) (j : F) :
    (s⁻¹).shift j = -s.linear.symm (s.shift (s.perm.symm j))
instance : Group (CellSymmetry G F)
instance : SMul (CellSymmetry G F) (CellSite G F)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.smul_def
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_def (s : CellSymmetry G F) (x : CellSite G F) :
    s • x = ⟨s.linear x.cell + s.shift x.label, s.perm x.label⟩

declarations.doc: The site `σ i` of cell `A n + b i` to which a symmetry sends the site `i` of cell `n`.
declarations.statement: instance : MulAction (CellSymmetry G F) (CellSite G F)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.translation
declarations.doc: Translation by `a`: it moves every cell by `a` and fixes the labels.
declarations.statement: def translation (a : G) : CellSymmetry G F

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.translation_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma translation_smul (a : G) (x : CellSite G F) :
    (translation a : CellSymmetry G F) • x = a +ᵥ x

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.translation_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma translation_mul (a b : G) :
    (translation a : CellSymmetry G F) * translation b = translation (a + b)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.mul_translation_mul_inv
declarations.doc: Conjugating a translation by a symmetry gives the translation by the transformed vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_translation_mul_inv (s : CellSymmetry G F) (a : G) :
    s * translation a * s⁻¹ = translation (s.linear a)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.translations
declarations.doc: The subgroup of translations.
declarations.statement: def translations (G F : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] : Subgroup (CellSymmetry G F)
instance : (translations G F).Normal

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.CellSymmetry.PointGroup
declarations.doc: The abstract point group of a crystal: cell symmetries modulo translations.
declarations.statement: abbrev PointGroup (G F : Type*) [AddCommGroup G]

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.Bonded
declarations.doc: Site `i` of the reference cell is bonded to site `j` of the cell `d`.
declarations.statement: def Bonded (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) (i j : F) (d : G) : Prop

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.adj_iff_bonded
declarations.doc: Bonds between any two cells are the translates of bonds to the reference cell.
declarations.statement:
lemma adj_iff_bonded (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) (n m : G) (i j : F) :
    g.toSimpleGraph.Adj ⟨n, i⟩ ⟨m, j⟩ ↔ g.Bonded i j (m - n)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.symmetries
declarations.doc: A symmetry preserves the bonds of the graph.
declarations.statement: def symmetries (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) : Subgroup (CellSymmetry G F)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_symmetries_iff
declarations.doc:
**A finite criterion for bond-preserving symmetries.** The data `(A, σ, b)` is a symmetry of
the crystal graph exactly when site `i` is bonded to site `j` in the cell `d` if and only if site
`σ i` is bonded to site `σ j` in the cell `A d + b j - b i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_symmetries_iff (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) (s : CellSymmetry G F) :
    s ∈ g.symmetries ↔ ∀ i j d, g.Bonded i j d ↔
      g.Bonded (s.perm i) (s.perm j) (s.linear d + s.shift j - s.shift i)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.symmetryIso
declarations.doc: A bond-preserving symmetry is an automorphism of the bond graph.
declarations.statement:
def symmetryIso (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) (s : g.symmetries) :
    g.toSimpleGraph ≃g g.toSimpleGraph

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.translation_mem_symmetries
declarations.doc: Translations are bond-preserving symmetries.
declarations.statement:
lemma translation_mem_symmetries (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F)) (a : G) :
    CellSymmetry.translation a ∈ g.symmetries

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.pointGroup
declarations.doc: The point group of a periodic graph: its bond-preserving symmetries modulo translations.
declarations.statement: abbrev pointGroup (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.exists_symmetry_of_equivariant
declarations.doc:
**Every automorphism of the bond graph that normalises the translations is a cell symmetry.**
If `φ` is a graph automorphism and `A` an automorphism of the translation group with
`φ (a +ᵥ x) = A a +ᵥ φ x`, then `φ` acts as a bond-preserving cell symmetry with linear part `A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_symmetry_of_equivariant (g : PeriodicGraph (Crystal.ofUnitCell G F))
    (φ : g.toSimpleGraph ≃g g.toSimpleGraph) (A : G ≃+ G)
    (hφ : ∀ (a : G) (x : CellSite G F), φ (a +ᵥ x) = A a +ᵥ φ x) :
    ∃ s ∈ g.symmetries, s.linear = A ∧ ∀ x, s • x = φ x

modules.title: Classical Ising interactions on a graph
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A classical Ising configuration assigns an up or down spin to every vertex of a graph.
Edges specify which spins interact. `IsingModel` adds a uniform exchange coupling `J`
and longitudinal field `h`, both in a fixed energy unit, to this connectivity.

The energy of a finite region is
`-J ∑ {x,y} σ(x) σ(y) - h ∑ x σ(x)`, where the first sum runs over its internal graph edges
and each spin has value ±1. We implement the edge sum as half the sum over ordered adjacent pairs:
symmetry counts each undirected edge twice and the simple graph excludes self-interactions.
Positive `J` favors alignment (ferromagnetism), negative `J` favors opposite spins,
and positive `h` favors up spins.

Joining disjoint regions changes their combined energy only through bonds connecting the
regions. Each crossing bond contributes at most `|J|` in absolute value. If sites have at
most `q` neighbors, the absolute energy is bounded by `(|J| q / 2 + |h|) |Λ|`. These bounds
control boundary corrections and energy growth with volume.

For ferromagnetic exchange `J ≥ 0`, uniform polarization aligned with the field attains
the least energy on every finite region. Its energy per site converges whenever the
average internal coordination converges. These results apply to arbitrary graphs;
crystal translations supply an additional symmetry.

## ii. Key results

- `IsingModel` : the nearest-neighbour Ising model on a graph, with uniform coupling and field.
- `IsingModel.energy` : the energy of a finite region.
- `IsingModel.abs_energy_union_sub_le` : the failure of additivity is bounded by the crossing bonds.
- `IsingModel.abs_energy_le_of_degree_le` : the energy grows at most linearly with the volume.
- `IsingModel.groundEnergy_eq` : the ferromagnetic ground-state energy of a region.
- `IsingModel.tendsto_groundEnergyDensity` : the ground-state energy density converges when the
  average internal coordination does.
- `IsingModel.energy_translate` : the energy is invariant under crystal translations.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Spin configurations
- B. Finite-region energy and locality
- C. Boundary interactions
- D. Energy growth with volume
- E. Ferromagnetic ground states
- F. Ground-state energy per site
- G. Crystal translation symmetry

## iv. References

* E. Ising, Beitrag zur Theorie des Ferromagnetismus.

sections.text:
## C. Boundary interactions

Combining disjoint regions adds precisely the exchange interactions across their common
boundary. The number of crossing bonds bounds this correction independently of the spin
configuration.

## D. Energy growth with volume

A bounded coordination number ensures that the energy of every spin configuration grows
at most linearly with the number of sites. The bound holds for either sign of exchange
coupling and field.

## E. Ferromagnetic ground states

For nonnegative exchange coupling, uniform polarization simultaneously minimizes every
bond interaction. Alignment with the field also minimizes every one-site contribution.
The minimum energy therefore depends only on the internal connections and the volume.

## F. Ground-state energy per site

The average internal coordination counts neighbors that remain in the region, averaged
over its sites. If this average converges along nonempty regions, the ferromagnetic
minimum energy per site converges with it. No regular degree, periodicity or prescribed
shape of region is required.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel
declarations.doc: A classical nearest-neighbor Ising model on the specified undirected graph.
declarations.statement:
structure IsingModel {X : Type*} (graph : SimpleGraph X) where
  /-- Uniform exchange coupling; positive values favor aligned spins. -/
  J : ℝ
  /-- Uniform longitudinal field; positive values favor up spins. -/
  h : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Configuration
declarations.doc: Up or down spins at every site of the crystal.
declarations.statement: abbrev Configuration (_I : IsingModel g)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.spin
declarations.doc: The dimensionless spin value, with `true` denoting up.
declarations.statement: def spin (b : Bool) : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.abs_spin
declarations.doc: Every Ising spin has unit magnitude.
declarations.statement: lemma abs_spin (b : Bool) : |spin b| = 1

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.pairSpin
declarations.doc: The exchange contribution of an ordered pair; nonadjacent sites contribute zero.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def pairSpin (I : IsingModel g) (σ : I.Configuration) (x y : X) : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.energy
declarations.doc:
Energy of the spins and internal edges of a finite region. The factor `1/2` counts each
undirected graph edge once. Spins outside the region do not contribute.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def energy (I : IsingModel g) (Λ : Finset X)
    (σ : I.Configuration) : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.energy_congr
declarations.doc: A region's energy depends only on the spin configuration inside that region.
declarations.statement:
lemma energy_congr (I : IsingModel g) (Λ : Finset X) {σ τ : I.Configuration}
    (hστ : ∀ x ∈ Λ, σ x = τ x) : I.energy Λ σ = I.energy Λ τ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.pairSpin_comm
declarations.doc: The exchange contribution is symmetric in the endpoints of a bond.
declarations.statement:
lemma pairSpin_comm (I : IsingModel g) (σ : I.Configuration) (x y : X) :
    I.pairSpin σ x y = I.pairSpin σ y x

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.energy_union
declarations.doc: Joining disjoint regions adds exactly their crossing exchange interactions.
declarations.statement:
lemma energy_union [DecidableEq X] (I : IsingModel g) (Λ M : Finset X)
    (hΛM : Disjoint Λ M) (σ : I.Configuration) :
    I.energy (Λ ∪ M) σ = I.energy Λ σ + I.energy M σ -
      I.J * ∑ x ∈ Λ, ∑ y ∈ M, I.pairSpin σ x y

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.abs_pairSpin
declarations.doc: An ordered bond contributes at most one in absolute spin units.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_pairSpin (I : IsingModel g) (σ : I.Configuration) (x y : X) :
    |I.pairSpin σ x y| = if g.Adj x y then 1 else 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.abs_sum_pairSpin_le
declarations.doc: The total exchange spin sum is bounded by the number of connections between the regions.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_sum_pairSpin_le (I : IsingModel g) (Λ M : Finset X)
    (σ : I.Configuration) :
    |∑ x ∈ Λ, ∑ y ∈ M, I.pairSpin σ x y| ≤ g.bondCountBetween Λ M

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.abs_energy_union_sub_le
declarations.doc: Failure of energy additivity is controlled solely by the bonds crossing the boundary.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_energy_union_sub_le [DecidableEq X] (I : IsingModel g)
    (Λ M : Finset X) (hΛM : Disjoint Λ M) (σ : I.Configuration) :
    |I.energy (Λ ∪ M) σ - I.energy Λ σ - I.energy M σ| ≤
      |I.J| * g.bondCountBetween Λ M

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.abs_energy_le
declarations.doc: The absolute energy is bounded by the internal bond count and the number of spins.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_energy_le (I : IsingModel g) (Λ : Finset X) (σ : I.Configuration) :
    |I.energy Λ σ| ≤ |I.J| / 2 * g.bondCountBetween Λ Λ + |I.h| * Λ.card

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.abs_energy_le_of_degree_le
declarations.doc: A coordination bound gives a uniform energy bound proportional to the region's volume.
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_energy_le_of_degree_le [g.LocallyFinite] (I : IsingModel g) (Λ : Finset X)
    (σ : I.Configuration) (q : ℕ) (hq : ∀ x ∈ Λ, (g.neighborFinset x).card ≤ q) :
    |I.energy Λ σ| ≤ (|I.J| * q / 2 + |I.h|) * Λ.card

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.IsGroundState
declarations.doc:
A configuration minimizing the energy of the finite region `Λ`.
Only interactions internal to the region enter this definition.
declarations.statement: def IsGroundState (I : IsingModel g) (Λ : Finset X) (σ : I.Configuration) : Prop

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.polarized
declarations.doc: Uniform spins aligned with the field; at zero field the up orientation is chosen.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def polarized (I : IsingModel g) : I.Configuration

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.groundEnergy
declarations.doc: The least finite-region energy over all spin configurations.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def groundEnergy (I : IsingModel g) (Λ : Finset X) : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.groundEnergy_eq_of_isGroundState
declarations.doc: An energy-minimizing configuration attains the least energy.
declarations.statement:
lemma groundEnergy_eq_of_isGroundState (I : IsingModel g) (Λ : Finset X)
    {σ : I.Configuration} (hσ : I.IsGroundState Λ σ) :
    I.groundEnergy Λ = I.energy Λ σ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.energy_polarized
declarations.doc: Uniform field-aligned polarization has saturated exchange and field contributions.
declarations.statement:
lemma energy_polarized (I : IsingModel g) (Λ : Finset X) :
    I.energy Λ I.polarized =
      -(I.J / 2) * g.bondCountBetween Λ Λ - |I.h| * Λ.card

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.energy_lower_bound
declarations.doc: Ferromagnetic energies cannot lie below the saturated exchange and field contributions.
declarations.statement:
lemma energy_lower_bound (I : IsingModel g) (hJ : 0 ≤ I.J) (Λ : Finset X)
    (σ : I.Configuration) :
    -(I.J / 2) * g.bondCountBetween Λ Λ - |I.h| * Λ.card ≤ I.energy Λ σ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.isGroundState_polarized
declarations.doc: Uniform field-aligned polarization is a ground state on every finite ferromagnetic region.
declarations.statement:
lemma isGroundState_polarized (I : IsingModel g) (hJ : 0 ≤ I.J) (Λ : Finset X) :
    I.IsGroundState Λ I.polarized

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.groundEnergy_eq
declarations.doc: The exact ferromagnetic minimum counts internal bonds and field-aligned spins.
declarations.statement:
lemma groundEnergy_eq (I : IsingModel g) (hJ : 0 ≤ I.J) (Λ : Finset X) :
    I.groundEnergy Λ = -(I.J / 2) * g.bondCountBetween Λ Λ - |I.h| * Λ.card

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.groundEnergyDensity
declarations.doc: The minimum finite-region energy divided by the number of sites.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def groundEnergyDensity (I : IsingModel g) (Λ : Finset X) : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.groundEnergyDensity_eq
declarations.doc: The ferromagnetic minimum per site is determined by average internal coordination.
declarations.statement:
lemma groundEnergyDensity_eq (I : IsingModel g) (hJ : 0 ≤ I.J) (Λ : Finset X)
    (hΛ : Λ.Nonempty) :
    I.groundEnergyDensity Λ =
      -(I.J / 2) * ((g.bondCountBetween Λ Λ : ℝ) / Λ.card) - |I.h|

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.tendsto_groundEnergyDensity
declarations.doc:
Convergent average internal coordination gives a ferromagnetic ground-state energy density.
The statement applies to any sequence of nonempty finite regions on any graph.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_groundEnergyDensity (I : IsingModel g) (hJ : 0 ≤ I.J)
    (Λ : ℕ → Finset X) (hΛ : ∀ n, (Λ n).Nonempty) (z : ℝ)
    (hz : Filter.Tendsto
      (fun n => (g.bondCountBetween (Λ n) (Λ n) : ℝ) / (Λ n).card)
      Filter.atTop (nhds z)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => I.groundEnergyDensity (Λ n))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (-(I.J / 2) * z - |I.h|))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.translate
declarations.doc: Transport a configuration along a crystal translation.
declarations.statement: def translate (I : IsingModel g.toSimpleGraph) (a : G) (σ : I.Configuration) : I.Configuration

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.translate_apply
declarations.doc: A transported spin has the same value at the transported site.
declarations.statement:
lemma translate_apply (I : IsingModel g.toSimpleGraph) (a : G)
    (σ : I.Configuration) (x : C.Site) : I.translate a σ (a +ᵥ x) = σ x

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.translateRegion
declarations.doc: Translate a finite region by the existing bijective action on crystal sites.
declarations.statement: def translateRegion (a : G) (Λ : Finset C.Site) : Finset C.Site

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.pairSpin_translate
declarations.doc: Exchange contributions are unchanged by translating both spins and sites.
declarations.statement:
lemma pairSpin_translate (I : IsingModel g.toSimpleGraph) (a : G) (σ : I.Configuration)
    (x y : C.Site) :
    I.pairSpin (I.translate a σ) (a +ᵥ x) (a +ᵥ y) = I.pairSpin σ x y

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.energy_translate
declarations.doc:
Uniform Ising interactions inherit the crystal's translation symmetry. Translating the
region as well as its configuration preserves its energy.
declarations.statement:
lemma energy_translate (I : IsingModel g.toSimpleGraph) (a : G)
    (Λ : Finset C.Site) (σ : I.Configuration) :
    I.energy (translateRegion a Λ) (I.translate a σ) = I.energy Λ σ

modules.title: Classical Ising models on standard crystals
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Uniform exchange and field parameters turn the existing crystal bond graphs into classical
Ising models. The hypercubic model works in arbitrary dimension; the square lattice is its
two-dimensional specialization. Honeycomb uses the same energy definition with its three
bonds per site. Geometry plays no role in either construction.

The main result concerns the ferromagnetic ground state of any crystal in `d` dimensions,
with any number of sites per unit cell. Take a hypercube of `n + 1` unit cells along each
lattice vector. Spins near its surface miss some of their neighbors, but they form a vanishing
fraction of the sample as it grows. The ground-state energy per spin therefore converges to
`-(J / 2) z̄ - |h|`, where `z̄` is the mean coordination of one unit cell: every spin
contributes `-J` for half of its `z̄` bonds, and the aligned field contributes `-|h|`.
The square lattice (`z̄ = 4`) and the honeycomb lattice (`z̄ = 3`) are instances.

## ii. Key results

- `IsingModel.hypercubic`, `IsingModel.square`, `IsingModel.honeycomb` : uniform Ising models on
  the standard bond graphs.
- `IsingModel.Hypercube.tendsto_averageCoordination` : surface spins form a vanishing fraction of a
  growing hypercube of cells.
- `IsingModel.tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_hypercube` : the ferromagnetic ground-state energy per
  spin of any crystal converges to `-(J / 2) z̄ - |h|`.
- `IsingModel.tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_square`, `..._honeycomb` : the square and honeycomb
  lattices.
- `IsingModel.tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_of_card` : the density for a crystal in which every
  site has `q` neighbours, with the diamond, fcc, bcc and hcp lattices as instances.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Ising models on the standard crystals
- B. Hypercubes of unit cells in an arbitrary crystal
- C. Ground-state energy density of a ferromagnetic crystal
- D. Regular crystals

## iv. References

* E. Ising, Beitrag zur Theorie des Ferromagnetismus.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.hypercubic
declarations.doc: Uniform classical Ising interactions on the hypercubic bond graph in arbitrary dimension.
declarations.statement: def hypercubic (d : ℕ) (J h : ℝ) : IsingModel (Crystal.hypercubicGraph d).toSimpleGraph

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.square
declarations.doc: The square-lattice model, specializing the hypercubic construction to two dimensions.
declarations.statement: def square (J h : ℝ) : IsingModel Crystal.squareGraph.toSimpleGraph

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.honeycomb
declarations.doc: The honeycomb classical Ising model, using the crystal's existing bonds.
declarations.statement: def honeycomb (J h : ℝ) : IsingModel Crystal.honeycombGraph.toSimpleGraph

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.cells
declarations.doc: The cells `{0, …, n}^d` of a hypercube of side `n + 1` unit cells.
declarations.statement: def cells (d n : ℕ) : Finset (Fin d → ℤ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.mem_cells
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_cells {d n : ℕ} (c : Fin d → ℤ) :
    c ∈ cells d n ↔ ∀ i, 0 ≤ c i ∧ c i ≤ n

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.card_cells
declarations.statement: lemma card_cells (d n : ℕ) : (cells d n).card = (n + 1) ^ d

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.interior
declarations.doc: The cells at least `R` unit cells away from every face of the hypercube.
declarations.statement: def interior (d n R : ℕ) : Finset (Fin d → ℤ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.mem_interior
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_interior {d n R : ℕ} (c : Fin d → ℤ) :
    c ∈ interior d n R ↔ ∀ i, (R : ℤ) ≤ c i ∧ c i ≤ n - R

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.card_interior
declarations.doc: The interior of a hypercube of side `n + 1` is a hypercube of side `n + 1 - 2 R`.
declarations.statement: lemma card_interior (d n R : ℕ) : (interior d n R).card = (n + 1 - 2 * R) ^ d

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.interior_subset
declarations.statement: lemma interior_subset {d n R : ℕ} : interior d n R ⊆ cells d n

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.region
declarations.doc: All sites of the crystal with unit cell labels `F` that lie in the cells `B`.
declarations.statement: def region (B : Finset (Fin d → ℤ)) : Finset (Crystal.ofUnitCell (Fin d → ℤ) F).Site

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.mem_region
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_region {B : Finset (Fin d → ℤ)} (x : (Crystal.ofUnitCell (Fin d → ℤ) F).Site) :
    x ∈ region B ↔ x.cell ∈ B

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.sum_region
CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.card_region
declarations.statement:
lemma card_region (B : Finset (Fin d → ℤ)) :
    (region (F := F) B).card = B.card * Fintype.card F

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.region_cells_nonempty
declarations.doc: Every hypercube contains at least one site if the unit cell does.
declarations.statement:
lemma region_cells_nonempty [Nonempty F] (d n : ℕ) :
    (region (F := F) (cells d n)).Nonempty

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.exists_range
declarations.doc:
Bonds have a finite range: there is a distance `R`, in units of the cell spacing, beyond
which no two sites are connected. This holds because the coordination is finite and every
site is a translate of one of finitely many reference sites.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_range :
    ∃ R : ℕ, ∀ x y : (Crystal.ofUnitCell (Fin d → ℤ) F).Site,
      g.toSimpleGraph.Adj x y → ∀ k, |y.cell k - x.cell k| ≤ R

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.neighbors_subset_region
declarations.doc:
Sites in the interior of a hypercube have all their neighbors in the sample, once
the interior is at least the bond range away from the surface.
declarations.statement:
lemma neighbors_subset_region {n R : ℕ}
    (hR : ∀ x y : (Crystal.ofUnitCell (Fin d → ℤ) F).Site,
      g.toSimpleGraph.Adj x y → ∀ k, |y.cell k - x.cell k| ≤ R)
    {x : (Crystal.ofUnitCell (Fin d → ℤ) F).Site} (hx : x.cell ∈ interior d n R) :
    g.neighbors x ⊆ region (cells d n)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.meanCoordination
declarations.doc:
The mean number of neighbors per site of a crystal with unit cell `F`: the coordination
averaged over the sites of one unit cell.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def meanCoordination : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.sum_card_neighbors_region
declarations.doc:
Summing the coordination over the sites of a set of cells counts every unit-cell
coordination once per cell.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_card_neighbors_region (B : Finset (Fin d → ℤ)) :
    ∑ x ∈ region B, (g.neighbors x).card =
      B.card * ∑ i : F, (g.neighbors ⟨0, i⟩).card

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.bondCountBetween_le
declarations.doc: The ordered bonds inside a region number at most the total coordination of its sites.
declarations.statement:
lemma bondCountBetween_le (Λ : Finset (Crystal.ofUnitCell (Fin d → ℤ) F).Site) :
    g.toSimpleGraph.bondCountBetween Λ Λ ≤ ∑ x ∈ Λ, (g.neighbors x).card

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.sum_interior_le_bondCountBetween
declarations.doc: Every site in the interior of the hypercube has all its bonds inside the hypercube.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_interior_le_bondCountBetween {n R : ℕ}
    (hR : ∀ x y : (Crystal.ofUnitCell (Fin d → ℤ) F).Site,
      g.toSimpleGraph.Adj x y → ∀ k, |y.cell k - x.cell k| ≤ R) :
    ∑ x ∈ region (F := F) (interior d n R), (g.neighbors x).card ≤
      g.toSimpleGraph.bondCountBetween (region (cells d n)) (region (cells d n))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.Hypercube.tendsto_averageCoordination
declarations.doc:
The average coordination of hypercubes converges to the mean coordination of the
crystal: the sites near the surface, whose neighbors are cut off, become a vanishing fraction
of the sample.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_averageCoordination :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ => (g.toSimpleGraph.bondCountBetween (region (cells d n))
        (region (cells d n)) : ℝ) / (region (F := F) (cells d n)).card)
      Filter.atTop (nhds (meanCoordination g))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_hypercube
declarations.doc:
The ground-state energy per spin of a ferromagnetic Ising model on any crystal, in
hypercubes of growing size, converges to `-(J / 2) z̄ - |h|`, where `z̄` is the mean
coordination. Each spin carries the energy `-J` for half of its bonds; the missing bonds
at the surface of the sample do not contribute in the limit. The field may have either
sign, and the lattice may have several sites per unit cell.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_hypercube (I : IsingModel g.toSimpleGraph) (hJ : 0 ≤ I.J) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => I.groundEnergyDensity (region (cells d n)))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (-(I.J / 2) * meanCoordination g - |I.h|))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.meanCoordination_honeycomb
declarations.doc: The honeycomb lattice has three neighbors per site.
declarations.statement: lemma meanCoordination_honeycomb : Hypercube.meanCoordination Crystal.honeycombGraph = 3

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_honeycomb
declarations.doc:
The ground-state energy per spin of the ferromagnetic honeycomb Ising model converges to
`-3 J / 2 - |h|` as the sample grows.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_honeycomb (J h : ℝ) (hJ : 0 ≤ J) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (honeycomb J h).groundEnergyDensity
        (Hypercube.region (Hypercube.cells 2 n)))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (-(3 * J / 2) - |h|))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.meanCoordination_square
declarations.doc: The square lattice has four neighbors per site.
declarations.statement: lemma meanCoordination_square : Hypercube.meanCoordination Crystal.squareGraph = 4

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_square
declarations.doc:
The ground-state energy per spin of the ferromagnetic square-lattice Ising model
converges to `-2 J - |h|` as the sample grows.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_square (J h : ℝ) (hJ : 0 ≤ J) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (square J h).groundEnergyDensity
        (Hypercube.region (Hypercube.cells 2 n)))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (-(2 * J) - |h|))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.meanCoordination_of_card
declarations.doc: If every site has `q` neighbors, the mean coordination is `q`.
declarations.statement:
lemma meanCoordination_of_card {q : ℕ} (h : ∀ x, (g.neighbors x).card = q) :
    Hypercube.meanCoordination g = q

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_of_card
declarations.doc:
**The ferromagnetic ground-state energy density of a `q`-regular crystal** converges to
`-q J / 2 - |h|`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_of_card {q : ℕ} (h : ∀ x, (g.neighbors x).card = q)
    (I : IsingModel g.toSimpleGraph) (hJ : 0 ≤ I.J) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => I.groundEnergyDensity (Hypercube.region (Hypercube.cells d n)))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (-(q * I.J / 2) - |I.h|))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_diamond
declarations.doc: The diamond lattice has four neighbors per site.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_diamond (J h : ℝ) (hJ : 0 ≤ J) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (⟨J, h⟩ : IsingModel Crystal.diamondGraph.toSimpleGraph
        ).groundEnergyDensity (Hypercube.region (Hypercube.cells 3 n)))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (-(4 * J / 2) - |h|))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_fcc
declarations.doc: The face-centred cubic lattice has twelve neighbors per site.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_fcc (J h : ℝ) (hJ : 0 ≤ J) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (⟨J, h⟩ : IsingModel Crystal.fccGraph.toSimpleGraph
        ).groundEnergyDensity (Hypercube.region (Hypercube.cells 3 n)))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (-(12 * J / 2) - |h|))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_bcc
declarations.doc: The body-centred cubic lattice has eight neighbors per site.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_bcc (J h : ℝ) (hJ : 0 ≤ J) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (⟨J, h⟩ : IsingModel Crystal.bccGraph.toSimpleGraph
        ).groundEnergyDensity (Hypercube.region (Hypercube.cells 3 n)))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (-(8 * J / 2) - |h|))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.IsingModel.tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_hcp
declarations.doc: The hexagonal close-packed crystal has twelve neighbors per site.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_groundEnergyDensity_hcp (J h : ℝ) (hJ : 0 ≤ J) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (⟨J, h⟩ : IsingModel Crystal.hcpGraph.toSimpleGraph
        ).groundEnergyDensity (Hypercube.region (Hypercube.cells 3 n)))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (-(12 * J / 2) - |h|))

modules.title: Gibbs weights and states of a finite-dimensional system
modules.doc:
The Gibbs state of a Hermitian energy operator, and the canonical and grand canonical ensembles.

## i. Overview

For a Hermitian matrix `h`, thought of as `β` times an energy, the *Gibbs weight* is `e^{-h}`,
and the *Gibbs state* is `a ↦ tr(e^{-h} a) / tr(e^{-h})`. It is a state of the matrix algebra: it
is normalized, Hermitian, and positive, because the weight is the square `r²` of the Hermitian
matrix `r = e^{-h/2}`, so that `tr(r² a* a) = tr((a r)* (a r)) ≥ 0`, and the partition function
`tr(r²)` is positive.

Every ensemble is a special case.

* The *canonical ensemble* at inverse temperature `β` for a Hamiltonian `H` has `h = β H`.
* The *grand canonical ensemble* at inverse temperature `β` and chemical potential `μ`, for a
  Hamiltonian `H` and a charge `N` such as the particle number, has `h = β (H - μ N)`.
  When the charge is conserved, `H` and `N` commute and the weight factorizes as
  `e^{-βH} e^{βμN}`: the canonical weight times a fugacity `e^{βμ}` per unit charge.

No structure of the system enters, so the same definitions serve a finite region of any lattice,
quantum or classical. A classical system is the case of diagonal matrices, where the Gibbs weight
is the Boltzmann factor `e^{-E(c)}` of each configuration `c`.

## ii. Key results

- `gibbsWeight` : the weight `e^{-h}`.
- `gibbsState` : the Gibbs state of a Hermitian operator, as a state of the matrix algebra.
- `canonicalState` : the canonical ensemble.
- `grandCanonicalState` : the grand canonical ensemble.
- `grandCanonicalWeight_of_commute` : factorization for a conserved charge.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Gibbs weight
- B. The Gibbs state
- C. The canonical and grand canonical ensembles
- D. Classical systems

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 2,
  Section 5.3.

sections.text: ## C. The canonical and grand canonical ensembles

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.gibbsWeight
declarations.doc: The Gibbs weight `e^{-h}` of an energy operator `h`.
declarations.statement: def gibbsWeight (h : Matrix n n ℂ) : Matrix n n ℂ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.gibbsRoot
declarations.doc: The square root `e^{-h/2}` of the Gibbs weight.
declarations.statement: def gibbsRoot (h : Matrix n n ℂ) : Matrix n n ℂ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.gibbsWeight_eq_root_mul
declarations.statement: lemma gibbsWeight_eq_root_mul (h : Matrix n n ℂ) : gibbsWeight h = gibbsRoot h * gibbsRoot h

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.gibbsRoot_isHermitian
declarations.statement:
lemma gibbsRoot_isHermitian {h : Matrix n n ℂ} (hh : h.IsHermitian) :
    (gibbsRoot h).IsHermitian

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.gibbsWeight_isHermitian
declarations.statement:
lemma gibbsWeight_isHermitian {h : Matrix n n ℂ} (hh : h.IsHermitian) :
    (gibbsWeight h).IsHermitian

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.partition
declarations.doc: The **partition function** `tr e^{-h}`.
declarations.statement: def partition (h : Matrix n n ℂ) : ℂ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.partition_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma partition_eq (h : Matrix n n ℂ) (hh : h.IsHermitian) :
    partition h = ((gibbsRoot h)ᴴ * gibbsRoot h).trace

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.gibbsRoot_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma gibbsRoot_ne_zero [Nonempty n] (h : Matrix n n ℂ) : gibbsRoot h ≠ 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.partition_pos
declarations.doc: **The partition function of a Hermitian operator is positive.**
declarations.statement: lemma partition_pos [Nonempty n] {h : Matrix n n ℂ} (hh : h.IsHermitian) : 0 < partition h

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.partition_ne_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma partition_ne_zero [Nonempty n] {h : Matrix n n ℂ} (hh : h.IsHermitian) :
    partition h ≠ 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.gibbsFunctional
declarations.doc: The Gibbs functional `a ↦ tr(e^{-h} a) / tr(e^{-h})`.
declarations.statement: def gibbsFunctional (h : Matrix n n ℂ) : Matrix n n ℂ →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.gibbsFunctional_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma gibbsFunctional_apply (h a : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    gibbsFunctional h a = (partition h)⁻¹ * (gibbsWeight h * a).trace

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.inv_partition_nonneg
declarations.doc: The inverse of the partition function is a nonnegative real number.
declarations.statement:
lemma inv_partition_nonneg [Nonempty n] {h : Matrix n n ℂ} (hh : h.IsHermitian) :
    0 ≤ (partition h)⁻¹

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.gibbsState
declarations.doc:
**The Gibbs state of a Hermitian operator** is a state of the matrix algebra: normalized,
Hermitian and positive.
declarations.statement: def gibbsState [Nonempty n] (h : Matrix n n ℂ) (hh : h.IsHermitian) : AlgState (Matrix n n ℂ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.canonicalState
declarations.doc: **The canonical ensemble** at inverse temperature `β` for a Hamiltonian `H`.
declarations.statement:
def canonicalState [Nonempty n] (β : ℝ) (H : Matrix n n ℂ) (hH : H.IsHermitian) :
    AlgState (Matrix n n ℂ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.grandCanonicalOp
declarations.doc: The operator whose Gibbs weight is the grand canonical weight: `β (H - μ N)`.
declarations.statement: def grandCanonicalOp (β μ : ℝ) (H N : Matrix n n ℂ) : Matrix n n ℂ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.grandCanonicalOp_isHermitian
declarations.statement:
lemma grandCanonicalOp_isHermitian {H N : Matrix n n ℂ} (hH : H.IsHermitian) (hN : N.IsHermitian)
    (β μ : ℝ) : (grandCanonicalOp β μ H N).IsHermitian

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.grandCanonicalState
declarations.doc:
**The grand canonical ensemble** at inverse temperature `β` and chemical potential `μ`, for a
Hamiltonian `H` and a charge `N`.
declarations.statement:
def grandCanonicalState [Nonempty n] (β μ : ℝ) (H N : Matrix n n ℂ) (hH : H.IsHermitian)
    (hN : N.IsHermitian) : AlgState (Matrix n n ℂ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.grandCanonicalOp_zero
declarations.doc: At zero chemical potential the grand canonical ensemble is the canonical one.
declarations.statement:
lemma grandCanonicalOp_zero (β : ℝ) (H N : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    grandCanonicalOp β 0 H N = (β : ℂ) • H

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.grandCanonicalWeight_of_commute
declarations.doc:
**Factorization for a conserved charge**: if `H` and `N` commute, the grand canonical weight is
the canonical weight times the fugacity factor `e^{βμ N}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma grandCanonicalWeight_of_commute (β μ : ℝ) {H N : Matrix n n ℂ} (hc : Commute H N) :
    gibbsWeight (grandCanonicalOp β μ H N) =
      gibbsWeight ((β : ℂ) • H) * NormedSpace.exp (((β * μ : ℝ) : ℂ) • N)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.gibbsWeight_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**For a diagonal energy operator the Gibbs weight is the Boltzmann factor** `e^{-E(c)}` of each
configuration `c`: the classical Gibbs distribution.
declarations.statement:
lemma gibbsWeight_diagonal (v : n → ℂ) :
    gibbsWeight (Matrix.diagonal v) = Matrix.diagonal fun c => Complex.exp (-v c)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.partition_diagonal
declarations.doc: The partition function of a diagonal energy operator is the sum of the Boltzmann factors.
declarations.statement: lemma partition_diagonal (v : n → ℂ) : partition (Matrix.diagonal v) = ∑ c, Complex.exp (-v c)

modules.title: Covariance of the finite-volume ensembles under site symmetries
modules.doc:
A symmetry of an interaction carries the Hamiltonian and the ensembles of a box to those of the
moved box.

## i. Overview

Let a group `Γ` act on the sites, all of which carry the same finite configuration space. An
interaction is *invariant* if moving a term moves the term of the moved region:
`quantumIso γ X (Φ X) = Φ (γ • X)`. Then the Hamiltonian of a box `Λ` is carried to the Hamiltonian
of `γ • Λ`, because moving commutes with lifting and with the sum over the regions inside the box.
Moving is a `*`-isomorphism preserving the trace, so it commutes with the exponential and carries
the Gibbs weight to the Gibbs weight and the Gibbs state to the Gibbs state: the expectation of the
moved observable in the ensemble of the moved box equals the expectation in the ensemble of the box.

## ii. Key results

- `quantumIso_exp` : moving commutes with the exponential.
- `Interaction.hamiltonian_smul` : the Hamiltonian of a moved box.
- `Interaction.canonicalState_smul`, `Interaction.grandCanonicalState_smul` : covariance of the
  canonical and grand canonical ensembles.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Moving the Gibbs weight
- B. Moving the Hamiltonian
- C. Moving the ensembles

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.quantumIso_exp
declarations.doc: Moving commutes with the exponential.
declarations.statement:
lemma quantumIso_exp (γ : Γ) (X : Finset S) (a : Alg (fun _ : S => Ω₀) X) :
    quantumIso γ X (NormedSpace.exp a) = NormedSpace.exp (quantumIso γ X a)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.quantumIso_trace
declarations.doc: Moving preserves the trace.
declarations.statement:
lemma quantumIso_trace (γ : Γ) (X : Finset S) (a : Alg (fun _ : S => Ω₀) X) :
    (quantumIso γ X a).trace = a.trace

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.quantumIso_gibbsWeight
declarations.statement:
lemma quantumIso_gibbsWeight (γ : Γ) (X : Finset S) (a : Alg (fun _ : S => Ω₀) X) :
    quantumIso γ X (gibbsWeight a) = gibbsWeight (quantumIso γ X a)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.quantumIso_partition
declarations.statement:
lemma quantumIso_partition (γ : Γ) (X : Finset S) (a : Alg (fun _ : S => Ω₀) X) :
    partition (quantumIso γ X a) = partition a

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.gibbsFunctional_quantumIso
declarations.doc: **The Gibbs functional is covariant.**
declarations.statement:
lemma gibbsFunctional_quantumIso (γ : Γ) (X : Finset S) (h b : Alg (fun _ : S => Ω₀) X) :
    gibbsFunctional (quantumIso γ X h) (quantumIso γ X b) = gibbsFunctional h b

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.IsInvariant
declarations.doc: An interaction is *invariant* under `γ` if moving a term gives the term of the moved region.
declarations.statement: def Interaction.IsInvariant (I : Interaction (fun _ : S => Ω₀)) (γ : Γ) : Prop

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.powersetSmul
declarations.doc: The bijection between the regions of a box and the regions of the moved box.
declarations.statement: def powersetSmul (γ : Γ) (Λ : Finset S) : Λ.powerset ≃ (γ • Λ).powerset

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.hamiltonian_smul
declarations.doc:
**The Hamiltonian of a moved box**: for an invariant interaction, moving the Hamiltonian of a
box gives the Hamiltonian of the moved box.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.canonicalState_smul
declarations.doc:
**The canonical ensemble is covariant**: the expectation of a moved observable in the
ensemble of the moved box is the expectation of the observable in the ensemble of the box.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.siteSmul
declarations.doc: The bijection between the sites of a box and the sites of the moved box.
declarations.statement: def siteSmul (γ : Γ) (Λ : Finset S) : ↥Λ ≃ ↥(γ • Λ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.chargeOp_smul
declarations.doc: **A uniform charge is moved to the uniform charge of the moved box.**
declarations.statement:
lemma chargeOp_smul (q₀ : Ω₀ → ℝ) (γ : Γ) (Λ : Finset S) :
    quantumIso γ Λ (chargeOp (fun _ : S => q₀) Λ) = chargeOp (fun _ : S => q₀) (γ • Λ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.grandCanonicalOp_quantumIso
declarations.doc:
The charge of a moved box, as a statement about the operator whose weight is the grand
canonical one.
declarations.statement:
lemma grandCanonicalOp_quantumIso (γ : Γ) (Λ : Finset S) (β μ : ℝ) (H N : Alg (fun _ : S => Ω₀) Λ) :
    quantumIso γ Λ (grandCanonicalOp β μ H N) =
      grandCanonicalOp β μ (quantumIso γ Λ H) (quantumIso γ Λ N)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.grandCanonicalState_smul
declarations.doc:
**The grand canonical ensemble is covariant**, for an invariant interaction and a uniform
charge.
declarations.statement:
lemma Interaction.grandCanonicalState_smul (I : Interaction (fun _ : S => Ω₀)) {γ : Γ}
    (hI : I.IsInvariant γ) (q₀ : Ω₀ → ℝ) (β μ : ℝ) (Λ : Finset S)
    (a : Alg (fun _ : S => Ω₀) Λ) :
    I.grandCanonicalState (fun _ : S => q₀) β μ (γ • Λ) (quantumIso γ Λ a) =
      I.grandCanonicalState (fun _ : S => q₀) β μ Λ a

modules.title: The quantum and classical nets of a system with finite site spaces
modules.doc:
The two nets of algebras over a set of sites with finite configuration spaces: operators and
functions.

## i. Overview

For sites `s` carrying finite sets `Ω s`, the quantum net assigns to a region the matrices on its
configurations, with the inclusions `M ↦ M ⊗ 1`. The classical net assigns to a region the complex
functions on its configurations, which are the diagonal operators, with the inclusions
`f ↦ f ∘ restr`: a function of the values in `X` is a function of the values in `Y ⊇ X`. Both
satisfy the axioms of a net, and the classical net sits in the quantum net as diagonal matrices.
Both have a quasi-local algebra by the construction on any net.

The inclusions are injective as soon as every site space is nonempty.

## ii. Key results

- `quantumNet` : the net of operators.
- `classicalNet` : the net of functions of configurations.
- `diagonalInclusion` : the classical algebra of a region as diagonal operators.
- `diagonalInclusion_incl` : the classical net is a subnet of the quantum net.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The quantum net
- B. The classical net

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 2,
  Section 6.1.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.quantumNet
declarations.doc:
**The quantum net**: the matrices on the configurations of each region, with `M ↦ M ⊗ 1` as
inclusion.
declarations.statement: def quantumNet : AlgebraNet S

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.CAlg
declarations.doc: The classical algebra of a region: the complex functions on its configurations.
declarations.statement: abbrev CAlg (X : Finset S) : Type _

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.classicalIncl
declarations.doc: A function of the values in `X` is a function of the values in a larger region `Y`.
declarations.statement: def classicalIncl {X Y : Finset S} (h : X ≤ Y) : CAlg Ω X →⋆ₐ[ℂ] CAlg Ω Y

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.classicalNet
declarations.doc: **The classical net**: the functions on the configurations of each region.
declarations.statement: def classicalNet : AlgebraNet S

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.diagonalInclusion
declarations.doc: The classical algebra of a region as the diagonal operators.
declarations.statement: def diagonalInclusion (X : Finset S) : CAlg Ω X →⋆ₐ[ℂ] Alg Ω X

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.diagonalInclusion_incl
declarations.doc:
**The classical net is a subnet of the quantum net**: the diagonal inclusion commutes with the
inclusions of regions.
declarations.statement:
lemma diagonalInclusion_incl {X Y : Finset S} (h : X ≤ Y) (f : CAlg Ω X) :
    inclMat h (diagonalInclusion Ω X f) = diagonalInclusion Ω Y (classicalIncl Ω h f)

modules.title: Interactions, finite-volume Hamiltonians and ensembles of a lattice system
modules.doc:
An interaction assigns an operator to each finite region of a lattice, and the finite-volume
Hamiltonian is the sum of the lifts to a box of the terms it contains.

## i. Overview

An *interaction* `Φ` assigns to each finite region `X` of the sites a Hermitian operator `Φ X` of
the algebra of `X`. The Ising chain has `Φ {x} = h σᶻ_x` and `Φ {x, y} = - J σᶻ_x σᶻ_y` for
neighbours. The *Hamiltonian of a finite box* `Λ` is
`H_Λ = ∑_{X ⊆ Λ} (Φ X ⊗ 1)`: every term supported inside the box, lifted to the box by `M ↦ M ⊗ 1`
and summed. A *charge* is a function `q_x` on the configuration space of each site, such as the
occupation number, and the total charge `N_Λ = ∑_{x ∈ Λ} q_x` of a box is the diagonal operator
with value `∑ q_x(c_x)` on the configuration `c`.

The lifts commute with the exponential: for a unital `*`-homomorphism `φ`, `φ (e^a) = e^{φ a}`, so
the Gibbs weight of a lifted operator is the lift of its Gibbs weight. The canonical and grand
canonical states of a box are the Gibbs states of `H_Λ` and `H_Λ - μ N_Λ` at inverse temperature
`β`, as in `Gibbs`. If the interaction conserves the charge, they factorize.

## ii. Key results

- `Interaction` : a family of Hermitian operators indexed by finite regions.
- `Interaction.hamiltonian` : the Hamiltonian of a finite box.
- `inclMat_exp` : the lift of an exponential is the exponential of the lift.
- `chargeOp` : the total charge of a box.
- `Interaction.canonicalState`, `Interaction.grandCanonicalState` : the ensembles of a box.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Interactions and the Hamiltonian of a box
- B. Lifts and the exponential
- C. Charges and the ensembles of a box

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 2,
  Section 6.2.

sections.text: ## A. Interactions and the Hamiltonian of a box
## C. Charges and the ensembles of a box

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction
declarations.doc: **An interaction**: a Hermitian operator of each finite region.
declarations.statement:
structure Interaction where
  /-- The term of the interaction supported in a region. -/
  Φ : ∀ X : Finset S, Alg Ω X
  /-- Every term is Hermitian. -/
  isHermitian : ∀ X, (Φ X).IsHermitian

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.hamiltonian
declarations.doc:
**The Hamiltonian of a finite box**: the sum of the lifts to the box of the terms of the
interaction supported inside it.
declarations.statement: def Interaction.hamiltonian (I : Interaction Ω) (Λ : Finset S) : Alg Ω Λ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.hamiltonian_isHermitian
declarations.statement:
lemma Interaction.hamiltonian_isHermitian (I : Interaction Ω) (Λ : Finset S) :
    (I.hamiltonian Λ).IsHermitian

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.inclMat_exp
declarations.doc: The lift `M ↦ M ⊗ 1` commutes with the exponential.
declarations.statement:
lemma inclMat_exp {X Y : Finset S} (h : X ≤ Y) (a : Alg Ω X) :
    inclMat h (NormedSpace.exp a) = NormedSpace.exp (inclMat h a)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.inclMat_gibbsWeight
declarations.doc: **The lift of a Gibbs weight is the Gibbs weight of the lift.**
declarations.statement:
lemma inclMat_gibbsWeight {X Y : Finset S} (h : X ≤ Y) (a : Alg Ω X) :
    inclMat h (gibbsWeight a) = gibbsWeight (inclMat h a)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Charge
declarations.doc:
A charge: a real number attached to each value of the configuration space of each site, such
as the occupation number of a mode.
declarations.statement: abbrev Charge (Ω : S → Type*)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.chargeOp
declarations.doc:
**The total charge of a box**: the diagonal operator with the value `∑_{x ∈ Λ} q_x(c_x)` on
the configuration `c`.
declarations.statement: def chargeOp (q : Charge Ω) (Λ : Finset S) : Alg Ω Λ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.chargeOp_isHermitian
declarations.statement: lemma chargeOp_isHermitian (q : Charge Ω) (Λ : Finset S) : (chargeOp q Λ).IsHermitian

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.canonicalState
declarations.doc: **The canonical ensemble of a box** at inverse temperature `β`.
declarations.statement:
def Interaction.canonicalState (I : Interaction Ω) (β : ℝ) (Λ : Finset S) :
    AlgState (Alg Ω Λ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.grandCanonicalState
declarations.doc:
**The grand canonical ensemble of a box** at inverse temperature `β` and chemical potential
`μ` for the charge `q`.
declarations.statement:
def Interaction.grandCanonicalState (I : Interaction Ω) (q : Charge Ω) (β μ : ℝ)
    (Λ : Finset S) : AlgState (Alg Ω Λ)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.Conserves
declarations.doc:
The interaction conserves the charge: the Hamiltonian of every box commutes with its
total charge.
declarations.statement: def Interaction.Conserves (I : Interaction Ω) (q : Charge Ω) : Prop

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.grandCanonicalWeight_of_conserves
declarations.doc:
**For a conserved charge the grand canonical weight of a box is its canonical weight times a
fugacity.**
declarations.statement:
lemma Interaction.grandCanonicalWeight_of_conserves (I : Interaction Ω) {q : Charge Ω}
    (hq : I.Conserves q) (β μ : ℝ) (Λ : Finset S) :
    gibbsWeight (grandCanonicalOp β μ (I.hamiltonian Λ) (chargeOp q Λ)) =
      gibbsWeight ((β : ℂ) • I.hamiltonian Λ) *
        NormedSpace.exp (((β * μ : ℝ) : ℂ) • chargeOp q Λ)

modules.title: Symmetric thermodynamic limit states
modules.doc:
Averaging the thermodynamic limit state of a lattice system over a group of site symmetries gives
a state of the infinite system that is invariant under the group.

## i. Overview

The Gibbs states of finite boxes break the symmetries of the lattice, because a box has a
boundary. Their limit points need not be invariant, and indeed are not in a phase with broken
symmetry. A limit point that is invariant is obtained by averaging over the group before taking
the limit: if the finite sets `F i` of group elements are asymptotically invariant (a Følner
condition), the limit of the averages of any state over them is invariant under the group.

For a lattice system with site symmetry group `Γ`, for instance the translations of a crystal, the
quasi-local algebra carries the action `symAction` of `Γ` by `*`-automorphisms. This gives a
translation invariant state of the infinite crystal, which is the hypothesis of the reduction of
the many-body problem to momentum sectors.

## ii. Key results

- `exists_invariant_state` : every state of the quasi-local algebra of a uniform lattice system has
  an invariant limit state.
- `Interaction.invariantLimitState` : the invariant state obtained from the canonical ensemble of
  an interaction.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Invariant states of a uniform lattice system
- B. The ensembles of an interaction

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 2,
  Section 6.2.3.

## B. The ensembles of an interaction

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.invariantLimit
declarations.doc:
**The invariant limit of a state of a uniform lattice system**: the Følner limit of its
averages over the site symmetries.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.invariantLimit_invariant
declarations.doc: **The invariant limit of a state is invariant under the site symmetries.**
declarations.statement:
lemma invariantLimit_invariant (φ : AlgState (uniformNet (S := S) Ω₀).Quasilocal)
    (F : ι → Finset Γ) (hne : ∀ i, (F i).Nonempty) (𝒰 : Ultrafilter ι)
    (hF : IsRightFolner F 𝒰) (γ : Γ) (a : (uniformNet (S := S) Ω₀).Quasilocal) :
    invariantLimit φ F hne 𝒰 (symAction (Ω₀ := Ω₀) γ a) = invariantLimit φ F hne 𝒰 a

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.exists_invariant_state
declarations.doc:
**Existence of invariant states**: if the finite sets of site symmetries are asymptotically
invariant, every state of the quasi-local algebra has an invariant limit state.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_invariant_state (φ : AlgState (uniformNet (S := S) Ω₀).Quasilocal)
    (F : ι → Finset Γ) (hne : ∀ i, (F i).Nonempty) (𝒰 : Ultrafilter ι)
    (hF : IsRightFolner F 𝒰) :
    ∃ ψ : AlgState (uniformNet (S := S) Ω₀).Quasilocal,
      ∀ (γ : Γ) a, ψ (symAction (Ω₀ := Ω₀) γ a) = ψ a

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.invariantLimitState
declarations.doc:
**The symmetric thermodynamic limit state of the canonical ensemble** of an interaction on a
uniform lattice system.
declarations.statement:
def Interaction.invariantLimitState (I : Interaction (fun _ : S => Ω₀)) (β : ℝ)
    (𝒰₀ : Ultrafilter (Finset S)) (h𝒰₀ : (𝒰₀ : Filter (Finset S)) ≤ atTop) (F : ι → Finset Γ)
    (hne : ∀ i, (F i).Nonempty) (𝒰 : Ultrafilter ι) :
    AlgState (uniformNet (S := S) Ω₀).Quasilocal

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.Interaction.invariantLimitState_invariant
declarations.doc: The symmetric limit state of an interaction is invariant under the site symmetries.
declarations.statement:
lemma Interaction.invariantLimitState_invariant (I : Interaction (fun _ : S => Ω₀)) (β : ℝ)
    (𝒰₀ : Ultrafilter (Finset S)) (h𝒰₀ : (𝒰₀ : Filter (Finset S)) ≤ atTop) (F : ι → Finset Γ)
    (hne : ∀ i, (F i).Nonempty) (𝒰 : Ultrafilter ι) (hF : IsRightFolner F 𝒰) (γ : Γ)
    (a : (uniformNet (S := S) Ω₀).Quasilocal) :
    I.invariantLimitState β 𝒰₀ h𝒰₀ F hne 𝒰 (symAction (Ω₀ := Ω₀) γ a) =
      I.invariantLimitState β 𝒰₀ h𝒰₀ F hne 𝒰 a

modules.title: Thermodynamic limit states of an interaction
modules.doc:
The Gibbs states of the finite boxes have limit points, which are states of the infinite system.

## i. Overview

Every local operator of a quantum lattice system is bounded, `a* a ≤ ‖a‖² · 1`, so the net of
box expectations of a fixed local observable is bounded. By compactness the canonical or grand
canonical Gibbs states of the boxes `Λ` converge, along any ultrafilter finer than the filter of
large boxes, to a state of the quasi-local algebra. This is the *thermodynamic limit state*. It is
a state of the infinite crystal, not a number attached to it.

## ii. Key results

- `matrix_exists_sumSq` : in a matrix algebra `a* a + p = c · 1` for a sum of squares `p`.
- `quantumNet_isLocallyBounded` : the net of operators is locally bounded.
- `Interaction.canonicalLimitState` : the thermodynamic limit state of the canonical ensemble.
- `Interaction.grandCanonicalLimitState` : that of the grand canonical ensemble.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Local boundedness of the net of operators
- B. Limit states of the ensembles

## iv. References

* O. Bratteli & D. Robinson, Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics 2,
  Section 6.2.3.

sections.text: ## A. Local boundedness of the net of operators
## B. Limit states of the ensembles

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.QuasiLocal.matrix_exists_sumSq
declarations.doc:
In a matrix algebra every `a* a` lies below a multiple of the identity by a sum of
squares.
declarations.statement:
lemma matrix_exists_sumSq {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (a : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, ∃ p ∈ sumSq (Matrix n n ℂ), star a * a + p = (c : ℂ) • (1 : Matrix n n ℂ)
